exercises.title: Side Lunge March
exercises.description: Side lunge march is an effective exercise that targets your glutes, hamstrings, and inner thighs.
exercises.common_mistakes: Allowing your knee to extend beyond your toes. Rounding your back.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a break. For the next exercise you will need to Take a large step to your right and lower your body into a side lunge
steps: 1. Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your hands on your hips.
2. Take a large step to your right and lower your body into a side lunge, keeping your left leg straight.
3. Push off your right foot and bring your right leg back to the starting position.
exercises.tips: To fully engage your glutes and hamstrings, it's important to keep your core muscles activated throughout the exercise.

exercises.title: Table Pose Feet Touching
exercises.description: Table Pose Feet Touching is an exercise where your feet are kept together instead of hip-width apart. This modification increases the engagement of your inner thighs, glutes, and core while improving posture, shoulder stability, and hip mobility.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting the hips sag too low
Locking the elbows
Dropping the head backward uncomfortably
Not squeezing the glutes
Feet placed too far apart
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a moment to relax and breathe deeply. Feet together, hands behind you — lift your hips like a table. Squeeze glutes and keep your core tight.
steps: 1. Sit on the floor, knees bent, feet flat, and feet touching each other,place your hands behind you, fingers pointing toward your body
2. Press into your palms and feet to lift your hips off the ground
3. Form a “table” shape with your body — knees, hips, and shoulders aligned
4. Reach your left hand toward your right leg
5. Back to table shape position and alternate sides
exercises.tips:
Press through the feet and palms
Keep feet together to engage inner thighs
Lift your hips until your torso forms a straight line
Keep the neck neutral
Activate your core and glutes throughout

exercises.title: Squat Jump Tap
exercises.description: The Squat Jump Tap is a dynamic move that combines a squat with a small jump and a tap. It helps improve lower-body strength, coordination, and cardiovascular endurance.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Not squatting low enough before jumping
Landing too hard, putting stress on knees
Losing control and balance during the jump
Letting knees cave inward
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a break. Bend down, jump up, tap the floor, and land softly
steps: 1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Jump into a squat and tap the floor with one arm.
3. Jump up back to starting position
4. Repeat and alternate sides
exercises.tips:
Keep your chest up and back straight
Land softly with bent knees
Focus on controlled, steady jumps
Engage your core to help with balance

exercises.title: Pull-Over Maschine (Lat Pull Over)
exercises.description: The Pull-Over Machine isolates the latissimus dorsi while also engaging the triceps, chest, and shoulders. It improves upper-body pulling strength, enhances back width, and supports posture and shoulder stability. This exercise is excellent for both strength development and muscle definition.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Using too much weight and swinging the arms
Arching the lower back excessively
Not controlling the return phase
Allowing elbows to flare outward
exercises.rest_speech_text: Relax your arms, engage your core, and get ready to pull smoothly with control and focus on your lats.
steps: 1. Sit at the Pull-Over Machine with your chest against the pad.
2. Grip the handles with elbows slightly bent.
3. Pull the handles down and forward in a smooth arc until your arms are fully extended in front of you.
4. Squeeze your lats at the bottom, then slowly return to the starting position.
5. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight and back flat against the pad
Lead the movement with your elbows, not your hands
Exhale while pulling the handles down, inhale while returning
Move slowly and under control throughout the full range of motion

exercises.title: Barbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.description: The Barbell Romanian Deadlift is a strength exercise that focuses on the posterior chain—mainly the hamstrings, glutes, and lower back. It’s excellent for improving hip hinge mechanics, developing lower-body strength, and enhancing balance and flexibility.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the lower back during the descent
Bending the knees too much
Lowering the bar too far
Hyperextending the back at the top
Not keeping the bar close to the body
exercises.rest_speech_text: Engage your core, hinge from the hips, and get ready to stretch and lift with control.
steps: 1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip.
2. Engage your core and keep your chest lifted.
3. With a slight bend in your knees, hinge at your hips to lower the bar slowly toward mid-shin level.
4. Keep your back flat and shoulders pulled back as the bar travels close to your legs.
5. Pause when you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings.
6. Drive your hips forward to return to the standing position, squeezing your glutes at the top.
exercises.tips:
Maintain a neutral spine throughout the movement
Keep the bar close to your thighs and shins as you lower
Push your hips back, not your knees forward
Only lower until you feel a strong stretch in the hamstrings
Control the tempo and avoid bouncing

exercises.title: Neck Circling
exercises.description: Neck Circling is a mobility exercise where you slowly rotate your head in a full circle. It helps improve neck flexibility, release tension, and increase blood flow to the upper spine.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Moving too fast or jerking the head
Overstretching the neck backward
Lifting the shoulders during rotation
exercises.rest_speech_text: Sit or stand with a straight back. Relax your shoulders, gently circle your head in one smooth motion, and breathe deeply.
steps: 1.Sit up straight with relaxed shoulders.
2. Slowly tilt your head to one side
3. Begin rotating your head in a full circle, moving through front, opposite side, and back
4. Return to the start and repeat in the opposite direction
exercises.tips:
Move slowly and gently
Keep shoulders relaxed
Breathe steadily

exercises.title: Lying Triceps Extension
exercises.description: LLying Triceps Extension targets the triceps muscles on the back of your upper arms. It helps build arm strength and improve muscle tone.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Moving elbows away from head
Using impulse instead of controlled motion
Lowering weight too fast or too far
Arching back excessively
exercises.rest_speech_text: Rest time. Lie down, keep elbows steady, bend and extend arms slowly to work your triceps
steps: 1.Lie on your back with a dumbbell in each hand
2. Hold weights above your chest with arms extended, elbows pointing up.
3. Slowly bend elbows to lower the weight toward your forehead.
4. Extend elbows back to the starting position without locking them out.
exercises.tips:
Keep elbows close to your head throughout
Move slowly and control the weight
Use a manageable weight to maintain form
Keep your core engaged to stabilize

exercises.title: Balance Lunge with Power
exercises.description: This exercise a forward lunge with stepping onto the ball. It improves lower body strength, balance, coordination, and power. Core muscles engaged like quads, glutes, and hamstrings.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Losing balance on the ball
Letting the front knee go past the toes
Not keeping the torso upright and core engaged
Stepping too far or too short onto the ball
exercises.rest_speech_text: Rest time. Step forward carefully onto the ball, keep your balance strong, then push back to start. Repeat smoothly.
steps: 1. Stand tall, feet hip-width apart, with a ball in front of you.
2. Step your right foot forward carefully onto the center of the ball and extend your arms to the sides for balance
3. Lower into a lunge by bending both knees.
4. Push through the front foot to return to standing.
5. Repeat with left leg
exercises.tips:
Start slowly and focus on controlled movement
Keep your core tight to maintain stability
Look forward, not down at your feet
Perform near a wall or sturdy surface for support

exercises.title: Dancing Cactus
exercises.description: An upper body exercise performed while sitting. You bend your elbows and move your arms out to the sides, then bring them back. This helps improve shoulder mobility, strengthens the upper back and shoulder muscles.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Moving arms too fast without control
Shrugging shoulders up towards the ears
Not keeping the back straight
Locking the elbows instead of keeping them bent
exercises.rest_speech_text: Break Time. Bend your elbows, slowly lift arms out to the sides, then bring them back in
steps: 1. Sit straight on a chair with feet flat on the floor
2. Bend your elbows, hands near your chest
3. Slowly raise your bent elbows out to the sides until arms are parallel to the floor
4. Pause briefly, then slowly bring elbows back toward the center.
exercises.tips:
Move slowly and smoothly
Keep your shoulders relaxed and down
Sit up straight with your core engaged
Breathe steadily throughout the movement

exercises.title: Reclined Cobler Pose
exercises.description: This is an exercise where you lie on your back, bend your knees, and bring the soles of your feet together, letting your knees fall out to the sides. Your arms rest extended beside your body. It's calming, opens the hips, and stretches the inner thighs.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Forcing the knees too close to the floor.
Arching the back excessively.
Tensing the shoulders or neck.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Relax. Lie down, bend your knees, bring your feet together and let your knees fall to the sides. Breathe deeply.
steps: 1. Lie flat on your back on a mat.
2. Bend your knees and bring the soles of your feet together.
3. Let your knees gently fall outward toward the floor.
4. Hold position for few seconds and return to starting position
exercises.tips:
Use pillows or blocks under your knees for support.
Keep breathing slowly to maximize the calming effect.

exercises.title: Dog Pose
exercises.description: Dog Pose is a stretch exercise that strengthens the arms and legs while stretching the back, hamstrings, calves, and shoulders.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the back
Putting too much weight on the wrists
Looking forward instead of relaxing the neck
Forcing legs to be straight
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Dog Pose. Hips up, heels down, breathe steady.
steps: 1. Start on your hands and knees
2. Spread your fingers wide and press your hands into the floor..
3. Tuck your toes under and lift your hips up toward the ceiling.
4. Try to straighten your legs and bring your heels toward the floor.
5. Keep your head between your arms, looking back at your legs.
6. Hold the pose while breathing slowly.
exercises.tips:
Bend your knees slightly if your hamstrings feel tight.
Keep your spine long and hips high.
Don’t worry if your heels don’t touch the ground.

exercises.title: Barbell Reverse Lunge
exercises.description: The Barbell Reverse Lunge strengthens the glutes, quads, and hamstrings while engaging the core for stability. Unlike forward lunges, the reverse step places less stress on the knees and provides a more controlled movement. This exercise is excellent for building unilateral power and stability.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Leaning too far forward and stressing the lower back
Letting the front knee collapse inward
Stepping back too short or too far
Bouncing the back knee off the floor
Arching the back or letting the chest fall forward under the barbell
exercises.rest_speech_text: Up next is Barbell Reverse Lunge. Grab the barbell, keep your balance steady, and get ready to step back with control.
steps: 1. Place a barbell across your upper back, gripping it firmly with both hands.
2. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, core engaged, and chest lifted.
3. Step one leg backward into a lunge position.
4. Lower until both knees are bent at about 90°, keeping the front knee stacked above the ankle.
5. Push through the heel of the front foot to rise back to the starting position.
6. Repeat on the opposite leg, alternating steps.
exercises.tips:
Keep your chest tall and shoulders pulled back 
Engage your core to stabilize the barbell
Step back far enough so the front shin stays vertical
Lower under control—avoid dropping into the lunge
Push through the heel of the front foot to return to standing

exercises.title: Half Squat Spread
exercises.description: The Half Squat Spread combines a partial squat with controlled arm movements. This exercise strengthens the lower body, improves posture, and activates the shoulders and upper back.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Standing too tall — not staying low enough in the squat
Letting knees go past toes
Dropping arms too fast
Arching the back or leaning forward
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a Break. Lower halfway down, spread your arms out to the sides, and bring them back in
steps: 1.Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, arms in front of your chest
2. Lower into a half squat — thighs about halfway to parallel
3. Jump up, spreading your legs wide apart and extend both arms out to the sides until shoulder height
4.  Return to the starting position, bring your legs back together and arms back in front of your chest.
exercises.tips:
Keep your back straight and core tight
Hold the squat at about knee-level height
Move your arms smoothly, not too fast
Keep knees in line with your toes

exercises.title: Indian Push Ups
exercises.description: Indian Push-Ups are a dynamic bodyweight exercise combining strength, flexibility, and mobility. The movement flows from a downward dog position into an upward dog position, engaging multiple muscle groups through a deep range of motion.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting hips drop too low or rise too high
Rushing the movement, reducing control
Bending elbows out to the sides excessively
Not fully transitioning into each phase of the movement
exercises.rest_speech_text: Great job! Next, flow through the motion slowly — from downward dog to upward dog — and breathe steadily
steps: 1.Start in a downward dog position — hips up, arms and legs straight.
2.Bend your elbows and lower your chest while gliding forward.
3. Sweep your torso forward, lifting your chest into an upward dog position.
4. Reverse the motion to return to downward dog
exercises.tips:
Move slowly and smoothly through the entire range
Keep your core tight to protect your lower back
Breathe in as you lower, breathe out as you push back
Focus on proper shoulder and spine alignment

exercises.title: Low Jacks
exercises.description: Low Jacks are a variation of jumping jacks where you stay in a low squat position. Instead of standing upright, you keep your knees bent and hop your feet in and out. This keeps your leg muscles engaged the whole time and adds a cardio element too
exercises.common_mistakes:
Standing up too high (reduces muscle activation)
Letting knees cave inward
Leaning too far forward
Landing hard on your feet
Moving too fast without control
exercises.rest_speech_text: Get ready for low jacks. Stay in a low squat and jump your feet in and out. Keep your legs strong and your body low
steps: 1. Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and bend your knees.
2. Jump your feet apart like a jumping jack
3. Jump your feet back together
4. Stay low the entire time — don’t stand up between jump
exercises.tips:
Keep your chest lifted and back straight
Land softly
Stay low the entire time for best results
Engage your core and glutes
Don’t let your knees go past your toes

exercises.title: Russian Twists
exercises.description: Russian Twists are a powerful core-strengthening exercise that targets the obliques and abdominal muscles. Performed in a seated position with the upper body slightly reclined and feet either on the floor or lifted, you twist the torso side to side. This movement improves rotational strength, core control, and can help define the waistline.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Moving the arms without twisting the torso
Rounding the back or collapsing the chest
Using momentum instead of muscle engagement
Holding the breath
exercises.rest_speech_text: Let’s work those abs—get ready to twist side to side.
steps: 1. Sit on the floor with your knees bent and your feet flat. Lean back slightly while keeping your back straight and your chest open.
2. Interlace your fingers or hold a weight with both hands. Extend your arms in front of you.
3. Lift your feet slightly off the ground while balancing on your glutes. Slowly twist your torso to the right, bringing your hands or the weight towards the right hip. Keep your core engaged.
4. Return to the center, balancing on your glutes with your feet off the ground. This is one repetition.
5. Repeat the twisting motion, this time to the left side. Continue alternating sides for your desired number of repetitions.
exercises.tips:
Keep your spine straight and chest lifted
Twist from the core—not just the shoulders
Breathe out as you twist to each side
Keep the movement controlled and slow

exercises.title: Dumbbell Overhead Tricep Extension
exercises.description: The Dumbbell Overhead Tricep Extension isolates and strengthens the triceps while improving shoulder flexibility and upper-arm definition. It also builds core stability and anti-extension strength, helping maintain posture and preventing back arching during overhead movements.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching the lower back
Flaring elbows outward
Dropping the dumbbell too quickly
Using the shoulders instead of the triceps
exercises.rest_speech_text: Engage your core and get ready to extend strong overhead.
steps: 1. Sit or stand tall holding one or two dumbbells overhead with arms extended.
2. Keep your elbows close to your ears and your core tight.
3. Lower the dumbbell(s) behind your head by bending your elbows.
4. Pause briefly, then press back up to the starting position.
exercises.tips:
Keep your elbows close to your head
Engage your core throughout the movement
Lower the weight slowly and with control
Exhale as you extend, inhale as you lower

exercises.title: Elbow Knee Crunch
exercises.description: Elbow Knee Crunch is a standing core activation move where you bring your elbow and opposite knee together in a controlled crunch motion. It improves balance, coordination, and core strength.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Moving too fast without control
Not lifting the knee high enough
Bending the back instead of engaging the core
Not rotating the torso enough to connect elbow to knee
exercises.rest_speech_text: Stand tall, hands near your head. Lift your knee and twist your body to meet the opposite elbow. Nice and controlled!
steps: 1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, hands behind your head
2. Lift your right knee while twisting your torso to bring the left elbow toward it
3.Return to standing position and repeat with other side
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight throughout the movement
Breathe out as you crunch, breathe in as you return
Focus on quality over speed
Maintain upright posture between reps

exercises.title: Stretching Arms Upward
exercises.description: This exercise gently opens the shoulders and upper back. Starting from a relaxed position with elbows bent and arms by your sides, you raise your arms upward, extending them over your head. It promotes better posture and upper body flexibility.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Raising shoulders toward ears
Arching the lower back excessively
Moving too fast
exercises.rest_speech_text: Arms Up Stretch. Start with bent elbows by your sides. Lift your arms slowly overhead. Keep your spine tall and shoulders relaxed.
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
2. Bend your elbows and bring arms to your sides
3. Slowly raise your arms overhead, straightening the elbows gently
4. Pause at the top for a deep breath.
5. Lower arms back down with control to the starting position.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core engaged as you lift the arms
Move slowly and with control
Focus on extending through your upper back and shoulders

exercises.title: Crunch Extended Arms
exercises.description: This exercise targets the upper abdominal muscles by performing a crunch while keeping your arms extended overhead. It helps strengthen the core and improve posture.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Using arms to pull the head up.
Jerking the body up too fast.
Straining the neck or shoulders.
Not engaging the core properly.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Crunch with Extended Arms. Lift your upper body slowly while keeping your arms straight back.
steps: 1.Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
2. Extend your arms straight above your head, keeping them in line with your shoulders.
3.Extend your arms straight back behind your head.
4. Tighten your core and slowly lift your upper body off the floor toward your knees.
5. Keep your arms extended and avoid pulling on your neck.
6. Hold briefly at the top, then slowly lower your upper body back down.
exercises.tips:
Keep your neck relaxed, don’t pull with your hands.
Use your abdominal muscles to lift, not your arms.
Breathe out as you crunch up and breathe in as you lower down.
Move slowly

exercises.title: Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.description: The Hip Flexor Stretch targets the muscles at the front of your hips. Stretching these muscles improves hip mobility, reduces lower back pain, and enhances overall posture and movement efficiency.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Allowing the back to arch excessively
Not keeping the hips square forward
Leaning too far forward or backward
Not engaging core muscles to stabilize
Holding breath during stretch
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a break. Step one foot forward, lower your back knee down, and gently push your hips forward to feel the stretch in your hip flexor.
steps: 1. Start in a kneeling lunge position with one foot forward and the other knee on the ground.
2. Keep your front knee directly above your ankle.
3. Slowly push your hips forward while keeping your torso upright.
4. Hold for 20-30 seconds, breathing deeply.
5. Switch sides and repeat.
exercises.tips:
Keep your pelvis tucked slightly under
Engage your core to protect your lower back
Maintain an upright torso
Hold the stretch gently without bouncing
Breathe deeply and relax into the stretch

exercises.title: Supine Marching
exercises.description: Supine Marching is a core stability exercise performed while lying down. This exercise strengthens the lower abdominals, promotes core stability, and improves control over pelvic movement.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Lifting legs too high or too fast
Letting the pelvis tilt or lower back arch off the floor
Tension in neck or shoulders
Holding your breath
exercises.rest_speech_text: For the next Lie on your back, bend your knees, and place your feet on the floor. Lift one leg, then the other, like you're marching in place
steps: 1. Lie on your back, arms by your sides, legs extended, feet flat on the floor
2. Lift your right leg up toward hip level
3. Slowly lower your right leg and repeat with left leg
exercises.tips:
Keep your core engaged throughout
Move slowly and with control
Maintain normal breathing 
Keep a slight touch between your lower back and the floor

exercises.title: Dips Machine ( +assisted dips)
exercises.description: The Dips Machine strengthens the triceps, chest, and shoulders while providing a stable, controlled environment. Assisted dips help beginners build strength safely, whereas unassisted dips challenge upper-body power and endurance. This exercise improves pushing strength, arm tone, and shoulder stability.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting the shoulders roll forward or shrug
Going too low, overstressing the shoulders
Using momentum instead of controlled movement
Flaring elbows outward
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a breath, reset your grip, and get ready to push strong through your arms and chest with control.
steps: 1. Adjust the assist weight if using assistance.
2. Grip the handles firmly, knees or feet on the platform.
3. Start with arms straight and shoulders down.
4. Lower your body by bending elbows to ~90 degrees.
5. Press back up to the starting position.
6. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
exercises.tips:
Keep your chest slightly forward and core tight
Lower yourself slowly until your upper arms are parallel to the floor
Push through your palms to return to the starting position
Adjust assistance as needed to maintain proper form

exercises.title: Butterfly Sit Ups
exercises.description: Butterfly Sit-Ups are performed lying on your back with knees bent and opened outward, soles of the feet touching. As you lift your torso, the abdominal muscles—especially the rectus abdominis—are engaged.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Pulling on your neck with your hands
Letting your feet or knees shift too much
Using impulse instead of your core
Dropping back too fast
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a break. Lie on your back, knees bent and wide, feet together. Sit up toward your legs and lower down slowly.
steps: 1. Lie on your back with your knees bent and the soles of your feet touching each other.
2. Your hands directed above head.
3. Engage your core and lift your upper body toward your legs.
4. Come up until your chest reaches the level of your knees or slightly beyond.
5. Slowly lower yourself back down with control.
exercises.tips:
Keep your feet pressed together
Focus on lifting with your abs, not your arms or neck
Control your movement up and down
Breathe out on the way up, in on the way down

exercises.title: Triceps Raises with Dumbbell
exercises.description: This exercise targets the triceps by isolating elbow extension while the body is in a forward-leaning position. It also improves posture, strengthens the back stabilizers, and develops arm tone.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the upper back
Not fully extending the arms
Swinging instead of controlling
exercises.rest_speech_text: Step forward with one foot and lean your body forward while keeping your back straight. Press your elbows against your body and start bending and extending your elbows, moving your arms back and forth.
steps: 1. Stand up straight and hold the weights in your hands.
2. Step forward with one foot and lean your body forward while keeping your back straight.
3. Press your elbows against your body and start bending and extending your elbows, moving your arms back and forth.
exercises.tips:
Keep your shoulders down and back
Focus on only moving the forearms
Engage your core

exercises.title: Barbell Pendlay Row
exercises.description: The Barbell Pendlay Row is a powerful back exercise that builds strength and explosiveness in the lats, rhomboids, and traps. Starting each rep from the floor emphasizes strict form and full range of motion. It also improves core stability, lumbopelvic control, and anti-extension strength, reinforcing posture and trunk rigidity during pulling movements.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the back or jerking the barbell
Pulling with the arms instead of the back
Lifting the bar too high or using momentum
Letting hips rise during the pull
exercises.rest_speech_text: Brace hard, back flat—row with power and control
steps: 1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, barbell on the floor in front of you.
2. Hinge at the hips until your torso is parallel to the ground.
3. Grip the bar just wider than shoulder-width, core tight, back flat.
4. Pull the bar explosively toward your lower ribs.
5. Lower it back to the floor and reset before the next rep.
exercises.tips:
Keep your back flat and chest over the bar
Engage your core and pull explosively toward your lower ribs
Reset on the floor after each rep for proper form
Lower the bar under control—don’t drop it

exercises.title: Standing Crawl Stroke
exercises.description: Standing Crawl Stroke engages your core and upper back. While keeping a slight forward bend from your hips you perform alternating forward arm circles. It targets posture muscles, enhances shoulder mobility, and activates your glutes and hamstrings for balance.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the lower back
Locking knees
Swinging arms too fast
Letting the head drop
exercises.rest_speech_text: Break time. Lean slightly forward from your hips. Swing your arms one by one like swimming strokes.
steps: 1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart
2. Slightly bend your knees and lean forward from your hips
3. Begin rotating one arm forward in a large circle
4. Alternate with the other arm, like freestyle swimming
exercises.tips:
Bend from the hips, not the back
Engage your core to stabilize
Move arms slowly with full control
Keep knees slightly bent and feet hip-width apart

exercises.title: Bicycle Crunches
exercises.description: Bicycle crunches is an exercise where you keep your upper body still and focus only on moving your legs in a pedaling motion. This primarily targets the lower abdominal muscles and hip flexors.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Lifting shoulders too much or moving upper body
Moving legs too fast
Arching the lower back off the floor
exercises.rest_speech_text: Time to break. Keep back down, pedal legs slowly, stay steady
steps: 1. Lie on your back, arms resting at your sides.
2.Keep your upper body still and back pressed into the floor.
3. Lift both legs slightly off the floor.
4.Move legs in a slow pedaling motion: one leg bent bringing knee closer, the other leg extended straight.
5. Alternate legs continuously, maintaining contro
exercises.tips:
Keep your back flat on the floor
Move legs slowly and with control
Engage your core throughout

exercises.title: Horse Kick
exercises.description: This version of the Horse Kick lets you hold on to a chair for balance while kicking one leg back. It works your glutes, hamstrings, and core, with less pressure on your wrists or knees.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching the lower back.
Kicking too high or too fast.
Letting the standing leg lock or wobble.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Horse Kick with chair. Stand tall, hold the chair, and kick one leg back slowly. Squeeze your glutes.
steps: 1. Stand behind a chair, place both hands on the top of the chair and keep your feet hip-width apart
2. Shift weight to one leg and kick the other leg back and slightly up.
3. Squeeze your glutes at the top.
4. Bring your leg back down slowly.
exercises.tips:
Keep your back straight and chest lifted.
Move slowly.
Squeeze your glutes at the top of the kick.
Don’t lean too far forward.

exercises.title: Elbow Windmill
exercises.description: This seated mobility exercise targets the shoulders, upper back, and thoracic spine. With hands placed behind the neck, the elbows are gently lifted and rotated in wide circles.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Pulling on the neck with the hands
Moving the torso instead of just the elbows
Shrugging the shoulders during the rotation
Performing the motion too quickly
exercises.rest_speech_text: Rest time! Sit tall, hands behind your neck. Start raising your elbows in smooth circles—feel the stretch across your chest and shoulders
steps: 1. Sit upright on a chair, feet flat on the ground.
2. Place both hands behind your neck, elbows relaxed to the sides..
3. Slowly raise one elbow to the side.
4. Slowly down back and switch side
exercises.tips:
Sit tall and keep your spine neutral
Let your hands rest lightly behind your neck
Focus on slow, wide circles with your elbows
Keep your core lightly engaged 
Don’t forget to reverse the direction of the circles

exercises.title: Biceps Curl Machine
exercises.description: The Biceps Curl Machine isolates the biceps brachii, helping to build arm strength, size, and definition. It provides a controlled movement that minimizes strain on the elbows and shoulders while enhancing pulling power and functional upper-body performance.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Using momentum or swinging the arms
Leaning backward or forward during the curl
Not fully extending the elbows at the bottom
Curling too fast without control
exercises.rest_speech_text: Relax your arms, brace your core, and get ready to curl with control and focus on your biceps.
steps: 1. Sit on the biceps curl machine with your upper arms resting on the pad.
2. Grip the handles firmly.
3. Curl the weight upward, contracting your biceps fully at the top.
4. Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position.
5. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
exercises.tips:
Keep your upper arms stationary against the pad
Exhale while curling the weight up, inhale while lowering
Move slowly and focus on squeezing the biceps at the top
Avoid locking out elbows at the bottom to maintain tension

exercises.title: Band Skullcrusher
exercises.description: The Band Skullcrusher is an effective isolation exercise for the triceps, using a resistance band to provide tension throughout the movement. It strengthens and tones the triceps, improves elbow stability.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Allowing elbows to flare outward
Using momentum
Arching the back or leaning excessively.
Not fully extending the arms
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a deep breath… elbows tight… feel your triceps ready… and get set.
steps: 1. Anchor the resistance band above head height or hold it behind your head while lying on a bench or floor.
2. Hold the band with both hands, elbows bent and tucked close to your head.
3. Extend your elbows to press your hands away from your head, keeping upper arms stationary.
4. Pause at full extension, squeezing the triceps.
5. Slowly return to the starting position, maintaining control and band tension.
exercises.tips:
Keep elbows close to the head 
Focus on a slow lowering phase 
Maintain a neutral spine and tight core
Adjust band tension to match your strength level

exercises.title: Leg Change Scrambler
exercises.description: Leg Change Scrambler is a dynamic, full-body movement performed in a plank. It involves quickly switching your legs back and forth. This exercise improves coordination, strengthens the core, legs, and shoulders, and elevates your heart rate for cardio benefits.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting hips bounce too high or sag low.
Not keeping hands under shoulders.
Holding breath during fast movements.
Moving too fast and losing form.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Let's take a moment to rest. Get ready in a plank. Switch your legs fast like you're running on the floor. Keep your body straight and core tight
steps: 1.Get into a plank with arms straight, hands under shoulders
2. Jump and switch your legs – bring one knee in and extend the other back.
3. Keep switching legs back and forth quickly.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight to protect your back.
Switch legs with control, not just speed.
Breathe steadily.
Keep shoulders over your wrists.

exercises.title: Side Stretch
exercises.description: The Side Stretch helps lengthen the muscles along the side of your body — mainly the obliques, shoulders, and hips. It improves flexibility, reduces muscle tightness, and is great for warm-ups, cool-downs, or quick posture resets.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Leaning forward or backward
Lifting the foot off the ground
Holding your breath
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Side Stretch. Reach up, lean gently to the side, and feel the stretch
steps: 1. Stand or sit tall with your back straight.
2. Raise one arm overhead, keeping it close to your ear
3. Slowly lean your upper body to the opposite side.
4. Keep your hips still — don't twist or lean forward
5. Feel the stretch along your side and hold for 10–20 seconds
6. Return to center and switch sides
exercises.tips:
Stretch gently — don’t force the movement.
Keep both feet or hips grounded.
Breathe deeply and slowly.

exercises.title: Posture Stretch
exercises.description: The Posture Stretch is a simple standing exercise that helps counteract poor posture caused by prolonged sitting. By drawing your arms back and opening the chest, it encourages proper alignment of the spine and shoulders.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Locking elbows too tightly
Tilting the head or arching the lower back
Shrugging the shoulders
Holding your breath
exercises.rest_speech_text: Great work! Clasp your hands behind you, pull your shoulders back, and open your chest. Hold and breathe.
steps: 1. Stand straight, feet shoulder-width apart, arms relaxed at your sides.
2. Clasp your hands together behind your back
3. Straighten your arms and gently pull them downward and slightly away from your back
4. Roll your shoulders back and lift your chest
5. Hold the stretch for 10–20 seconds while breathing deeply
6. Slowly return to the starting position, lowering your arms by your sides, and relax.
exercises.tips:
Keep your shoulders relaxed 
Gently squeeze the shoulder blades together
Engage your core
Focus on lengthening the spine upward

exercises.title: High Knees
exercises.description: High knees are a great cardio exercise that can help improve your leg strength, endurance, and coordination.
exercises.common_mistakes: Leaning back or hunching forward. Allowing your knees to collapse inward or outward. Going too fast or too slow.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a short break, breathe deeply, and get ready to drive your knees up — High Knees start soon!
steps: 1. Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your arms at your sides.
2. Begin to jog in place, lifting your knees up towards your chest and alternating legs.
3. As you lift each knee, swing your opposite arm forward to help generate momentum.
4. Continue lifting your knees and swinging your arms for the desired duration of the exercise.
exercises.tips: Engage your core throughout the exercise to maintain proper form and maximize the benefits. Focus on lifting your knees up as high as possible to engage your hip flexors and improve flexibility.

exercises.title: Back Neck Stretch
exercises.description: This is a gentle stretch for the back of the neck that helps relieve tension and improve flexibility. It can reduce neck stiffness and promote relaxation.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Moving too quickly
Using too much force
Holding breath during the stretch
exercises.rest_speech_text: Time to rest. Sit tall, slowly tilt your head forward and hold the stretch gently
steps: 1.Sit comfortably with a straight back.
2. Slowly tilt your head forward, bringing your chin toward your chest and hold the stretch for 10 seconds
3. Slowly return to the starting position.
exercises.tips:
Move slowly and gently
Breathe deeply and relax
Stop if you feel pain

exercises.title: Vertical Fold
exercises.description: This exercise is a dynamic exercise that combines balance, flexibility, and coordination. Starting standing with arms overhead, you fold forward, lift one leg, and reach toward that leg with both arms, then switch sides. It improves hamstring flexibility, engages the core for stability.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the back too much 
Losing balance by rushing the movement
Not keeping the lifted leg straight
Reaching too far with arms and straining
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a moment to catch your breath and relax. Fold forward, lift one leg, reach with arms, then switch sides.
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, arms raised overhead.
2. Move forward at the hips and lift your right leg straight out in front.
3. Reach both arms toward your lifted right leg, keeping your back long
4. Hold briefly, then lower the leg and return to standing with arms overhead.
5. Repeat the movement on the left leg.
exercises.tips:
Keep your spine long while folding forward
Maintain a slight bend in the standing knee for stability
Move slowly and control your balance
Engage your core to support your lower back

exercises.title: Band Rapunzel Pushdown
exercises.description: The Band Rapunzel Pushdown is an isolation exercise targeting the triceps using a resistance band. It emphasizes controlled extension of the elbow, improving arm strength, toning, and stability in the upper arm. This exercise is excellent for building triceps definition and enhancing upper body pushing strength.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Flaring elbows outward
Using momentum
Leaning forward or arching the back.
Not fully extending the arms or locking elbows
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a deep breath… get your elbows in… feel your triceps engage… and get ready.
steps: 1. Anchor the resistance band above head height (door, bar, or sturdy support).
2. Stand tall facing the anchor, holding the band with both hands.
3. Step back slightly to create tension, elbows close to your sides.
4. Press the band down by extending your elbows fully, keeping upper arms stationary.
5. Pause at the bottom, squeezing the triceps.
6. Slowly return to the starting position with control.
exercises.tips:
Keep your elbows tucked at your sides
Focus on squeezing the triceps at the end of the pushdown
Maintain a slight bend in the knees and a neutral spine
Move slowly on both the downward and upward phases

exercises.title: High Plank Windmill
exercises.description: High Plank Windmill strengthens the core muscles, shoulders, arms, and improves overall balance and spinal mobility. Starting in a high plank position, you rotate your torso and extend one arm upward. This exercise challenges your stability while engaging multiple muscle groups.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Dropping hips or raising them too high
Rotating hips instead of the upper body
Letting shoulders collapse or sag
Holding breath during the movement
Moving too fast
exercises.rest_speech_text: Break. Hold a high plank, rotate your body and arm together to the same side, keeping your core tight and controlled
steps: 1. Start in a high plank position with hands shoulder-width apart, body in a straight line.
2. Slowly rotate your torso to one side and extend the opposite arm upward toward the ceiling.
3. Rotate your torso and lift the arm on the same side as the rotation, reaching it toward the ceiling.
4. Hold briefly, then return to plank position.
5. Repeat on the other side.
exercises.tips:
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels
Engage your core throughout the movement
Rotate the torso with control, not the hips
Breathe steadily and smoothly
Move slowly to maintain balance and form

exercises.title: Walking Plank
exercises.description: The Walking Plank is an exercise that involves moving from a forearm plank position to a full-arm plank (push-up position) and then back down, "walking" the hands forward and backward. It targets the core, shoulders, arms, and improves overall stability and upper body strength.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting hips sag or rise too high
Rotating the torso excessively
Moving too fast
Not engaging the core
exercises.rest_speech_text: Break.Walking Plank. From forearms, press up to hands, then lower back down, keep your body straight.
steps: 1. Start in a forearm plank position with elbows under shoulders and body straight.
2. Place your right hand on the floor, then your left hand, coming up into a full plank
3. Lower your right forearm to the floor, then your left forearm, returning to the forearm plank.
exercises.tips:
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels
Engage your core
Move slowly and with control
Keep shoulders aligned over wrists when “walking” hands

exercises.title: Lying Leg Curl
exercises.description: The Lying and Seated Leg Curl exercises isolate the hamstrings, improving knee flexion strength, balance between quads and hamstrings, and overall lower-body stability. The lying version emphasizes the hamstrings in a stretched position, while the seated version targets them in a shortened position, ensuring full-range development.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Lifting hips off the bench or seat
Using momentum instead of controlled motion
Incomplete range of motion
Allowing knees or ankles to shift during the movement
exercises.rest_speech_text: Relax your legs, brace your core, and get ready to curl smoothly with control.
steps: 1. Lie face down on the leg curl machine, with ankles under the pad.
2. Keep hips and thighs pressed firmly against the bench.
3. Curl your legs up toward your glutes, squeezing the hamstrings.
4. Lower slowly back to the starting position.
5. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
exercises.tips:
Adjust the machine to fit your leg length for comfort and proper alignment
Keep hips and thighs pressed firmly against the pad
Move slowly, focusing on squeezing the hamstrings
Exhale while curling, inhale while returning

exercises.title: Head Turns
exercises.description: This exercise involves sitting on a bench, placing one arm on your shoulder, and slowly turning your head to each side. It helps improve neck mobility and relieve tension, promoting better posture.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Turning the head too fast or abruptly
Using the shoulders or torso to assist the movement
Not keeping the spine straight
exercises.rest_speech_text: Great job! Sit tall, place your arm on your shoulder, slowly turn your head side to side, stay relaxed.
steps: 1. Sit on a bench with feet flat on the floor
2. Place your right hand on your right shoulder.
3. Slowly turn your head to the left as far as comfortable
4. Return to the center and turn to the other side
exercises.tips:
Move slowly and gently
Keep your shoulders relaxed
Focus on smooth, controlled motions
Breathe naturally

exercises.title: Deltoid Stretch
exercises.description: The Deltoid Stretch focuses on lengthening and loosening the deltoid muscle group that covers the shoulder joint. This stretch helps improve shoulder mobility, reduce muscle tightness.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Pulling the arm too hard
Raising the shoulder toward the ear
Bending the elbow improperly
Holding breath during stretch
Slouching or rounding the back
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a break. Bring one arm across your chest, use the other arm to gently pull it closer, and hold while keeping your shoulder relaxed.
steps: 1. Stand with a straight back.
2. Extend one arm straight across your chest at shoulder height.
3. Use the opposite hand to gently pull that arm closer to your chest.
4. Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds while breathing deeply.
5. Release slowly and repeat on the other arm.
exercises.tips:
Keep the shoulder down and relaxed 
Pull the arm gently across the body without forcing
Maintain a straight posture with engaged core
Breathe deeply and relax muscles

exercises.title: Floor Dip and Reach
exercises.description: Floor Dips and Reach target your triceps, shoulders, and chest. This bodyweight exercise helps build upper body strength and improves arm definition.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Dropping hips too low
Using impulse instead of controlled movement
Elbows flaring out wide
exercises.rest_speech_text: Break time. Lower yourself slow, elbows tight, push back up strong
steps: 1.Sit on the floor with hands placed behind you, fingers pointing forward.
2. Bend your knees and keep feet flat on the floor
3. Lift your hips off the floor by straightening your arms.
4. Lower your body by bending your elbows until your hips nearly touch the floor.
5. Push back up to the start position
exercises.tips:
Keep your elbows close to your body
Lower yourself slowly and push up steadily
Keep your core engaged

exercises.title: Spine Extension
exercises.description: Spine Extension is an exercise where you lift bent arms overhead, stretch your upper back, then bend elbows and bring arms back down. It helps improve posture, shoulder mobility, and spinal flexibility.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Overarching the lower back during extension
Rushing through the movement
Shrugging shoulders upward
exercises.rest_speech_text: Break Time. Lift your bent arms overhead, stretch gently back, then bring your arms back in and down
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart. Bend your elbows so your hands are near your ribs, palms facing forward.
2. Breathe in as you raise your elbows upward and straighten your arms fully overhead.
3. Gently stretch backward through your upper spine.
4. Breathe our while bending your elbows and lowering them back toward your sides.
exercises.tips:
Engage your core gently
Move slowly and smoothly
Breathe in while lifting and extending; exhale while returning
Keep your feet grounded and shoulders relaxed

exercises.title: Bodyweight Lunges
exercises.description: The Bodyweight Lunge is classic forward lunge is a bodyweight exercise where you step forward and bend the front knee. It strengthens the lower body and enhances stability, coordination, and balance.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting the front knee move past the toes
Leaning the upper body forward
Lifting the back heel too early
Inward collapse of the front knee
exercises.rest_speech_text: Time for a break. Step forward, bend both knees, keep your back straight. Let’s lunge
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, arms at your sides.
2. Step forward with your right foot.
3. Bend your front knee, keeping the back leg extended and heel lifted
4. Lower your hips until both knees are bent.
5. Push through the front heel to return to standing and repeat with other leg
exercises.tips:
Keep your front knee aligned with your ankle
Lower yourself straight down, not forward
Keep your torso upright
Engage your core throughout the movement

exercises.title: Barbell Curl
exercises.description: The Barbell Curl is a classic isolation exercise that targets the biceps, helping to build arm size, strength, and definition. It also engages the forearms and grip muscles, improving upper body pulling strength and overall arm aesthetics.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Swinging the bar using momentum 
Allowing elbows to move forward or away from the torso
Using too much weight, reducing range of motion
Not fully extending the arms at the bottom
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a breath… focus on control… and get ready to curl strong.
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an underhand grip (palms facing up).
2. Keep elbows tucked close to your torso.
3. Slowly curl the bar upward toward your shoulders, contracting your biceps.
4. Pause briefly at the top and squeeze the biceps.
5. Lower the bar back down slowly to full arm extension.
6. Repeat for the recommended number of reps.
exercises.tips:
Keep your elbows close to your body
Avoid swinging — move slowly and under control
Focus on squeezing the biceps at the top
Maintain a straight posture and engaged core
Use a full range of motion for best results

exercises.title: Hands Stretch
exercises.description: This exercise involves stretching your hands and fingers while sitting comfortably on a mat. It helps improve hand and wrist flexibility, reduce stiffness.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Raising shoulders toward ears
Locking elbows too rigidly
Forcing palms into uncomfortable positions
Holding breath during the stretch
Poor sitting posture
exercises.rest_speech_text: Sit tall, raise your hands overhead, turn your palms to face the ceiling, and breathe deeply.
steps: 1. Sit with your feet stretched out in front, shoulder width apart.
2. Slowly raise your hands above your head.
3. Turn your palms inside out, so they face the ceiling.
4. Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, breathing deeply.
5. Slowly lower your hands back down.
exercises.tips:
Sit tall with a straight back and relaxed shoulders
Keep elbows soft, not locked
Turn palms slowly and gently to face ceiling
Breathe deeply and relax into the stretch

exercises.title: Head Tilting
exercises.description: Head tilting is a neck stretch where you slowly tilt your head to one side to stretch the muscles along the side of your neck. Helps improve neck flexibility, reduce tension, and relieve stiffness.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Tilting too fast or jerking the head
Raising the shoulder on the same side as the tilt
exercises.rest_speech_text: Great job! Let's take a short break. Slowly tilt your head to the side, hold for a few seconds, and relax
steps: 1.Sit upright on a chair with feet flat on the floor, keep your back straight and shoulders relaxed.
2. Slowly lower your head forward
3. Return to center
4. Gently tilt your head back to look upward
5. Return to the center
exercises.tips:
Move slowly and smoothly
Keep shoulders relaxed and down
Breathe deeply throughout the movement

exercises.title: Down Box
exercises.description: Down Box is a bodyweight exercise where you move from a standing position into a crouched or “box” position, resembling a squat with your hands on the floor. It helps improve mobility, strengthens your lower body and core, and enhances body control and coordination.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting heels lift off the floor
Dropping the chest too low
Rounding the back
Moving too fast without control
exercises.rest_speech_text: For next exercise, Hold your hands together in front of you and sit down. Back to the starting position, strike your left hand to your right side.
steps: 1. Stand tall with your feet hip- or shoulder-width apart
2. Go to a squat, back to a standing position and kick with your left hand to the ride side
3. Alternate sides.
exercises.tips:
Keep your heels down
Move slowly and stay balanced
Keep your chest open
Engage your core when lowering

exercises.title: Lunge Squats
exercises.description: Lunge Squats combine a lunge and a squat to work your legs, glutes, and core. This exercise improves lower body strength, balance, and coordination.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting the front knee go past the toes
Leaning forward too much
Not keeping your back straight
Losing balance
exercises.rest_speech_text: Break. Step forward, lower down, keep your balance, then push back up
steps: 1. Stand tall, feet hip-width apart.
2. Step forward with one leg and lower your body until both knees are bent
3. Keep your front knee above your ankle, not over toes
4.Push back to the starting position and repeat with other leg
exercises.tips:
Keep your chest up and back straight
Step forward far enough so your knee stays above your ankle
Engage your core for stability
Move slowly and controlled

exercises.title: Semicircle Head Turning
exercises.description: This exercise gently mobilizes your neck by moving your head in a semicircular motion. It helps improve neck flexibility, reduce stiffness, and relieve tension.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Moving the head too quickly or jerkily
Overextending the neck beyond comfortable range
Holding your breath during the movement
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a break. Sit tall, slowly move your head in a semicircle, relax your neck, breathe steady.
steps: 1.Sit comfortably on a bench with your feet flat on the floor and rest your arms on knees
2. Lower your chin toward your chest, starting the movement to the left.
3. Slowly move your head in a semicircular motion, starting from one side, going forward and around to the other side.
4. Repeat in the opposite direction
exercises.tips:
Move slowly and smoothly
Keep your shoulders relaxed
Breathe evenly throughout the exercise

exercises.title: Side Jumps
exercises.description: Side Jumps are a cardio exercise that improves agility, coordination, and lower body strength. This dynamic movement helps enhance balance, burn calories, and strengthen the legs and core.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Landing heavily without control
Letting knees cave inward
Not using arms for balance
Jumping too far or too little
exercises.rest_speech_text: Get ready for the exercise.Jump side to side, land soft, keep knees aligned, use your arms.
steps: 1. Stand with feet hip-width apart and slightly bend knees and prepare to jump.
2. Jump laterally to the right, landing softly on the balls of your feet.
3.Immediately jump back to the left side
exercises.tips:
Land softly on the balls of your feet
Keep knees aligned with toes
Use your arms to help balance
Start with smaller jumps, increase range gradually

exercises.title: Cable Rope Face Pulls
exercises.description: The Cable Rope Face Pull is an effective upper-body exercise that targets the rear deltoids, traps, and upper back. It also strengthens the rotator cuff muscles, improving shoulder health, posture, and stability.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Pulling the rope down instead of toward the face
Using too much weight and relying on momentum
Flaring the elbows too high or keeping them too low
Not retracting the shoulder blades fully
Letting the lower back arch or torso sway
exercises.rest_speech_text: Set your stance, lock your core, and get ready to pull to your face with control.
steps: 1. Attach a rope handle to a high pulley on a cable machine.
2. Stand facing the machine with feet shoulder-width apart and grab the rope with an overhand grip
3. Step back slightly so there’s tension on the cable, and engage your core.
4. Start with your arms extended in front of you.
5. Exhale and pull the rope toward your face, leading with your elbows and separating your hands as you pull back.
6. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the peak of the movement.
7. Inhale and slowly return to the starting position with control.
exercises.tips:
Keep your elbows in line with your shoulders 
Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together at the end of each rep
Use a controlled motion—avoid jerking the rope
Keep your wrists neutral and avoid twisting excessively
Exhale as you pull, inhale as you return to the start

exercises.title: Back Extension Machine
exercises.description: The Back Extension Machine strengthens the lower back, glutes, and hamstrings while engaging the core for stability. It improves spinal support, posture, and posterior chain strength, reducing the risk of lower-back injuries and enhancing performance in lifting and athletic movements.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching the lower back excessively at the top
Using momentum instead of controlled motion
Not engaging the glutes and hamstrings
Raising the torso too high or twisting the spine
exercises.rest_speech_text: Relax your upper body, engage your core, and get ready to lift with control, focusing on your glutes and lower back.
steps: 1. Adjust the machine so your hips rest on the pad and feet are secured.
2. Start with your torso upright and spine neutral.
3. Slowly bend forward at the hips, lowering your upper body.
4. Contract your glutes and hamstrings to raise your torso back to the starting position.
5. Repeat for the desired number of reps with controlled motion.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight and spine neutral throughout the movement
Focus on controlled lifting and lowering
Squeeze the glutes and hamstrings at the top
Avoid excessive hyperextension

exercises.title: Forward Arm Circles
exercises.description: Stand tall with your arms extended straight out to the sides at shoulder height. Slowly rotate your arms forward in small controlled circles to warm up your shoulders and improve upper body mobility.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Moving arms too fast or too large
Shrugging or lifting shoulders toward ears
Leaning forward or arching back excessively
Locking elbows
exercises.rest_speech_text: To do this exercise Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart.Extend arms out to sides, circle them forward slowly and controlled
steps: 1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, arms stretched sideways at shoulder height.
2. Keep elbows slightly bent, shoulders relaxed.
3. Slowly circle arms forward in small, controlled motions.
exercises.tips:
Keep movements slow and smooth
Maintain slight bend in elbows
Focus on controlled
Keep shoulders relaxed

exercises.title: Dumbbell Rolling Tricep Extension
exercises.description: The Dumbbell Rolling Tricep Extension combines a skullcrusher with a close-grip press to strengthen the triceps through a full range of motion. It also engages the chest and shoulders while improving core stability, anti-extension control, and upper-body coordination for smoother pressing movements.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Flaring elbows outward
Arching the lower back
Dropping the dumbbells too quickly
Using momentum instead of controlled motion
exercises.rest_speech_text: Stay tight and controlled—get ready to extend and press.
steps: 1. Lie on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand, arms extended above your chest.
2. Bend your elbows to lower the dumbbells toward your shoulders, keeping elbows close.
3. Once the dumbbells reach near your shoulders, roll them slightly forward toward your chest.
4. Press the weights back up to the starting position in one smooth motion.
exercises.tips:
Keep elbows close to your body
Lower the dumbbells slowly and with control
Engage your core to protect your lower back
Press powerfully but smoothly back up

exercises.title: Alternating Side Lunge
exercises.description: Alternating Side Lunges strengthens the legs, hips, and glutes while improving balance and lateral movement.Step to the side into a lunge position, bending the knee and pushing hips back, then return to standing and repeat on the other side.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting the knee go past the toes
Leaning the torso too far forward
Not pushing hips back enough
Losing balance when stepping out
exercises.rest_speech_text: Time to Break. Stand tall, step to the side, bend the knee, push hips back, stand tall, then switch sides.
steps: 1.Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
2.Step with one foot out to the side, bend your knee, pushing your hips back. Keep other leg straight.
3. Push off your right foot to return to standing.
4. Repeat with opposite side.
exercises.tips:
Keep your chest up and back straight
Push hips back as you bend the knee
Step wide enough to feel the stretch
Move controlled and steady

exercises.title: Sit Bow
exercises.description: This exercise stretches the back and hips and gently activates your core. Sit on the edge of a chair. Bend one leg while the other foot stays flat on the floor. Place your hands on your legs. Slowly lean forward by bending your upper body, keeping your back straight.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the back
Leaning too fast
Hands not resting on legs
exercises.rest_speech_text: Time to rest. Sit, bend one leg, place the other on the floor, hands on your legs. Slowly lean forward.
steps: 1. Sit on the edge of a chair
2. Bend one leg, keep the other foot flat on the floor
3. Slowly lean forward, bending only your upper body
4. Hold the stretch for a few seconds, then return
exercises.tips:
Keep your back straight while bending
Move slowly and with control
Breathe steadily

exercises.title: Hamstring Sit Back
exercises.description: The Hamstring Sit Back provides a deeper stretch for the hamstrings, hip abductors, and inner thigh muscles, while also improving hip joint mobility and lower back flexibility.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the back or collapsing chest forward
Twisting hips unevenly or shifting weight improperly
Forcing the stretch beyond comfort
Not keeping the extended leg straight
Holding breath or tensing unnecessarily
exercises.rest_speech_text: Sit back slowly, extend one leg to the side, bend the other leg underneath you, keep your back straight and breathe deeply
exercises.slow_down_phrases: Slow down to control every movement.
steps: 1. Start from a seated position on the floor, with one leg bent under you and the other leg extended forward.
2. Your arms are stretched out in front of you to maintain balance.
3. Slowly lean forward onto the bent leg and begin to transfer your weight forward.
4. Try to feel the stretch in your hamstrings and lower back.
5. Allow the relaxed muscles time to stretch, holding this position for a few seconds.
exercises.tips:
Keep your spine long and chest lifted 
Engage core muscles to support your back
Point toes of the extended leg upwards
Breathe deeply and relax muscles during the hold

exercises.title: Dumbbell Incline Bench Press
exercises.description: The Dumbbell Incline Bench Press targets the upper chest, shoulders, and triceps while improving pressing strength and muscle symmetry. The incline angle emphasizes the upper pectorals and enhances shoulder stability. It also develops core stability, lumbopelvic control, and anti-extension strength, supporting posture and preventing back arching during lifts.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching the lower back excessively
Lowering the dumbbells too quickly
Flaring the elbows too wide
Using uneven or unsteady movement
exercises.rest_speech_text: Brace your core and get ready to press strong on the incline.
steps: 1. Sit on an incline bench holding dumbbells at chest level, palms forward.
2. Engage your core and press the dumbbells upward until your arms are extended.
3. Pause briefly at the top, keeping control.
4. Slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
exercises.tips:
Keep your feet flat and core tight
Control the dumbbells through the full range
Lower slowly and press powerfully
Maintain steady breathing—exhale as you press up

exercises.title: Walking Lunges
exercises.description: Walking lunges are a dynamic lower-body exercise that works your legs, glutes, and core. You take steps forward, lowering your body into a lunge each time, which helps build strength, balance, and coordination.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting the front knee go past toes
Leaning the upper body forward
Taking steps that are too short
Losing balance due to lack of core engagement
exercises.rest_speech_text: Rest time. Now stand tall,step forward and bend both knees into a lunge. Keep your balance and keep going
steps: 1. Stand tall, feet hip-width apart.
2. Step forward with your right leg.
3.Bend both knees and lower your body to lunge
4. Push off the back foot and step forward with your left leg into the next lunge
5. Keep alternating legs, walking forward with control.
exercises.tips:
Keep your torso upright, don’t lean forward.
Knee shouldn’t go past your toes.
Step far enough to allow both knees to bend comfortably.
Engage your core for balance.

exercises.title: Flutter Kicks
exercises.description: Flutter Kicks are a core exercise where you lie on your back with your arms by your sides and alternate kicking your legs up and down in a small, fast motion. This exercise strengthens the lower abs, hip flexors, and improves endurance and core stability.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching your lower back off the floor
Kicking legs too high or too slow
Holding your breath
Tensing your neck or shoulders
exercises.rest_speech_text: Break Time. Lie back, keep arms down, kick legs quickly and small, keep core tight.
steps: 1. Lie flat on your back, arms resting by your sides
2. Lift both legs slightly off the floor
3. Alternate kicking your legs up and down in a small, quick motion
exercises.tips:
Keep your lower back pressed into the floor
Keep kicks small and controlled
Breathe steadily throughout
Engage your core throughout the movement

exercises.title: Roll Outs
exercises.description: Roll Outs is a core strengthening exercise performed lying on your back. Lifting both legs engages your abdominal muscles, hip flexors, and lower back more deeply. This exercise helps improve core stability, spinal mobility, and balance.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching or straining the lower back.
Holding your breath during the exercise.
Letting legs drop or lose tension.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Rest time. Lie back, lift legs, roll hips slowly, keep core tight, breathe steady
steps: 1. Lie on your back, lift both legs so knees are slightly bent
2. Slowly roll your hips upward and forward, lifting your lower back slightly off the floor
3. Slowly roll your hips back down to the floor.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight and engaged throughout.
Move slowly and with control.
Keep legs lifted steadily without shaking.
Breathe evenly, don’t hold your breath.

exercises.title: Hollow Hold
exercises.description: The Hollow Hold is an core exercise that builds strength and endurance in the abdominal muscles, while also engaging the hip flexors, lower back, and quads. The goal is to maintain a banana-like body shape while lying on your back.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching the lower back off the floor
Holding breath during the hold
Raising legs or arms too high or too low
Straining the neck by lifting the head too much
Losing core engagement
exercises.rest_speech_text: Hollow Hold. Lie down, place your hands behind your head, elbows open. Lift your legs and shoulders, keep your lower back flat.
steps: 1. Lie on your back with legs straight and feet together.
2. Place your hands behind your head with elbows bent and open wide.
3. Press your lower back firmly against the floor.
4. Lift your legs off the floor, keeping them straight.
5. Raise your head and shoulders slightly off the floor while supporting your head with your hands.
6. Hold the position for the desired time, breathing calmly.
7. Slowly return to the floor to rest.
exercises.tips:
Gently support your head
Keep your elbows open and in line with your shoulders
Engage your abs fully to keep your lower back pressed to the ground
Breathe steadily throughout the hold

exercises.title: Diagonal Fold
exercises.description: Diagonal Fold is a gentle stretch where, lying on your back, you reach one hand to touch the opposite leg. This helps stretch your lower back, hips, and obliques, improving flexibility and releasing tension.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Lifting both shoulders off the floor.
Forcing the hand too far causing discomfort.
Holding your breath.
Not keeping the head relaxed or turning it in an uncomfortable way.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Relax. Lie down, reach one hand to opposite leg, twist gently, keep shoulders down, breathe slow
steps: 1. Lie on your back, arms relaxed by your sides, bend one knee and bring it across your body.
2. Lift your opposite hand and reach your lifted leg
3. Slowly release and switch sides.
exercises.tips:
Keep the shoulders flat on the ground.
Move slowly and only as far as comfortable.
Breathe deeply and relax.
Keep your neck comfortable — look straight or gently turn away from the bent leg.

exercises.title: Jump Twist
exercises.description: Jump Twist involves jumping up and rotating your torso to one side while extending the opposite arm outward, creating a full-body rotational movement. This exercise develops explosive power, coordination.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Incomplete torso rotation during the jump
Landing with stiff knees or poor form
Losing control during landing
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next:Jump Twist. Jump, twist your body to one side, extend both arms to the opposite side.
steps: 1. Stand feet shoulder-width apart, arms relaxed at sides.
2. Slightly bend knees, jump up, and rotate your torso to one side.
3. Extend both arms fully to the opposite side of the twist.
4. Land softly with knees bent, facing the rotated direction.
5. Repeat, twisting to the other side on the next jump.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core engaged
Land softly with knees bent
Use your arms
Focus on smooth, controlled movements

exercises.title: Dumbbell Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.description: The Dumbbell Bulgarian Split Squat is a powerful single-leg exercise that builds strength, balance, and stability in the quads, glutes, and hamstrings. It improves lower-body symmetry and mobility while also developing core stability, lumbopelvic control, and anti-extension strength. This move enhances posture, coordination, and reduces injury risk.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting the front knee go too far past the toes
Dropping the torso forward
Losing balance or rushing reps
Allowing the back leg to take too much load
exercises.rest_speech_text: Stay tall, brace your core, and get ready to feel the burn in your legs.
steps: 1. Stand a few feet in front of a bench, holding dumbbells at your sides.
2. Place the top of your back foot on the bench behind you.
3. Engage your core and keep your torso upright.
4. Lower your back knee toward the floor until your front thigh is parallel.
5. Push through your front heel to return to the starting position.
exercises.tips:
Keep your chest upright and core tight
Lower under control—don’t bounce
Drive through the front heel
Use a stable bench and moderate weights

exercises.title: Kettlebell Situp
exercises.description: The Kettlebell Situp targets the rectus abdominis and hip flexors while increasing core strength and stability. Holding a kettlebell adds resistance, enhancing lumbopelvic control, anti-extension strength, and overall trunk stability, which supports better posture and reduces injury risk.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Pulling with the arms instead of engaging the core
Arching the lower back excessively
Using momentum to rise instead of controlled movement
Not maintaining a neutral neck position
exercises.rest_speech_text: Brace your core—rise and control the movement.
steps: 1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, holding a kettlebell at your chest or extended overhead.
2. Engage your core and slowly lift your torso toward your knees.
3. Pause briefly at the top while keeping the kettlebell stable.
4. Lower your torso back to the starting position with control.
exercises.tips:
Keep the core tight throughout the movement
Exhale as you rise, inhale as you lower
Hold the kettlebell close to your chest or overhead for variation
Move slowly to maximize abdominal engagement

exercises.title: Shoulder Press
exercises.description: The Shoulder Press strengthens the deltoids, triceps, and upper chest while engaging the core for stabilization. It improves overhead pressing strength, shoulder stability, posture, and functional upper-body power for daily activities and athletic performance.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching the lower back excessively
Locking out elbows at the top of the movement
Using momentum instead of controlled motion
Letting wrists bend backward or forward
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a breath, brace your core, and get ready to press overhead with control and power.
steps: 1. Sit on the machine or bench with back supported and feet flat on the floor.
2. Grip the handles or dumbbells at shoulder height.
3. Press the weight overhead until arms are almost straight, without locking elbows.
4. Lower slowly back to shoulder height under control.
5. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight and back pressed against the pad or bench
Exhale while pressing up, inhale while lowering
Avoid shrugging shoulders—keep them down and stable
Use a full but controlled range of motion

exercises.title: Jumping Steps
exercises.description: Jumping Steps is a cardio and lower-body exercise. It improves leg strength, balance, and endurance, while raising your heart rate.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Landing hard or flat-footed
Hunching your back
Letting knees cave in
Moving too fast
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Jumping Steps. Stay light and switch feet with control.
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart
2. Slightly bend your knees and jump forward with one foot landing ahead of the other
3.Push off the back foot to jump forward again, switching the front leg.
4.Repeat in a steady rhythm—light jumps, alternating feet.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight to help balance.
Land softly.
Swing your arms to help.
Start slowly and build speed.

exercises.title: Superman
exercises.description: Superman is a core and stability exercise where you extend one arm forward and the opposite leg backward while keeping your spine neutral. This move strengthens your core, lower back, glutes, and shoulders, and improves balance and coordination.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching or rounding the back excessively
Lifting the arm or leg too high
Losing balance due to rushing
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Superman. On all fours, reach one arm forward and opposite leg back. Keep your body stable and core tight.
steps: 1. Get on all fours.
2. Extend your right arm forward and left leg back.
3. Hold for a second, keeping balance and alignment.
4. Return to starting position slowly.
5. Repeat with the left arm and right leg.
exercises.tips:
Keep hips level and core engaged
Stretch arm and leg straight out, not up
Move slowly and with control

exercises.title: Hammer Curl
exercises.description: Hammer Curls are a bicep exercise that targets the brachialis, a muscle underneath the biceps, as well as the brachioradialis in the forearm.
exercises.common_mistakes: Excessive Swinging. Poor Wrist Alignment. Not Fully Contracting.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Rest. Stand up straight, holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. Keeping the top of your arms stationary, bend your arms at the elbows to extend the dumbbells toward your shoulders. Keep your wrists straight. Lower the dumbbells to the starting position.
steps: 1. Stand up straight with a dumbbell in each hand by your sides, palms facing your body (neutral grip).
2. While keeping your upper arms stationary, bend your elbows to curl the dumbbells towards your shoulders. Keep your wrists straight.
3. As you curl the dumbbells, squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement.
4. Lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position with control, maintaining a neutral grip.
exercises.tips: Hold the dumbbells with a neutral grip (palms facing each other) throughout the exercise.

exercises.title: Chair Stretch
exercises.description: Chair Stretch is a gentle flexibility exercise done while sitting. It helps release tension in the back, shoulders, legs, and neck.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the spine.
Holding breath.
Forcing the body too far forward or sideways.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a break. For the next exercise place a chair in front of you and put your elbows on it. After that fall down and stretch your musclese
steps: 1. Put your elbows on the chair and your head below the seat.
2. Stretch your back down, raising your shoulders up.
3. Hold for a few seconds, then roll back up
exercises.tips:
Keep your back straight while moving.
Don’t bounce or rush the stretch.
Breathe in when lifting up, out when bending forward.
Keep both feet flat and stable.

exercises.title: Shoulder Roof
exercises.description: Shoulder Roof is a strength exercise where you hold a high plank and slightly shift your weight back, lifting the hips just a bit while keeping arms straight and strong. It targets shoulders, core, and upper back, improving stability and endurance.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting the hips sag or rise too much
Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears
Bending the elbows
Not engaging the core
Holding your breath
exercises.rest_speech_text: Break time. go to plank position, push the floor, feel the roof shape in your shoulders. Keep your body strong and still.
steps: 1. Start in a high plank: hands under shoulders, feet hip-width apart
2.Press through your palms, slightly lifting your hips to form a gentle “roof” shape
3. Hold the position for a few seconds.
4. Return to regular plank
exercises.tips:
Keep a straight line from head to heels
Push the floor away to activate shoulders
Engage your abs to support the spine
Keep your neck long and in line with your spine

exercises.title: Mountain Runner
exercises.description: This is a high-energy core and cardio exercise done in a plank position. You "run in place" by quickly driving your knees toward your chest while keeping your hands on the floor and your body in a straight line. It strengthens your core, shoulders, legs, and improves your endurance.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting hips sag or rise too high
Moving too fast and losing control
Not engaging the core
Bouncing shoulders forward or backward
