exercises.rest_speech_text: Get ready for Mountain Runner. Stay in plank and run your knees in—tight core, steady pace
steps: 1. Get into a plank position — hands under your shoulders, legs straight, body in one line.
2. Pull your right knee toward your chest.
3. Quickly switch — extend the right leg back and pull the left knee in.
4. Keep switching legs quickly, like you're running in place.
exercises.tips:
Don’t let your hips bounce up and down — keep them steady.
Keep your shoulders over your hands.
Breathe steadily and move at a pace you can handle.

exercises.title: Knee Rotation Standing
exercises.description: Knee Rotation is an exercise that involves rotating your knee in a circular motion while standing. Using a chair for balance, this movement helps improve joint flexibility, increase blood flow, and prepare your legs for more intense activity.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rushing the motion
Losing balance by not holding the chair
exercises.rest_speech_text: For the following exercise stand tall, hand on the chair, lift one knee, make smooth circles—switch directions
steps: 1. Stand with a chair on your side and place one hand lightly on the chair for support
2. Shift your weight to the leg closest to the chair and lift the other knee slightly in front of you
3. Gently rotate the raised knee in a circular motion
4. Gently rotate the raised knee in a circular motion
5. Perform a few reps in one direction, then reverse
6. Switch legs and repeat
exercises.tips:
Hold the chair lightly for balance
Keep your upper body steady
Make small, controlled circles

exercises.title: Cable Low Single Arm Lateral Raise
exercises.description: The Cable Low Single Arm Lateral Raise is an isolation exercise that primarily targets the lateral (middle) deltoid, helping to build shoulder width and symmetry. It also engages the traps and core for stability.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Swinging the arm or using momentum 
Raising the arm too high or beyond shoulder level
Leaning excessively to the side
Shrugging the shoulder 
Letting the cable pull the arm back too quickly
exercises.rest_speech_text: Stay tall, control the cable, and get ready to lift with precision.
steps: 1. Attach a single handle to the low pulley of a cable machine.
2. Stand sideways to the machine, with the handle in the hand farthest from the pulley.
3. Keep your feet shoulder-width apart and your core engaged.
4. Begin with your arm slightly in front of your body, palm facing inward.
5. Exhale and slowly raise your arm out to the side until it reaches shoulder height.
6. Pause briefly at the top, keeping tension on the cable.
7. Inhale and lower the handle back to the starting position under control.
exercises.tips:
Keep your torso stable and core engaged
Lead with your elbow, not your hand
Raise the arm only to shoulder height
Maintain a slight bend in the elbow throughout
Control both the lift and return phases for full muscle engagement

exercises.title: Leg raises
exercises.description: Leg Raises target the lower abdominals while also engaging the hip flexors and stabilizing the core. They improve core strength, pelvic control, and overall abdominal endurance, supporting better posture and functional movement.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching the lower back during the lift
Swinging the legs instead of controlled movement
Using momentum instead of engaging the abs
Not lowering the legs fully under control
exercises.rest_speech_text: Relax your legs, brace your core, and get ready to lift slowly and controlled, feeling your lower abs engage.
steps: 1. Lie flat on your back with arms by your sides or under your glutes for support.
2. Keep legs straight (or slightly bent) and together.
3. Lift your legs upward until they are perpendicular to the floor.
4. Slowly lower your legs back down without arching the lower back.
5. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
exercises.tips:
Keep your lower back pressed to the floor or pad
Exhale while lifting legs, inhale while lowering
Move slowly and focus on contracting the abs
If too difficult, bend the knees slightly

exercises.title: Wide Leg Bend
exercises.description: Wide Leg Bend is a simple exercise that stretches and strengthens your inner thighs, hips, and lower back. It helps improve flexibility and balance.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding or slouching the back
Locking the knees
Bouncing while stretching
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Wide Leg Bend sitting. Sit wide, lean forward slowly, and hold
steps: 1. Sit on the floor with your legs stretched wide apart, keep your back straight.
2. Slowly lean forward from your hips, reaching your hands toward your feet.
3. Keep your legs straight but don’t lock your knees.
4. Hold the stretch for 15–30 seconds.
5. Slowly sit back up.
exercises.tips:
Keep your back straight, don’t round your shoulders.
Breathe deeply and relax.

exercises.title: Side Skiing with Balance
exercises.description: Side Skiing with Balance is an exercise that mimics the motion of skiing. It is excellent for improving balance, coordination, and lateral leg strength without stressing the joints.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Leaning too far forward or backward
Not engaging core muscles
Rushing the movement without balance pause
exercises.rest_speech_text: Rest time. For the next exercise, stand tall,slide your leg to the side, then switch. Keep it slow and balanced.
steps: 1. Stand upright with feet hip-width apart.
2. Shift your weight onto the left leg and slightly bend it
3. Slide your right leg to the side with control while keeping toes facing forward.
4. Pause briefly at the widest point for balance.
5. Bring the leg back to starting position.
exercises.tips:
Keep your torso upright and abs tight
Maintain a soft bend in the knees
Pause briefly after each side for better balance

exercises.title: Ball Kick
exercises.description: The Ball Kick in a side-lying position is a controlled lower-body movement that targets the outer thighs, glutes, and hip stabilizers. This is great for toning legs and improving hip mobility and balance.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rolling the hips backward or forward
Using impulse instead of controlled motion
Not keeping the leg straight during the kick
Arching the lower back
exercises.rest_speech_text: Lie on your side, lift your top leg and kick forward, then back — stay stable and in control.
steps: 1. Lie on your side with legs extended and stacked, rest your head on your lower arm and place the top hand on the floor for balance.
2. Lift your top leg slightly above hip height, slowly kick your leg forward with control.
3. Without lowering the leg, sweep it backward past your hip, return to center and repeat the motion.
4. Switch sides
exercises.tips:
Keep your hips stacked and core engaged
Kick with control, not speed
Keep your upper body relaxed

exercises.title: Barbell Hip Thrust
exercises.description: The Barbell Hip Thrust is a powerful lower-body exercise that primarily targets the glutes while also engaging the hamstrings and core. It is one of the best movements for building glute strength, improving hip extension power, and enhancing overall athletic performance.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching the lower back
Placing the feet too far forward or too close to the body                                                               Dropping the chin back
Performing partial reps without reaching full hip extension
Letting knees cave inward
exercises.rest_speech_text: Brace your core, drive through your heels, and get ready to power up.
steps: 1. Sit on the ground with your upper back against a bench and roll a padded barbell over your hips.
2. Bend your knees and place your feet flat on the floor, shoulder-width apart.
3. Brace your core, tuck your chin, and keep your torso tight.
4. Drive through your heels, lifting your hips until they are fully extended.
5. At the top, pause and squeeze your glutes.
6. Lower your hips slowly back to the ground with control.
exercises.tips:
Keep your chin tucked and eyes forward
Drive through your heels, not your toes
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top and hold briefly
Position the barbell with padding 
Keep shins vertical at the top of the movement

exercises.title: Roof Kickback
exercises.description: The Roof Kickback is a glute-focused bodyweight exercise performed on hands and knees. You lift one leg up and back, as if pressing the sole of your foot toward “roof.” This move strengthens your glutes, hamstrings, and lower back.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching the lower back too much
Not keeping the core engaged
Letting the neck drop or straining it
Kicking too fast, losing control
Not lifting the leg high enough to engage glutes properly
exercises.rest_speech_text: Rest time. On hands and knees — kick your foot up like you’re pressing the roof. Keep your core tight and move slow
steps: 1. Get on all fours — hands under shoulders, knees under hips
2. Lift one leg, bend the knee, and press the foot up toward the ceiling
3. Squeeze the glute at the top
4. Lower the leg without touching the floor
5. Repeat and switch legs
exercises.tips:
Keep your back flat and core tight
Move slowly and with control
Keep your head in line with your spine

exercises.title: Full Squat on Place
exercises.description: The Full Squat on Place is a deep bodyweight squat where you lower your hips as close to the floor as possible while keeping your heels grounded. This movement strengthens the lower body, improves hip and ankle mobility.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting the knees cave inward
Lifting the heels off the floor
Rounding the back or leaning too far forward
Bouncing at the bottom of the squat
Not engaging the core
exercises.rest_speech_text: Stand tall, feet shoulder-width apart. Drop into a deep squat while keeping your heels on the floor.
steps: 1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly turned out.
2. Slowly bend your knees and lower your hips down as far as possible.
3. Keep your heels firmly planted on the ground and knees tracking over your toes.
4. Hold the bottom position briefly, then press through your heels to stand back up.
exercises.tips:
Keep your feet shoulder-width apart                  Push your knees outward in line with your toes
Keep your heels flat and chest lifted
Lower slowly and avoid bouncing
Engage your core for balance and support

exercises.title: Seated Forward Bend
exercises.description: This exercise is performed while sitting on a chair and focuses on stretching the shoulders, chest, and upper back. A slow forward bend from the hips helps improve spinal mobility, posture, and shoulder flexibility.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the back
Jerking the motion forward
Dropping the head too low
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a break. Sit on a chair, arms extended behind you. Gently bend forward and feel the stretch in your back and shoulders.
steps: 1. Sit upright on a chair.
2. Feet flat on the floor, arms extended behind and clasped
3. Slowly bend forward from the hips, keep your back straight, neck relaxed
4. Hold the stretch, then gently return to starting position
exercises.tips:
Move smoothly
Keep your back straight
Breathe slowly and deeply

exercises.title: Elbow Cat Cow Pose
exercises.description: The Elbow Cat Cow Pose is a spine stretch done on your elbows and knees. It helps improve back flexibility, eases tension, and warms up your spine.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting elbows slide forward or backward.
Moving too fast or jerking the spine.
Holding breath during movement.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Elbow Cat Cow. On elbows and knees, arch your back in, then round it out slowly.
steps: 1. Start on your hands and knees..
2. Lower down so your elbows touch the floor, keeping them under your shoulders.
3. Breathe in: Arch your back gently, lifting your chest and tailbone
4. Breathe out: Round your back, tucking your chin and tailbone
exercises.tips:
Move slowly and smoothly between poses.
Keep your elbows steady on the floor.
Breathe deeply and evenly.

exercises.title: Side Neck Stretch
exercises.description: The Side Neck Stretch is an exercise that helps relax your neck and shoulders. It reduces tension, improves flexibility.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Lifting the shoulder
Tilting or twisting the torso
Pulling too hard on your head
Holding your breath
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Side Neck Stretch. Sit or stand tall, gently tilt your head to one side, and hold.
steps: 1. Sit or stand up straight.
2. Slowly tilt your head to one side, bringing your ear toward your shoulder.
3. Hold the stretch for about 15–30 seconds.
4. Switch sides and repeat.
exercises.tips:
Keep your shoulders relaxed, don’t let them rise.
Don’t force the stretch — it should feel gentle.
Breathe deeply and slowly.

exercises.title: Sitting Press
exercises.description: This is a strength exercise where you sit and press a kettlebell overhead with one or both hands. It targets your shoulders, arms, and upper back, and improves core stability while keeping pressure off your legs.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching your lower back
Using too heavy a kettlebell
Shrugging your shoulders
Letting your wrist bend backward
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Sitting Press with Kettlebell. Sit tall and press the weight straight up.
steps: 1. Sit on the floor with your legs extended out in front of you, spread apart slightly.
2. Hold a kettlebell at shoulder height with one hand or both hands.
3. Press the kettlebell up until your arm is straight overhead
4. Lower it back down slowly to shoulder level.
5. Do the reps, then switch arms
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight to support your back.
Sit up straight, don’t lean backward.
Use a light kettlebell at first to avoid strain.
Breathe out as you press up, breathe in as you lower.

exercises.title: Basic Crunch
exercises.description: A basic crunch is a core-strengthening exercise where you lie on your back, bend your knees, and lift your upper body slightly off the ground to engage your abdominal muscles. It’s great for building core strength and improving posture.
exercises.common_mistakes: Pulling the neck with your hands.                         Not keeping your lower back on the ground. Holding your breathe.                                       Lifting too high using the impulse , not your abs
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next up: basic crunches. Lie on your back, bend your knees, and get ready to lift with your core
steps: 1. Lie down on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
2. Place your hands behind your head, with your elbows pointing outwards.
3. Lift your shoulders and upper back off the floor, engaging your abdominal muscles.
4. Hold for the moment, then slowly lower down
exercises.tips: Lift with your abs not with the neck.                   Don't go too fast, it's not about speed

exercises.title: Barbell Bench Press (Flat & Incline)
exercises.description: The Barbell Bench Press strengthens the chest, shoulders, and triceps while improving upper-body pushing power. The flat version targets the mid-chest, while the incline emphasizes the upper chest and shoulders. Both variations develop core stability, lumbopelvic control, and anti-extension strength.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching the lower back excessively
Flaring elbows outward
Bouncing the bar off the chest
Using momentum instead of controlled movement
exercises.rest_speech_text: Brace your core, chest up—press with control.
steps: 1. Lie on a flat or incline bench with feet planted firmly on the floor.
2. Grip the barbell slightly wider than shoulder-width.
3. Lower the bar to your chest with elbows at 45°–75° to your torso.
4. Press the bar back up to full arm extension.
exercises.tips:
Keep your feet flat and core tight
Lower the bar slowly to the chest and press with control
Maintain shoulder blades retracted and elbows at a 45°–75° angle
Exhale while pressing and inhale while lowering

exercises.title: Triceps Extension Machine
exercises.description: The Triceps Extension Machine isolates and strengthens the triceps brachii, improving arm definition, pushing strength, and elbow stability. It provides a controlled movement that reduces strain on the shoulder joint while targeting the posterior arm muscles effectively.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Using momentum or swinging the arms
Lifting elbows off the pad or moving them outward
Not fully extending the elbows at the bottom
Curling too fast without control
exercises.rest_speech_text: Relax your arms, brace your core, and get ready to push with control, feeling your triceps work.
steps: 1. Sit on the triceps extension machine and adjust the seat so your elbows align with the pivot point.
2. Grip the handles with elbows fixed in place.
3. Extend your arms fully, contracting the triceps at the bottom.
4. Slowly return to the starting position with control.
5. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
exercises.tips:
Keep elbows fixed and close to the body
Exhale while extending the arms, inhale while returning
Focus on squeezing the triceps at full extension
Maintain a slow, controlled motion throughout

exercises.title: Overhead Arm Drop
exercises.description: The Overhead Arm Drop is a shoulder and upper back movement where you raise your arms overhead and then slowly lower them down. It helps improve shoulder mobility, posture, and gently works the upper body muscles.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching the back too much
Shrugging the shoulders
Moving too fast
Locking the elbows
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Overhead Arm Drop. Sit on the chair, raise your arms, then lower slowly."
steps: 1. Sit on a chair with your back straight, feet flat on the ground, and arms by your sides.
2. Raise both arms straight up overhead, keeping your shoulders relaxed.
3. Lower your arms back down in a controlled motion to the starting position.
4. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight and shoulders relaxed.
Move slowly and with control—no swinging.
Breathe in when lifting, breathe out when lowering.

exercises.title: Standing One Foot
exercises.description: This exercise develops balance, stability, and ankle mobility by standing on one foot while extending the other leg forward. Adding the flex-and-point movement strengthens the ankles, calves, and feet, improves circulation, and enhances coordination.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Leaning the torso too far forward or sideways
Locking the knee of the supporting leg
Moving the lifted leg too high, causing imbalance
Rushing through the flex-and-point instead of slow, controlled motions
Forgetting to breathe during holds
exercises.rest_speech_text: Stand tall shift your weight, and get ready to balance on one leg while flexing and pointing your foot.
steps: 1. Stand tall near a wall, chair, or table for support.
2. Shift your weight onto your left foot, lifting your right foot a few inches off the floor and extending it forward.
3. Hold this position.
4. Flex and point your lifted foot.
5. Slowly return your right foot to the floor.
6. Switch sides and repeat with the left leg.
exercises.tips:
Stand near a wall, chair, or table for safety support
Keep your gaze fixed on a point in front of you
Engage your core to prevent wobbling
Lift the leg only a few inches
Perform the ankle flex-and-point slowly

exercises.title: Rotational Arm Reach
exercises.description: Rotational Arm Reach is a gentle seated twist where you reach one arm across your body while turning your torso. It helps improve spine flexibility, engage the core, and loosen tight shoulders
exercises.common_mistakes:
Twisting only the arm, not the torso
Shrugging shoulders upward
Leaning back instead of rotating
Moving too fast
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a break and sit tall, twist gently, and reach across your body. Breathe and relax.
steps: 1.Sit on a chair with feet flat, back upright and extend one arm in front of you
2. Rotate your torso and reach the arm across to the opposite side
3. Return to center and repeat to other side
exercises.tips:
Keep both feet flat on the floor
Sit up tall before rotating
Move slowly and breathe steadily
Focus on reaching diagonally, not just sideways

exercises.title: Sprinters Sit Ups
exercises.description: Sprinter Sit Ups are a full-body core move. You lie down and then sit up fast, lifting one knee toward your chest while reaching with the opposite arm — like a running motion. This works your abs, hips, and coordination.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Swinging arms too much (not using muscles)
Rounding your back or straining your neck
Letting your feet slam to the floor
Moving too fast
Not fully engaging the core
exercises.rest_speech_text: Up next: sprinter sit-ups. Lie on your back, get ready to sit up fast and drive one knee to your chest like you're running
steps: 1. Lie flat on your back with your legs straight and your arms at your sides.
2. Tighten your abs
3.Sit up fast and lift your right knee toward your chest and at the same time, reach your left arm forward as if sprinting
4. Return to lying down
5. Repeat with the opposite leg and arm
exercises.tips: Make sure to lift your feet off the floor with each repetition to effectively engage your abs. Don't move too fast and keep your core tight whole time

exercises.title: Chair Squat
exercises.description: Chair squats are a glute exercise where you sit down and stand up from a chair. It helps build strength, balance, and good form for regular squats.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Knees caving inward
Rounding the back
Sitting too hard or fast
Leaning too far forward
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Chair Squats. Stand tall in front of the chair, lower down like you're sitting, and push up to stand again
steps: 1. Stand in front of a chair, feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Keep your chest up and arms stretched out in front for balance.
3. Slowly bend your knees and lower yourself down as if you’re going to sit.
4. Tap the chair lightly
5. Push through your heels and stand back up.
exercises.tips:
Keep your weight in your heels, not your toes.
Don't let your knees go past your toes.
Keep your back straight and core engaged.

exercises.title: Seated Spinal Twist
exercises.description: Seated Spinal Twist is a stretch exercise that improves spinal mobility and flexibility in the back, shoulders, and hips. It also helps reduce tension and improve posture.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the back instead of sitting tall
Forcing the twist, causing discomfort
Holding the breath
Letting the shoulders rise or twist unevenly
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a moment to relax and center yourself after completing the Seated Spinal Twist. Ready for more? Let's maintain that calm focus as we transition into the next yoga pose.
steps: 1. Sit on chair with legs extended, keep your back straight and shoulders relaxed.
2.Place your right hand behind you and your left hand on your right knee.
3. Breathe out and gently twist your upper body to the right.
4. Hold the stretch while breathing slowly.
5. Return to center and repeat on the other side.
exercises.tips:
Sit up straight to lengthen your spine
Breathe deeply and twist gently
Keep both sitting bones grounded
Use your hand behind you for light support

exercises.title: Kettlebell Goblet Squat
exercises.description: The Kettlebell Goblet Squat is a lower-body exercise that targets the quads, glutes, and hamstrings while improving hip mobility and core stability. Holding the kettlebell in front of the chest enhances lumbopelvic control, anti-extension strength, and upright posture, reducing injury risk during dynamic or loaded movements.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Leaning forward excessively
Letting knees cave inward
Lifting heels off the floor
Using momentum instead of controlled movement
exercises.rest_speech_text: Chest up, core tight—get ready to squat strong.
steps: 1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a kettlebell close to your chest.
2. Engage your core and push your hips back as you squat down.
3. Keep your chest upright and knees aligned with your toes.
4. Lower until thighs are parallel to the floor, then press through your heels to return upright.
5. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
exercises.tips:
Keep your chest lifted and core engaged
Push your hips back as you squat down
Maintain weight evenly on your heels
Lower slowly and drive upward through the heels

exercises.title: Kettlebell Clean & Press
exercises.description: The Kettlebell Clean & Press is a full-body, compound exercise that develops strength, power, and coordination. The clean phase engages the glutes, hamstrings, quads, lats, and core, while the press emphasizes shoulders, triceps, and upper chest. It also improves core stability, lumbopelvic control, and anti-extension strength, enhancing posture and functional strength.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Using the arms too much during the clean
Leaning back or arching the lower back during the press
Dropping the kettlebell uncontrolled
Rushing the movement and losing coordination
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a deep breath, brace your core, reset your grip, and get ready to clean and press with control.
steps: 1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, kettlebell on the floor.
2. Hinge at the hips, grab the kettlebell, and perform a clean by driving through the hips to bring it to shoulder height.
3. Brace your core and press the kettlebell overhead until the arm is fully extended.
4. Lower the kettlebell back to the shoulder, then to the floor, under control.
5. Repeat for the desired number of reps, alternating sides if using a single kettlebell.
exercises.tips:
Hinge at the hips for the clean and snap them forward explosively
Keep the core tight and spine neutral during the press
Press the kettlebell overhead in a straight line
Move slowly and under control to maintain proper form

exercises.title: Cactus Arms Rotations
exercises.description: This is a mobility and shoulder-opening exercise. You lift your arms and bend your elbows so your forearms point straight ahead. and rotate them forward and back to improve shoulder range of motion and posture.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Lifting shoulders up to ears
Rushing the movement
Arching the back or twisting the torso
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Cactus Arms Rotation. Bend your elbows like a cactus and rotate your arms forward and back. Get ready.
steps: 1. Stand tall, back straight.
2. Raise your arms to shoulder height and bend your elbows.
3. Slowly rotate your arms forward, bringing your forearms in front of you.
4. Then rotate your arms back, trying to bring the forearms in line with your shoulders again.
exercises.tips:
Keep your shoulders down and relaxed.
Move only your shoulders, not your back or spine.
Keep your core gently engaged.

exercises.title: Side Lunges
exercises.description: Side lunges strengthen your legs, glutes, and inner thighs while improving balance and mobility. You step out to the side and lower into a lunge.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Bending the spine forward
Letting the knee collapse inward
Taking too small of a step
exercises.rest_speech_text: Break time. Next: Side Lunges. Step out to the side, bend one knee, keep the other leg straight, then return. Get ready.
steps: 1.Stand tall with feet together, hands at your chest or on hips.
2. Take a big step to the right, keeping your left leg straight.
3. Bend your right knee and push your hips back, lowering into a side lunge.
4. Keep your chest lifted and right knee over your right foot.
5. Push off your right foot to return to the starting position.
6. Repeat on the left side. Alternate sides.
exercises.tips:
Keep both feet flat on the floor.
Don’t let your knee go past your toes.
Move slowly and with control.

exercises.title: Cable Crossover
exercises.description: The Cable Crossover is a dynamic chest isolation exercise that targets the pectoral muscles from multiple angles. It builds muscle definition, enhances shoulder stability, and improves functional pushing strength. The continuous cable tension keeps the chest engaged throughout the entire range of motion, making it an excellent finisher for chest workouts.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Using too much weight and relying on momentum
Letting the arms go too far back, stressing the shoulders
Leaning excessively forward
Not maintaining slight elbow bend throughout the motion
exercises.rest_speech_text: Shake out your arms, stay tall, and get ready to bring your hands together with power and control through your chest.
steps: 1. Set the pulleys to chest height (or adjust to desired angle).
2. Stand in the center, holding one handle in each hand with a slight forward lean.
3. Start with your arms extended out to the sides, elbows slightly bent.
4. Bring your hands together in front of your chest in a smooth arc.
5. Squeeze your chest at the center, then slowly return to the starting position with control.
exercises.tips:
Keep a small bend in your elbows at all times
Maintain a steady, controlled movement—avoid swinging
Squeeze your chest at the center of the motion
Adjust cable height to hit different parts of the ches

exercises.title: Hip Lifting
exercises.description: Hip lifting is an exercise where you raise your hips while lying on your back. It targets the glutes, hamstrings, and lower back, and helps improve core stability and hip strength.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Using your lower back too much instead of glutes
Lifting too high and overextending the spine
Letting knees fall outward or inward
exercises.rest_speech_text: Hip Lifting. Lie on your back, bend your knees, lift your hips up, then lower slowly. Get ready.
steps: 1. Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, keep your arms by your sides, palms facing down.
2. Squeeze your glutes and slowly lift your hips up toward the ceiling and hold for a second at the top
3.Slowly lower your hips back down.
exercises.tips:
Keep your feet flat and don’t lift your heels.
Avoid arching your back—lift using your hips and glutes.
Engage your core for better support.

exercises.title: Fronted Bent Elbows Raises
exercises.description: This exercise targets the shoulders and upper back. You raise your bent arms in front of you, which helps improve posture, build shoulder strength, and support upper body control.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Lifting the hands instead of the elbows
Straightening the arms
Swinging
exercises.rest_speech_text: Fronted Bent Elbows Raise. Stand tall, bend your arms in front of you. Raise your elbows to shoulder height, then lower slowly. Get ready.
steps: 1. Stand tall, arms bent, elbows close to your sides, palms facing each other.
2. Slowly raise your elbows in front of you to shoulder height
3. Lower them slowly back down.
exercises.tips:
Keep your back straight—no leaning back.
Lift with control—don’t rush.
Keep elbows in line with your shoulders, not higher.

exercises.title: Neck Twist
exercises.description: Neck Twist is an exercise that improves neck mobility and flexibility. It helps relieve tension in the neck and upper shoulders.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Twisting too quickly or forcefully
Moving the shoulders along with the neck
Holding the breath during the movement
Over-rotating
exercises.rest_speech_text: Prepare for neck twists. Sit tall, relax your shoulders, and slowly turn your head side to side.
steps: 1. Sit on a chair, back and neck straight.
2. Slowly turn your head to the right, Immediately return to the starting position.
3. Immediately return to the starting position.
4. Repeat the movement in the other direction.
exercises.tips:
Sit with your back straight
Move your head slowly
Keep your shoulders relaxed 
Breathe deeply
Only twist to a comfortable range

exercises.title: Star Jump
exercises.description: A Star Jump is a dynamic full-body cardio move where you jump up and spread your arms and legs wide. It boosts explosiveness, coordination, heart rate, and muscle endurance.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Landing with straight legs
Letting knees collapse inward
Slouching or leaning back during the jump
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Star Jumps. Big jump—arms and legs out like a star!
steps: 1.Stand tall with feet together and arms at your sides.
2. Squat slightly, bending your knees.
3. Jump straight up, spreading your legs and arms outward into a star shape.
4. Land softly with knees slightly bent, returning to the starting position.
5.Repeat.
exercises.tips:
Engage your core to stay stable in the air.
Land lightly on your feet to protect your knees.
Use your arms when jumping.
Keep a steady rhythm—don’t rush.

exercises.title: Overhead Arms Raise
exercises.description: Overhead Arms Raise is a gentle stretching and mobility exercise performed in a standing position that improves shoulder flexibility and mobility,activates upper body muscles and enhances posture
exercises.common_mistakes:
Flaring elbows outward too much
Raising arms without full extension
Leaning backward while raising
Moving too quickly
exercises.rest_speech_text: Start with elbows bent at your sides. Raise and extend your arms overhead, then return slowly.
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart, bend your elbows at your sides so your hands are near your shoulders.
2. Raise and extend your arms upward, reaching overhead.
3. Pause briefly at the top.
4. Slowly reverse the motion, bending elbows back to the starting position.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core lightly engaged
Move arms in a smooth, controlled arc
Fully extend the elbows overhead
Keep neck relaxed and avoid shrugging

exercises.title: Skiing
exercises.description: The Skiing exercise is a cardio and coordination move that mimics the action of skiing downhill. It helps to improve balance, agility, and cardiovascular endurance.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Stiff legs and no knee bend
Forgetting to use the arms
Losing balance due to poor posture
Not breathing steadily
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Skiing. Jump side to side like you're on skis—light feet, strong core!
steps: 1. Stand with your back straight, arms at your sides, legs together.
2.Bend your knees slightly and get into a small squat
3. Jump to the right, landing on both feet, swinging arms as if holding ski poles.
4. Jump to the left right away, swinging your arms in the opposite direction
5. Keep jumping side to side in a smooth rhythm.
6. Stay light on your feet and keep your knees soft.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight to stay balanced.
Land softly and avoid locking your knees.
Use your arms to help with rhythm and coordination.
Start slow, then pick up speed as you get more comfortable.

exercises.title: Spine Extension Facelying
exercises.description: This is an exercise where you lie on your stomach and lift your upper body slightly. It helps strengthen the back, improve posture, and support a healthy spine.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Lifting too high
Pushing with your hands
Arching the neck
Holding your breath
exercises.rest_speech_text: Spine Extension Facelying. Lie on your belly. Keep your hands by your sides. Lift your chest a little and hold. Get ready.
steps: 1.Lie on your stomach, arms at your sides or under your shoulders.
2. Rest your forehead gently on the floor.
3. Slowly lift your chest, shoulders, and head a little off the ground.
4. Keep your neck long—don’t look up and hold for 2-3 seconds
5. Slowly lower down
exercises.tips:
Keep your shoulders relaxed, not squeezed.
Don’t use your arms to push—lift with your back muscles.
Don't lift too high. It’s not about height—it’s about control.
Breathe out as you lift, breathe in as you lower.

exercises.title: Dumbbell Kneeling Single Arm Row
exercises.description: The Dumbbell Kneeling Single Arm Row strengthens the back, shoulders, and arms while improving posture and stability. Working one side at a time enhances muscle balance and coordination. It also develops core stability, lumbopelvic control, and anti-rotation strength.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Twisting the torso or jerking the weight
Dropping the shoulder of the working arm
Overextending at the top of the movement
Using momentum instead of controlled motion
exercises.rest_speech_text: Keep your core steady—get ready to pull strong and controlled.
steps: 1. Place one knee and the same-side hand on a bench, holding a dumbbell in the opposite hand.
2. Keep your back straight and core engaged.
3. Pull the dumbbell upward toward your hip, squeezing your back muscles.
4. Pause briefly, then lower the dumbbell under control.
5. Complete reps on one side, then switch arms.
exercises.tips:
Keep your back flat and core tight
Pull the dumbbell toward your hip, not your shoulder
Move slowly and control both lift and descent
Keep your head in line with your spine

exercises.title: Toy Abs
exercises.description: Toy Abs is dynamic core exercise where you lie on your back and move your arms and legs like a wind-up toy. It targets the abs, especially the lower belly, and also improves coordination.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting your lower back lift off the floor
Moving too fast
Straining the neck or shoulders
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Toy Abs. Lie on your back, arms and legs up—get ready to march!
steps: 1. Lie on your back with your arms and legs lifted off the floor.
2. Keep your knees bent and arms straight up.
3. Tighten your core to keep your lower back on the floor.
4. Start to move opposite arms and legs, like you're marching in the air.
5. Keep switching sides in a controlled rhythm.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight the whole time.
Move slowly and with control.
Keep your head down and neck relaxed.
If it’s hard, keep your knees higher or feet closer to your body.

exercises.title: Oblique Stretch
exercises.description: The Oblique Stretch targets the oblique muscles on the sides of your abdomen. It's great for improving side body flexibility, relieving tension in the torso, and promoting better posture.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Leaning too far forward instead of to the side
Lifting the opposite hip off the chair
Holding your breath
Twisting instead of side bending
exercises.rest_speech_text: Great job! Sit tall, raise one arm, support it with the other hand, bend gently to the side.
steps: 1. Sit upright on a chair, feet flat on the floor
2. Raise your right arm overhead and use your left hand to gently hold the right wrist
3. Slowly bend to the left, feeling the stretch along your right side
4. Hold for 10–20 seconds, breathing deeply
5. Return to center and switch sides
exercises.tips:
Keep both feet flat on the floor
Sit tall and keep your back straight
Reach gently—not forcefully
Breathe slowly throughout the stretch

exercises.title: T-Bar Machine
exercises.description: The T-Bar Row Machine targets the mid-back muscles, including the lats, traps, and rhomboids, while also engaging the biceps and rear shoulders. It builds pulling strength, improves posture, and supports overall upper-body stability and functional strength.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the back or leaning excessively forward
Using momentum instead of controlled movement
Pulling with the arms instead of leading with the elbows
Not maintaining a stable core throughout the lift
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a breath, brace your core, and get ready to pull with control, leading with your elbows and engaging your back.
steps: 1. Position yourself on the T-Bar Row Machine, feet firmly on the platform and chest against the pad if available.
2. Grip the handles securely with both hands.
3. Pull the weight toward your torso by driving your elbows back.
4. Squeeze your back muscles at the top of the movement.
5. Slowly return to the starting position under control and repeat.
exercises.tips:
Keep your chest up and back straight
Lead the row with your elbows, not your hands
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the peak contraction
Control the weight on both the pulling and returning phases

exercises.title: Hanging Squat with Ball
exercises.description: Hanging Squat with Ball is a strength exercise where you perform a squat while holding a soft ball between your back and a wall. This setup helps guide proper form, supports balance, and reduces pressure on the knees.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Feet placed too close to the wall
Knees pushing past the toes
Lifting heels off the ground
Moving too fast
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a break. Stand with the ball behind your back against the wall. Slowly squat down, then push back up using your legs
steps: 1. Stand with your back against a soft ball pressed between you and a wall.
2. Slowly lower into a squat, keeping knees in line with toes.oor.
3. Press through your heels to return to standing.
exercises.tips:
Keep your feet slightly forward from the wall
Maintain contact between your back and the ball
Lower slowly and avoid leaning too far forward
Push through your heels to rise up

exercises.title: Leg Span with Torniquet
exercises.description: This stretch is done standing, with feet spread wide and a strap or resistance band used for support or added tension. It helps improve flexibility in the inner thighs, hamstrings, and hips.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Locking the knees
Rounding the back too much
Going too fast
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Standing Leg Stretch. Feet wide, bend forward, feel the stretch."
steps: 1. Stand tall with your feet wide apart
2. Place a tourniquet under one leg and wrap the other leg around it.
3. Then smoothly raise your straight leg back until your shin is parallel to the floor.
4. Return to the starting position and repeat.
exercises.tips:
Keep your toes pointing slightly forward or outward.
Engage your core to protect your lower back.
Don’t force it—gentle tension only.
Use a chair or wall for balance if needed.

exercises.title: Stretching Sides
exercises.description: Stretching Sides targets the sides of your torso and spine while seated comfortably on a chair. It improves flexibility in the obliques and helps relieve tension from prolonged sitting or poor posture.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Leaning forward or backward 
Lifting both hips off the chair
Holding breath during the stretch
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Side Stretch on the Chair. Sit up tall, reach one arm overhead, and gently bend to the side.
steps: 1. Sit on a chair with feet flat on the floor.
2. Place one hand on the chair or thigh for support.
3. Raise the opposite arm overhead and gently lean to that side
4. Hold the stretch for a few seconds while breathing.
5. Return to center and repeat on the other side.
exercises.tips:
Keep both feet flat on the floor
Sit tall with a straight back
Only one hip should lift slightly

exercises.title: Arms Circles
exercises.description: Arm Circles is a shoulder-focused movement performed in a standing position. With arms extended out to the sides, you gently raise and lower them in a controlled arc. This targets shoulder mobility, deltoid endurance.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Swinging arms too fast
Bending elbows
Lifting shoulders up toward the ears
Arching the back during movement
Forgetting to engage the core
exercises.rest_speech_text: Rest time. Stand tall, arms to the sides. Raise and lower them with control. Feel the shoulders work.
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Extend your arms fully out to the sides, shoulder-height, palms down.
3. Slowly raise your arms upward.
4. Without bending your elbows, lower your arms back down.
exercises.tips:
Keep your arms straight and level with the shoulders
Move slowly and with control
Maintain a neutral spine and engaged core
Breathe steadily throughout
Stop if you feel shoulder strain or pain

exercises.title: Yoga Backbend
exercises.description: A yoga backbend is a movement where you arch your spine backward. It opens up the chest, shoulders, and hip flexors, strengthens the back, and improves flexibility and posture.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Knees falling apart
Holding your breath
Lifting with only the lower back
Putting weight into the neck
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Standing position. Stand tall, feet apart, core engaged. Get ready.
steps: 1.Stand with your feet hip-width apart.
2. Distribute your weight evenly on both feet.
3. Keep your knees soft, not locked and let your arms rest naturally by your sides.
4. Straighten your back and lift your chest slightly.
5. Roll your shoulders back and down.
6. Look straight ahead and gently engage your core.
exercises.tips:
Keep your neck relaxed.
Squeeze your glutes and core for support.
Don’t over-arch your lower back—lift evenly.
Breathe deeply.

exercises.title: Kettlebell Skull Crusher
exercises.description: The Kettlebell Skull Crusher isolates the triceps, building strength and definition in the upper arms. Using a kettlebell allows for a natural wrist position and better grip control. It also enhances core stability and anti-extension strength, supporting safe posture during overhead and pressing movements.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Flaring elbows outward
Arching the lower back
Dropping the kettlebell too quickly
Using momentum instead of controlled motion
exercises.rest_speech_text: Elbows tight, core engaged—press with control.
steps: 1. Lie on a flat bench or the floor holding a kettlebell in both hands, arms extended above your chest.
2. Keep elbows close to your head and core engaged.
3. Lower the kettlebell toward your forehead by bending the elbows.
4. Pause briefly, then press back up to the starting position.
5. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
exercises.tips:
Keep elbows tucked close to your head
Lower the kettlebell slowly with control
Engage your core to protect your lower back
Focus on squeezing the triceps at the top

exercises.title: High Knee Hands Up
exercises.description: High Knee Hands Up is a cardio move that boosts your heart rate while engaging your core, legs, and arms. It combines high knees with your arms reaching upward, improving coordination, endurance, and full-body activation.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Dropping arms down
Leaning back or forward
Letting knees stay too low
Forgetting to engage your core
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: High Knee Hands Up. Lift your knees and keep your arms high.
steps: 1.Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and arms raised straight overhead.
2. Begin to jog in place, lifting your knees up towards your chest and alternating legs.
3. As you lift each knee, swing your opposite arm forward to help generate momentum.
4. Continue lifting your knees and swinging your arms for the desired duration of the exercise.
exercises.tips:
Keep your arms straight and strong overhead.
Lift your knees high, not just fast.
Breathe regularly and stay in rhythm.

exercises.title: Heel Touches
exercises.description: Heel Touches are a great core exercise that focuses on the side abs. You lie on your back and reach side to side to touch your heels, which helps tighten and tone the waistline.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting the shoulders drop flat
Rushing the movement
Straining your neck
Lifting feet off the ground
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Heel Touches. Lie back, lift your shoulders, and reach side to side.
steps: 1.Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
2. Keep your arms down by your sides.
3. Lift your shoulders slightly off the ground—this engages your core.
4.Reach your right hand toward your right heel, then back to center.
5. Now reach your left hand toward your left heel.
6. Keep alternating sides in a steady, controlled motion.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight the whole time.
Move slowly and with control, not fast.
Don’t pull on your neck—keep your head relaxed.
Keep your feet still on the floor.

exercises.title: Pistol Stretch
exercises.description: This is stretching exercise that targets the neck, upper back, and obliques. It helps release tension in the neck and shoulders, improves posture, and enhances spinal mobility.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Twisting too forcefully
Moving the arm and head to the same side
Slouching in the chair
exercises.rest_speech_text: In the next exercise sit tall, stretch one arm to the side, gently turn your head the other way, and breathe.
steps: 1.Sit upright on a chair with feet flat on the ground.
2.Extend one arm out to the side and turn your head to opposite side
3. Hold for 10–20 seconds.
4. Switch sides and repeat.
exercises.tips:
Sit tall with your back straight
Keep shoulders relaxed
Move slowly and with control
Breathe in as you stretch, breathe out as you hold

exercises.title: Slow Box
exercises.description: Slow Box is a controlled, cardio and coordination exercise. It helps to build shoulder endurance, core stability, and focus. It’s great for warming up or improving neuromuscular control.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Throwing punches too fast, losing control
Slouching your back or shoulders
Not rotating the torso
Locking elbows completely during punches
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a break. Stand strong, fists up. Slowly punch forward, one arm at a time. Breathe steady, stay in control.
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart and raise your fists near your chin like a boxer
2. Slowly extend your right arm forward to punch.
3. Pull it back, then punch with your left arm.
4. Keep alternating arms at a slow, controlled pace
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight and back straight
Punch forward slowly and smoothly
Breathe out with each punch to engage your core
Keep your knees slightly bent for better balance

exercises.title: Kettlebell Deadlift (Single)
exercises.description: The Single Kettlebell Deadlift strengthens the hamstrings, glutes, lower back, and core while improving hip hinge mechanics and unilateral stability. Using one kettlebell at a time also develops core stability, lumbopelvic control, and anti-rotation strength, promoting proper posture and reducing injury risk.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the back or shoulders
Bending the knees excessively or locking them
Using the arms to lift instead of hinging at the hips
Twisting or leaning to one side during the lift
exercises.rest_speech_text: Hinge with control, core tight—lift strong from the hips.
steps: 1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a kettlebell in one hand in front of your thighs.
2. Engage your core and hinge at the hips, keeping a slight bend in the supporting knee.
3. Lower the kettlebell toward the floor while keeping your back flat.
4. Drive your hips forward to return to standing, squeezing the glutes at the top.
5. Repeat for the desired reps, then switch sides.
exercises.tips:
Keep your spine neutral and core engaged
Push hips back while lowering the kettlebell
Maintain a slight bend in the supporting knee
Lift and lower the kettlebell in a controlled manner

exercises.title: Standing Butterfly Stroke
exercises.description: This exercise mimics the arm movements of the butterfly swimming stroke but done standing. It helps strengthen the shoulders, upper back, and arms while also improving coordination and mobility.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Moving arms too fast or jerky
Shrugging shoulders up to ears
Arching or leaning backward
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Standing Butterfly Stroke. Move your arms wide like swimming
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Extend your arms straight out in front of you at shoulder height, palms facing down.
3.Pull your arms outward and backward in a wide arc, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
4. Bring your arms back to the front, keeping them straight.
5. Repeat the motion smoothly and steadily.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core engaged to stay stable.
Avoid shrugging your shoulders—keep them relaxed.
Move slowly and with control.
Breathe steadily.

exercises.title: Dumbbell Row Bilateral
exercises.description: The Dumbbell Row Bilateral strengthens the back, shoulders, and arms while improving posture and upper-body stability. Performing both arms simultaneously enhances core stability, lumbopelvic control, and anti-rotation strength, supporting proper trunk alignment during pulling movements.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the back or hunching shoulders
Using momentum instead of controlled motion
Allowing elbows to flare outward
Not engaging the core for stability
exercises.rest_speech_text: Brace your core, hinge slightly, and pull with control.
steps: 1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
2. Hinge slightly at the hips while keeping your back flat.
3. Pull both dumbbells toward your waist simultaneously, elbows close to your body.
4. Pause briefly, then slowly lower the dumbbells to the starting position.
exercises.tips:
Keep your back flat and core tight
Pull dumbbells toward your torso, leading with your elbows
Move slowly, controlling both lifting and lowering phases
Maintain a neutral neck position

exercises.title: Side Leg Raise
exercises.description: Side Leg Raise is a lower-body exercise that targets the hip muscles, especially the gluteus medius. It helps improve hip strength, stability, and balance.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rolling your hips backward
Swinging the leg or moving too fast
Lifting the leg too high
Not keeping the core engaged
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Side Leg Raise. Stand tall, hold the chair, and lift your leg to the side.
steps: 1. Stand tall, holding the back of a chair for balance. Keep your body straight and core tight.
2. Slowly lift your right leg out to the side, keeping it straight.
3.Pause for a moment at the top.
4. Slowly lower your leg back down without touching the floor.
5. Repeat for desired reps then switch to other leg.
exercises.tips:
Keep your hips stacked—don’t lean backward. 
Don't lift too high 
Keep your toes pointing forward or slightly down.

exercises.title: Knee to Elbow
exercises.description: Knee to Elbow is a cardio exercise where you bring your knee toward the opposite elbow while in a plank position. It works your abs, obliques, and hip flexors, and helps improve balance and coordination.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rushing through reps
Not actually twisting the upper body
Pulling on your neck if hands are behind the he
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Knee to Elbow. Twist your body, lift those knees.
steps: 1. Lie on your back. Right knee should be bent and touches your right elbow.
2. Lift up your straight left leg.
3. Return your left leg to the starting position with control.
4. Perform desired repetitions on one side before alternating to the other side.
5. Repeat the exercise, alternating sides for the desired number of sets.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight the whole time.
Move with control, not speed.
Keep your chest lifted—don’t hunch over.

exercises.title: Overhead Clap
exercises.description: Overhead Clap is an exercise where you stand upright and raise your arms overhead to clap. It improves shoulder mobility, warms up the upper body muscles.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Moving too fast and losing control
Not fully extending arms overhead
Raising shoulders towards ears during the clap
Arching the lower back
exercises.rest_speech_text: Get ready for the overhead clap. Stand tall, raise your arms, and clap smoothly and controlled.
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Let your arms hang relaxed by your sides.
3. Raise your arms overhead until palms meet and clap.
4. Slowly lower your arms back down.
exercises.tips:
Keep your back straight and engage your core
Raise arms fully overhead to meet palms
Perform movements smoothly and with control
Relax your neck and avoid shrugging shoulders

exercises.title: Lying Face Down Straight Leg R
exercises.description: This exercise strengthens the glutes, hamstrings, and lower back by lifting your straight right leg while lying on your stomach. It helps improve hip stability and lower body strength.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching your lower back too much.
Letting hips rotate or lift off the floor.
Bending the leg during the lift.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Lying Face Down Straight Leg Raise. Lift your right leg straight up slowly.
steps: 1. Lie belly down on the mat with your hands under your head and your feet at shoulder level.
2. Put your feet straight up and begin to lift your leg up smoothly.
3. Return to the starting position and repeat.
exercises.tips:
Keep your hips pressed down on the floor.
Move slowly and with control.
Keep your head resting comfortably, looking down.

exercises.title: Lunge Hold
exercises.description: The Lunge Hold is an exercise that strengthens the quads, hamstrings, glutes, and calves, while also improving balance, stability, and core engagement.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting the front knee extend beyond the toes
Dropping the back knee too close to the ground
Leaning forward
Not engaging the core
Lifting the heel of the front foot off the ground
exercises.rest_speech_text: Lunge Hold. Step one foot forward, lower into a lunge, and hold. Keep your back knee off the floor.
steps: 1. Stand tall, feet hip-width apart.
2. Step one foot forward into a lunge position.
3. Lower your body until both knees are bent—back knee just above the floor.
4. Ensure your front knee is directly over your ankle.
5. Hold this position for 25-40 seconds, keeping your torso upright and core engaged.
6. Return to starting position and switch sides
exercises.tips:
Keep your torso upright
Front knee should stay directly above the ankle
Back knee should hover just above the ground
Distribute weight evenly between both legs
Keep your shoulders relaxed

exercises.title: Kettlebell Russian Twist
exercises.description: The Kettlebell Russian Twist is a core exercise that targets the obliques, rectus abdominis, and transverse abdominis while improving rotational strength and trunk stability. Holding a kettlebell increases resistance and engages core stability, anti-rotation control, and lumbopelvic control.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding or slouching the back
Using momentum instead of controlled rotation
Lifting the feet too high or letting them drop uncontrollably
Twisting only the arms without engaging the torso
exercises.rest_speech_text: Brace your core—twist controlled and strong.
steps: 1. Sit on the floor with knees bent and feet slightly off the ground.
2. Hold a kettlebell with both hands close to your chest.
3. Lean back slightly while keeping a straight spine.
4. Rotate the kettlebell to one side, then the other, moving through your torso.
5. Continue alternating sides for the desired number of reps.
exercises.tips:
Keep your chest lifted and spine neutral
Rotate through the torso, not just the arms
Move slowly and under control
Keep core engaged throughout the exercise

exercises.title: Sitting Arms Straight
exercises.description: This exercise activates the shoulders and helps improve posture and upper back mobility. You sit on the floor with legs extended and arms bent near to your body, then extend your arms by sliding them on your legs.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Leaning the torso too far forward
Rounding the spine
Moving too quickly
exercises.rest_speech_text: Sit up straight and relax your arms. Take a deep breath in through your nose and slowly exhale through your mouth.
steps: 1. Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight in front of you and your feet together. Bent your elbows and place arms near your body
2. Keeping your back straight, slowly slide your hands forward past your knees, aiming to stretch as far as you comfortably can
3. Slowly return to the starting position, and then repeat the stretch.
exercises.tips:
Keep your back straight
Focus on shoulder motion only
Breathe steadily

exercises.title: Windmill with KB
exercises.description: The Windmill with a kettlebell is a slow, controlled exercise that builds shoulder stability, core strength, hip mobility, and hamstring flexibility.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting the kettlebell drift forward or backward.
Rounding the back or locking the knees.
Bending forward instead of sideways.
Not looking at the kettlebell—this affects balance.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Up next: Windmill with Kettlebell. Keep your core tight, move slowly, and keep your eyes on the weight.
steps: 1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a kettlebell in your right hand.
2. Clean the kettlebell to your shoulder then press it overhead.
3. The kettlebell should be placed on the back of your forearm, which is vertical.
4. Push your hips towards the right side (towards the kettlebell).
5. Keep the kettlebell arm vertical the entire time and eyes on the weight
6. Go down as far as you comfortably can, then return to standing.
exercises.tips:
Keep the kettlebell stacked above your shoulder at all times.
Move slowly and with control.
Engage your core and glutes throughout.
Your back should stay straight, not rounded.

exercises.title: Squat Reach
exercises.description: Squat Reach is a full-body exercise that combines a lower-body squat with a dynamic upper-body reach. This helps strengthen the legs, glutes, and shoulders while improving mobility and coordination.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Separating the arms
Letting knees move past toes or cave inward
Arching the lower back
Not reaching arms fully overhead
Lifting the heels during the squat
exercises.rest_speech_text: Break. Squat down with your arms going down together—then reach overhead as you stand up.
steps: 1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and arms pressed together in front of you.
2. Lower into a squat by bending your knees and pushing your hips back—arms move down toward the floor.
3. As you rise from the squat, lift your arms overhead together in a smooth motion.
exercises.tips:
Keep your arms pressed together 
Maintain a flat back and strong core
Drive through your heels as you stand up
Make your arm movement smooth and controlled

exercises.title: Curling
exercises.description: Curling mimics a dynamic balance and coordination drill. You stand upright, extend one leg backward while simultaneously reaching the opposite arm behind you, and slightly bend the supporting leg. It improves core stability, glute activation, shoulder mobility, and coordination.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Leaning too far forward or arching the back
Not keeping the core engaged
Moving too fast without control
Twisting the torso excessively
Dropping the arms instead of extending
exercises.rest_speech_text: Stand tall, arms in front at chest level. Extend one leg and the opposite arm behind you. Slightly bend the front leg.
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, arms held at chest level, palms together.
2. Simultaneously extend your right leg behind you and reach your left arm backward.
3. Return to starting position with control.
4. Repeat on the other side, alternating sides with each rep
exercises.tips:
Keep your core braced throughout the movement
Maintain a neutral spine—don’t over-arch the back
Move smoothly and with control
Extend the back leg and arm fully to feel the stretch

exercises.title: Air Row
exercises.description: Air Row is a bodyweight exercise. Standing you pull your elbows back as if rowing, squeezing your shoulder blades. It strengthens the upper back, shoulders, and arms, and improves posture.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Shrugging shoulders
Letting elbows drop too low
Not squeezing the shoulder blades
exercises.rest_speech_text: For the next exercise Stand tall, pull your elbows back like rowing, squeeze your back, then return slowly.
steps: 1. Stand tall, extend arms forward at shoulder height
2. Pull elbows back, keeping them close to the body and squeeze shoulder blades together
3. Return arms to the front slowly
exercises.tips:
Keep your back straight
Pull elbows straight back, not out
Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades
Breathe out as you pull back

exercises.title: Floor to Overhead
exercises.description: Floor to Overhead is a powerful exercise that engages your entire body. It’s a great full-body movement for building strength, coordination, and endurance.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the back when lowering the dumbbell
Using only the arms to lift
Letting knees cave inward
Jerking the dumbbell overhead
exercises.rest_speech_text: Rest time. Stand tall with the dumbbell. Lower with control, then powerfully lift overhead. Stay strong and steady.
steps: 1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell with both hands in front of you.
2. Bend your knees and hips to lower the dumbbell toward the floor, keeping your back flat.
3. Engage your core and drive through your heels to stand up.
4. As you rise, lift the dumbbell overhead in a smooth, controlled motion.
5. Lower the dumbbell back to chest level, then return to the starting position.
exercises.tips:
Keep your back straight and chest open when lowering
Push through your heels to rise
Breathe out as you press the dumbbell overhead

exercises.title: Double Crunch
exercises.description: Double Crunch focuses on bringing the upper body toward the knees while the knees are kept bent and lifted off the floor. It effectively targets both the upper and lower abdominals, making it a powerful bodyweight exercise for core strength and stability.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Jerking the upper body or neck
Using impulse instead controlled movement
Arching the lower back off the floor
Holding your breath during the crunch
Letting the feet drop down or swing
exercises.rest_speech_text: Rest Time. Lie on your back, knees bent and lifted. Pull your chest toward your knees with control.
steps: 1.Lie on your back with knees bent, feet off the ground, and shins parallel to the floor.
2. Place your fingertips gently behind your head, elbows wide.
3. Lift your upper body toward your knees in a crunch motion while keeping the knees bent and raised.
4. Pause at the top and squeeze your abs.
5. Slowly return to the starting position with control.
exercises.tips:
Keep your knees bent and lifted
Engage your abs before you move
Pull your chest gently toward your knees—not your head with your hands
Keep your lower back gently pressed into the floor
Breathe out while crunching, breathe in while returning

exercises.title: Back Raise
exercises.description: Back Raise is a foundational bodyweight exercise that strengthens the lower back, glutes, and hamstrings. Performed by lifting the upper body while lying face-down, it helps support better posture, core stability, and spinal health.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Jerking the upper body instead of lifting with control
Lifting the chest too high, causing hyperextension
Holding breath during movement
Tensing the neck instead of keeping it neutral
Not engaging glutes and core
exercises.rest_speech_text: Break time. Lie on your stomach, hands by your sides. Gently lift your chest off the floor and squeeze your back muscles.
steps: 1. Lie flat on your stomach on a mat, arms at your sides or fingertips lightly touching your temples.
2. Keep legs extended and toes relaxed.
3. Slowly raise your chest a few inches off the floor.
4. Hold for 1–2 seconds at the top, then lower back down with control.
exercises.tips:
Move slowly and with control
Keep your neck in line with your spine
Engage your glutes and core before lifting
Lift only as far as comfortable—no need for high elevation
Breathe out as you lift, in as you lower

exercises.title: Dumbbell Overhead Press
exercises.description: The Dumbbell Overhead Press builds strength and stability in the shoulders, triceps, and upper chest. Using dumbbells promotes balanced muscle engagement and greater shoulder mobility. It also enhances core stability, lumbopelvic control, and anti-extension strength, supporting proper posture and preventing back arching during overhead lifts.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching the lower back
Flaring elbows too wide
Using momentum instead of control
Incomplete range of motion
exercises.rest_speech_text: Brace your core, stay tall, and press with control.
steps: 1. Sit or stand with dumbbells at shoulder height, palms facing forward.
2. Engage your core and keep your back straight.
3. Press the dumbbells upward until your arms are fully extended.
4. Pause briefly, then lower the dumbbells back to the starting position.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight and spine neutral
Press the dumbbells straight up, not forward
Lower slowly and under control
Avoid locking the elbows at the top

exercises.title: Dancer
exercises.description: The Dancer is a graceful balance and stretch pose that strengthens the legs, improves flexibility in the spine and hips, and opens the chest and shoulders.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Collapsing the chest forward
Arching the lower back excessively
Twisting the hips.                                           
Holding the breath
Pulling the lifted leg too forcefully
exercises.rest_speech_text: Stand tall, bend one knee and grab the ankle behind you, reach your other arm forward, and lift into a graceful balance
exercises.slow_down_phrases: Lower into the position gradually and mindfully, controlling your breathing.
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and arms by your sides.
2. Bend your right knee and reach your right hand back to grab the inside of your right ankle.
3. Raise your left arm forward and up for balance.
4. Hold the pose for 15–30 seconds, breathing steadily.
5. Slowly release and switch sides.
exercises.tips:
Keep your standing leg strong and straight
Focus on a fixed point in front of you
Breathe evenly and deeply throughout the pose

exercises.title: Dumbbell Step Up
exercises.description: The Dumbbell Step-Up is a unilateral lower-body exercise that strengthens the quads, glutes, and hamstrings while improving balance and coordination. Holding dumbbells also engages the core and develops lumbopelvic control and anti-extension strength, enhancing posture and reducing injury risk during dynamic movements.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Pushing off the back leg instead of the front
Letting the front knee go past the toes
Leaning forward or losing balance
Using momentum instead of controlled motion
exercises.rest_speech_text: Stand tall, core tight, and step up with control.
steps: 1. Stand facing a sturdy bench or platform, holding dumbbells at your sides.
2. Step one foot onto the platform, pressing through the heel to lift your body up.
3. Bring the trailing leg up to stand tall on the platform.
4. Step back down with control and repeat on the other leg.
5. Continue alternating or complete reps on one side, then switch.
exercises.tips:
Keep your chest upright and core engaged
Step onto the platform with control
Drive through the heel of the working leg
Maintain equal weight in both dumbbells

exercises.title: Double Lumbar Vertebrae Warm Up
exercises.description: This warm-up exercise focuses on gently mobilizing and stretching the lower lumbar spine and hip flexors while lying on your back. By raising each leg, holding the knee with your arms, then pulling both knees toward the chest, it enhances lumbar flexibility, releases lower back tension.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Lifting the head or straining the neck 
Pulling the knees too forcefully
Using impulse instead controlled movement
Not keeping the lower back relaxed 
Holding breath instead of steady breathing
exercises.rest_speech_text: Lie on your back, raise one knee, then the other, hold both and pull to chest, and lower legs slowly. Let’s start.
steps: 1. Lie flat on your back with legs extended and arms resting by your sides.
2. Slowly bend your right knee and raise it toward your stomach. Use your right arm to hold the knee gently.
3. Bend your left knee and raise it toward your stomach. Use your left arm to hold this knee.
4. Using both hands, gently pull both knees together toward your chest, feeling a stretch in your lower back and hips.
5. Hold this position briefly while maintaining steady breathing.
6. Slowly return to starting position
exercises.tips:
Keep your neck relaxed, head resting on the floor
Move slowly and with control
Keep lower back relaxed and avoid arching it off the floor
Breathe evenly
Use arms to gently guide the knees

exercises.title: Pulling KB to Chest
exercises.description: This exercise involves pulling a kettlebell toward your chest. It primarily targets your upper back, arms, and core. It builds strength in your biceps, shoulders, and trapezius muscles, and improves posture and pulling power.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the back during the squat
Pulling the KB with impulse, not muscles
Letting knees collapse inward
Not keeping heels grounded
exercises.rest_speech_text: Pulling kettlebell to the chestSquat down with control, stand up, then pull the kettlebell to your chest.
steps: 1.Stand tall holding a kettlebell with both hands.
2. Lower into a squat, keeping your chest up and heels down.
3. Stand back up to starting position.
4. Pull the kettlebell up to your chest with elbows close to your sides.
5. Lower the kettlebell and repeat the sequence.
exercises.tips:
Keep your chest lifted and back straight in the squat
Control the kettlebell pull — squeeze your back and biceps
Keep knees aligned with toes
Breathe out as you pull the KB to your chest

exercises.title: Neck Stretch
exercises.description: This is a neck mobility exercise done while sitting on a chair. By slowly tilting your head to the side, you stretch the neck muscles and release built-up tension. It helps improve posture.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Tilting the entire torso instead of just the head
Lifting the shoulders
Rushing through the stretch
Using hands to force the stretch
exercises.rest_speech_text: Sit tall, relax your shoulders, and gently tilt your head to one side. Feel the stretch along your neck.
steps: 1. Sit tall on a chair with your feet flat on the floor.
2. Let your arms hang naturally by your sides.
3. Slowly tilt your head to the right, aiming your ear toward your shoulder
4. Hold the stretch for a few seconds while breathing steadily.
5. Return to center and repeat on the other side.
exercises.tips:
Keep your back straight and shoulders relaxed
Move slowly and stay within a comfortable range
Breathe slowly and deeply during the stretch

exercises.title: Rowing Crunches
exercises.description: This exercise is performed lying on your back. As you crunch, you bring your knees toward your chest while lifting your shoulders and upper back off the ground. It's great for strengthening abdominal muscles, especially the lower abs.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Lifting the legs or head too high
Jerking instead of controlled motion
Straining the neck due to poor head position
Hands not placed under hips for proper back support
exercises.rest_speech_text: Lie on your back, place your hands under your hips. Get ready to pull your knees in and lift your shoulders up.
steps: 1. Lie on your back, place your hands together under your hips.
2. Extend your legs forward slightly off the ground.
3. Bend your knees and bring them toward your chest.
4. At the same time, lift your shoulders and head off the ground, engaging your abs.
5. Hold for a moment, then slowly return to the starting position.
exercises.tips:
Move slowly and with control
Keep your lower back pressed to the floor
Don’t strain your neck
Engage your core at the top of the crunch

exercises.title: KB Push Ups
exercises.description: The kettlebell Push-Ups is a push-up performed with your hands on kettlebell handles. This increases the range of motion and activates more stabilizer muscles, particularly in the shoulders, chest, and core.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting hips drop or lift too much
Pushing elbows out too wide
Lowering down too fast without control
Forgetting to tighten your core
exercises.rest_speech_text: Kettlebell push-ups. Hold the kettlebells, lower your chest slowly, then push back up strong
steps: 1. Place the kettlebell down on the mat. Come into a plank position with your hands holding onto the kettlebell.
2. Lower your chest to kettlebells slowly
3. Push back up to the start position.
4. Repeat the movement.
exercises.tips:
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels
Engage your core and glutes for stability
Lower slowly for control, push up with power
Keep wrists stacked over the kettlebells

exercises.title: Barbell Overhead Press
exercises.description: The Barbell Overhead Press is a compound upper-body exercise that primarily targets the shoulders, triceps, and upper chest. This exercise builds strength, stability, and power in the entire upper body, improving posture and athletic performance.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Leaning too far back, putting stress on the lower back
Not engaging the core, causing loss of stability
Pressing the bar forward
Flaring the elbows out too wide
Shrugging the shoulders or locking out the elbows
exercises.rest_speech_text: Brace your core, stand tall, and get ready to press with power.
steps: 1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell at shoulder level with an overhand grip
2. Engage your core and glutes to stabilize your spine.
3. Inhale deeply, then press the bar straight upward until your arms are fully extended overhead.
4. Move your head slightly back as the bar passes, then return it forward under the bar at the top.
5. Pause briefly at the top, keeping your body aligned and core tight.
6. Slowly lower the bar back to shoulder level under control.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight and glutes engaged to prevent back arching.

Press the bar in a straight line, slightly moving your head back as it passes
Keep wrists straight and stacked over elbows
Lower the bar slowly and under control
Exhale while pressing up, inhale as you lower the bar

exercises.title: Shaolin Rotation
exercises.description: Shaolin Rotation challenges your balance, coordination, and core strength by combining torso rotation with a raised bent leg. While standing on one leg, you rotate your upper body side to side with arms extended and lowered, enhancing stability and improving spinal mobility.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting the standing leg’s knee lock or collapse inward
Rotating hips instead of isolating torso rotation
Losing balance
Not keeping the raised leg bent
exercises.rest_speech_text: Shaolin Rotation. Stand tall, raise one leg bent, Rotate your torso side to side smoothly.
steps: 1. Stand tall and raise one leg, bending the knee
2. Extend your arms out to the sides and lower them by your sides
3. Engage your core and slowly rotate your torso to the left, keeping hips stable.
4. Return to center, then rotate to the right side.
5. Complete the desired number of repetitions, then switch legs.
exercises.tips:
Keep your standing leg engaged
Focus on rotating from the waist
Maintain steady breathing and controlled movement
Use a wall or chair for support if balance is difficult

exercises.title: Forward Bend
exercises.description: Forward Bend is a standing stretch where you bend at the hips and reach toward the floor. This exercise is excellent for improving hamstring flexibility, stretching the lower back, and calming the nervous system.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the back excessively
Locking the knees
Forcing the hands to touch the ground
Not engaging the core
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Forward Bend. Stand tall, then hinge at your hips and reach toward the floor. Keep your knees soft and relax your head.
steps: 1.Stand tall with your feet hip-width apart and arms relaxed at your sides.
2. Breathe out and hinge forward at your hips, reaching your hands down toward your feet.
3. Hold the position for a few breaths or as needed.
4. To rise, engage your core and slowly roll up to standing.
exercises.tips:
Slightly bend your knees
Let your head hang naturally
Focus on hinging from the hips
Breathe slowly and deeply

exercises.title: Butt Kickers
