exercises.description: Butt Kickers are a dynamic cardio move that involves jogging in place while kicking your heels up toward your glutes. This exercise targets the hamstrings, improves cardiovascular endurance, and increases lower body mobility.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Leaning too far forward or backward
Not kicking high enough
Landing heavily on the feet
Poor arm coordination or letting arms hang
Performing too quickly without control
exercises.rest_speech_text: Butt Kicker. Jog in place and kick your heels up toward your glutes. Keep your chest up.
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, arms behind you.
2. Begin jogging in place, lifting your right heel toward your right glute.
3. Lower your right foot and immediately lift your left heel toward your left glute.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight and posture upright
Land softly on the balls of your feet
Kick your heels up toward the glutes
Start slow to maintain control, then increase speed

exercises.title: Lying Leg Straightening
exercises.description: Lying Leg Straightening helpsto  improve leg strength and flexibility, especially in the quadriceps and hamstrings.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Holding the leg too tightly
Using the arm to pull the leg too forcefully
Letting the lower back arch off the floor
Holding breath
exercises.rest_speech_text: Prepare to lift your leg gently, supporting it under the knee with your arm, keeping your movement slow and controlled.
steps: 1. Lie on your back on a flat, comfortable surface and extend both legs straight.
2. Slowly lift one leg, bending the knee slightly and use the same side arm to gently hold your leg under the knee
3. Hold the position for 15–20 seconds to stretch and strengthen.
4. Slowly lower the leg back down, keeping control
5. Repeat with other leg
exercises.tips:
Use gentle, steady pressure with the arm
Keep your core engaged
Relax your shoulders and neck on the floor
Breathe deeply

exercises.title: Sitting Elbow Raises
exercises.description: The Sitting Elbow Raises exercise improves shoulder mobility, posture, and activates the upper back.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Lifting shoulders instead of elbows
Slouching
Fast movements
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a rest. Sit up straight, hands near your shoulders, gently lift your elbows up and lower them down.
steps: 1. Sit on a chair, keep your back straight
2. Bend your arms at the elbows, hands near shoulders
3. Slowly lift elbows upward
4. Lower them back down
exercises.tips:
Keep your back straight
Lift elbows smoothly and with control
Look forward

exercises.title: Leg Press 45° and horizontal
exercises.description: The Leg Press is a lower-body strength exercise that targets the quads, glutes, and hamstrings while allowing heavy loads with reduced spinal stress. The 45° variation emphasizes overall leg strength and glute activation, while the horizontal variation slightly shifts focus toward the quads.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting knees cave inward or bow outward
Locking the knees at full extension
Lifting the hips off the seat
Using momentum instead of controlled movement
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a deep breath, brace your core, reset your feet, and get ready to press strong and controlled.
steps: 1. Sit on the leg press machine with feet on the platform, knees slightly bent.
2. Engage your core and press the sled away without locking your knees.
3. Lower the platform slowly until knees form about a 90° angle.
4. Push through your heels to return to the starting position.
5. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
exercises.tips:
Keep feet flat and shoulder-width depending on target muscles
Maintain a slight bend in the knees at full extension
Engage the core and keep lower back pressed against the pad
Lower the sled slowly and push through your heels

exercises.title: Ab Crunch Machine
exercises.description: The Ab Crunch Machine isolates the abdominal muscles, primarily the rectus abdominis, to strengthen and tone the core. It improves trunk stability, posture, and functional core strength, supporting better performance in daily activities and other exercises.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Using momentum instead of controlled motion
Pulling with the arms instead of the abs
Arching the lower back during the crunch
Lifting too high, reducing core engagement
exercises.rest_speech_text: Relax your torso, brace your core, and get ready to crunch with control, feeling your abs contract.
steps: 1. Sit on the ab crunch machine and adjust the pad to fit your chest or shoulders.
2. Grip the handles (if available) and keep your feet flat.
3. Crunch forward, contracting your abs fully.
4. Slowly return to the starting position under control.
5. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
exercises.tips:
Keep your back against the pad and core engaged
Exhale as you crunch forward, inhale while returning
Move slowly and focus on contracting the abs
Avoid using the neck or shoulders to lift

exercises.title: Barbell Situp
exercises.description: The Barbell Sit-Up is an advanced core-strengthening exercise that targets the abs while engaging the shoulders, chest, and hip flexors for stability and control. This move enhances core power, posture, and total-body stability.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Using momentum
Lifting the barbell too far forward or arching the back
Letting the feet lift off the ground during the sit-up
Bending elbows instead of keeping arms locked
Holding the barbell too heavy, compromising form
exercises.rest_speech_text: Get ready for Barbell Sit-Ups. Keep your core strong, lift with control, and let’s power up that midsection!
steps: 1. Lie flat on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
2. Hold a barbell with both hands, arms fully extended above your chest.
3. Engage your core and slowly lift your torso off the ground into a full sit-up.
4. Keep the barbell directly over your shoulders throughout the motion.
5. At the top, pause briefly while maintaining control.
6. Slowly lower your torso back to the starting position.
exercises.tips:
Use a light barbell at first to perfect your form
Keep the bar directly above your shoulders 
Exhale while rising, and inhale as you lower down slowly
Engage your core from the start
Maintain a slow and steady rhythm

exercises.title: Standing Torso Twist
exercises.description: Standing Torso stretch and mobility exercise. While keeping both arms straight in front at shoulder height, you rotate your torso—turning the arm to the side. This adds a slight hamstring and postural engagement component.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Twisting hips instead of the upper body
Letting arms drop or bending them
Locking knees
Rushing the movement without core engagement
exercises.rest_speech_text: Rest time. Stand tall, arms straight forward. Twist left with your left arm, right with your right. Keep your knees straight
steps: 1. Stand upright with feet hip-width apart and knees straight and arms extended forward
2. Rotate your torso to the left, moving your left arm to the side and keeping your right arm forward.
3. Return to the center and switch side
exercises.tips:
Keep your arms parallel and extended fully
Move slowly and with control
Keep knees straight
Breathe out as you twist, breathe in as you return to center

exercises.title: Plow Pose
exercises.description: The Plow Pose is an excersice where the legs are lifted overhead until the toes touch the floor behind the head. This pose deeply stretches the spine, shoulders, and neck.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Putting too much pressure on the neck
Twisting the torso
Not lifting the hips high enough
Moving too fast
exercises.rest_speech_text: Rest time. Lie on your back, lift your legs, and gently bring them over your head. Let your toes touch the floor.
steps: 1. Lie on your back with arms at your sides, palms facing down.
2. Lift your legs up.
3. Continue lifting your hips off the floor and bring your legs over your head.
4. Support your lower back with your hands.
5. Hold the pose and breathe deeply.
exercises.tips:
Support your back with your hands for stability
Move slowly and breathe evenly
If toes don’t reach the floor keep them lifted
Avoid sudden or jerky movements

exercises.title: Dumbbell Laying Reverse Fly
exercises.description: The Dumbbell Lying Reverse Fly targets the rear deltoids, traps, and upper back. Performed while lying face down on a flat or incline bench, it helps improve shoulder stability, posture, and upper-back strength. It also promotes balanced shoulder development and reduces the risk of injury from dominant front delts.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Swinging the arms instead of controlled movement
Lifting the weights too high and shrugging shoulders
Using momentum rather than isolating rear delts
Letting elbows drop below shoulder line
exercises.rest_speech_text: Get ready for strong shoulders and a solid back!
steps: 1. Lie face down on a flat or incline bench, holding dumbbells under your shoulders.
2. Keep your arms slightly bent and palms facing each other.
3. Exhale and lift the weights out to the sides until your elbows reach shoulder height.
4. Pause briefly, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
5. Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back down with control.
exercises.tips:
Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout the motion
Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top
Move slowly and avoid using momentum
Keep your neck neutral and body stable on the bench

exercises.title: Crunch Reach
exercises.description: Crunch Reach is an abdominal exercise that targets the upper abs and obliques by combining a traditional crunch with an arm reach. This movement enhances core strength, improves flexibility.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Pulling on the neck with hands
Using impulse instead of controlled muscle engagement
Lifting the lower back off the floor
Holding breath during movement
Not reaching fully or collapsing forward
exercises.rest_speech_text: Lie on your back, crunch up and reach your arm towards your toes with control
steps: 1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
2. Slowly raise your upper body while running your hands between your knees.
3. Reach your arm fully towards the feet.
4. Slowly lower back down with control.
exercises.tips:
Keep your chin slightly tucked, avoiding neck strain
Use slow and controlled movements
Engage your core before lifting
Reach your arm fully towards your toes

exercises.title: Abductor Machine
exercises.description: The Abductor Machine isolates the outer thigh muscles (abductors), improving hip stability, lateral strength, and balance. Strengthening these muscles supports knee alignment, athletic performance, and overall lower-body function.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Using excessive weight and swinging the legs
Leaning forward or backward during the movement
Moving too quickly through the range of motion
Not fully controlling the legs at the end of the movement
exercises.rest_speech_text: Relax your legs, brace your core, and get ready to push outward with control.
steps: 1. Sit on the abductor machine with legs against the pads.
2. Adjust the starting position for comfort.
3. Slowly push your legs outward, focusing on the outer thighs and glutes.
4. Return to the starting position under control.
5. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
exercises.tips:
Adjust the machine for a comfortable starting position
Keep your back straight and core engaged
Move slowly and control the motion throughout
Exhale while pushing legs outward, inhale while returning

exercises.title: Y Raise
exercises.description: The Y Raise is a shoulder and upper back strengthening exercise. You lie on your stomach, raise your arms diagonally, and slowly lower them. It targets postural muscles and helps improve shoulder mobility and upper back strength.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Raising arms too high or shrugging shoulders
Arching the lower back
Letting arms bend too much
exercises.rest_speech_text: Break Time. Lie on your stomach. Lift your arms into a Y shape and squeeze your upper back.
steps: 1. Lie flat on your stomach
2. Stretch arms forward diagonally into Y shape
3. Raise your arms off the ground slowly and squeeze shoulder blades together
4. Lower arms with control
exercises.tips:
Keep your arms straight and lift slowly
Squeeze your shoulder blades together
Keep your neck in line with your spine

exercises.title: Barbell Upright Row
exercises.description: The Barbell Upright Row is a compound upper-body exercise that targets the shoulders and traps while also engaging the biceps and upper back. It’s an excellent movement for building shoulder width and upper-back definition.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Using too much weight and jerking the bar up
Pulling the bar too high, which can strain the shoulders
Letting the wrists bend excessively or flare outward
Hunching the back or rounding the shoulders
Neglecting to control the lowering phase
exercises.rest_speech_text: Stand tall, engage your shoulders, and get ready to pull straight up.
steps: 1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip in front of your thighs.
2. Keep your core tight and back straight.
3. Exhale and pull the barbell upward along your torso, leading with your elbows.
4. Raise the bar until your upper arms are parallel to the floor or slightly below shoulder level.
5. Pause briefly at the top, feeling the contraction in your shoulders and traps.
6. Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position under control.
exercises.tips:
Keep your back straight and core engaged
Use a moderate weight
Pull the bar close to your body in a straight line
Lead with your elbows, keeping them higher than your wrists
Avoid raising the bar above shoulder height

exercises.title: Hamstring Curl
exercises.description: The standing hamstring curl strengthens the hamstrings at the back of the thigh while gently stretching the quadriceps at the front.This exercise improves knee stability, leg strength, and flexibility.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Bending at the hips instead of isolating the knee
Allowing knees to separate
Swinging the foot or using momentum
Leaning the upper body forward or backward
Holding breath during the movement
exercises.rest_speech_text: Stand tall behind the chair, keep your knees together, and get ready to lift your foot slowly toward your glutes
steps: 1. Stand behind a straight-backed chair with feet slightly apart, hands lightly resting on the chair for support.
2. Shift your weight onto your right leg, keeping it slightly bent.
3. Slowly bend your left knee, bringing your heel toward your glutes, about 10–12 inches off the floor. Keep both knees together.
4. Hold briefly at the top of the movement.
5. Slowly lower the left foot back to the starting position.
6. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions and switch leg.
exercises.tips:
Keep your torso straight and core engaged
Move slowly and controlled
Keep knees close together throughout the exercise
Exhale while lifting the foot, inhale while lowering
Use a chair or wall for stability

exercises.title: Bent Over Back Fly
exercises.description: The Bent Over Back Fly targets the upper back, rear deltoids. Performed while hinging at the hips with a flat back, the arms move outward in a flying motion, engaging muscles responsible for posture and shoulder retraction.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the back or hunching shoulders
Swinging arms
Not hinging correctly at the hips
Raising arms too high or too low
Locking elbows
exercises.rest_speech_text: For Next exercise, bend forward from the hips, arms down. Raise arms out to the sides until shoulder level, then lower slowly
steps: 1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
2. Hinge at the hips to bring your torso forward, keeping your back straight and core tight.
3. With a slight bend in your elbows, lift both arms out to the sides until they are at shoulder height.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
5. Slowly lower your arms back to the starting position.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight and back flat
Maintain a slight bend in the elbows
Breathe out as you raise the arms, breatje in as you lower
Control the movement

exercises.title: Hand Walk outs
exercises.description: Hand Walk Outs are a full-body exercise that starts from a standing position and involves bending at the hips to walk your hands forward into a high plank position. This movement strengthens the core, shoulders, arms, and hamstrings.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting the hips sag in plank position
Not walking hands out far enough
Bending the knees too early when reaching down
Rushing the movement without control
Holding your breath during the walkout
exercises.rest_speech_text: Hand Walk Outs. Stand tall, bend forward to place your hands on the ground, walk out to a plank, hold briefly.
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
2. Bend at the hips and reach your hands toward the floor.
3. Place your hands on the floor and walk them forward one at a time until you're in a high plank position.
4. Hold the plank for 1–2 seconds, keeping your core tight and back flat.
5. Walk your hands back toward your feet and return to standing.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core engaged and glutes tight
Move slowly and with control
Focus on a straight spine as you walk out and in
Don’t let the lower back arch in plank

exercises.title: Straight Leg Raise
exercises.description: The Straight Leg Raise is an exercise that targets abdominal muscles while improving core strength, coordination, and control. Performed while lying on your back both legs raised up.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting the lower back lift off the floor
Bending the knees
Moving too quickly
Holding breath during the movement
exercises.rest_speech_text: Straight Leg Raise. Lie on your back, lift both legs, lower one leg down slowly, then switch. Keep your core strong
steps: 1. Lie on your back on the floor, facing upward. Place your arms under hips
2. Raise both legs straight up toward the ceiling.
3. Slowly lower one leg down toward the floor while keeping the other leg up.
4. Stop just before the lowered leg touches the floor.
5. Bring the lowered leg back up and lower the opposite leg.
exercises.tips:
Keep your hands under your hips for back support 
Breathe out while lowering each leg
Keep your movements slow and controlled
Press your lower back into the floor

exercises.title: Camel Stretch
exercises.description: The Camel Stretch is a kneeling backbend that opens up the chest, hip flexors, and spine. It enhances flexibility in the front body and improves postural alignment.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Leaning backward without lifting the chest
Compressing the lower back
Dropping the head too far back
Placing hands too far
Forcing the movement
exercises.rest_speech_text: Kneel down, place hands on your lower back, and gently arch your back while lifting the chest. Stretch your front body.
exercises.slow_down_phrases: Try to slow down and deepen the stretch to fully feel it.
steps: 1.Start by kneeling with a cushion placed between your feet for comfort.
2.Place your hands on your lower back, palms down, and fingers pointing downwards.
3. Gently arch backwards, lifting your chest upwards and puffing your chest forward.
4. Lower down onto your hands, one by one, towards your heels, feeling the stretch in the front of your body.
5. Lift your hips upwards, creating an arch with your body, and gently lean backwards, maintaining balance and controlling the movement.
6. Hold the pose for several deep breaths, allowing the stretch to unfold and relax.
7. To come out of the pose, gently release your hands from your heels, lift your torso, and return to a seated upright position.
exercises.tips:
Keep your hips aligned over your knees
Engage your glutes and core for support
Lift the chest upward before bending back
Only go as far as comfortable

exercises.title: Hip Thrust Maschine (Glute Drive)
exercises.description: The Hip Thrust Machine, also known as the Glute Drive, primarily strengthens the gluteus maximus while also engaging the hamstrings and core. It builds power for athletic movements, enhances hip stability, improves posture, and helps shape and firm the lower body.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Overarching the lower back at the top
Not achieving full hip extension
Letting the chin lift excessively or dropping the head
Using too much momentum instead of controlled glute activation
exercises.rest_speech_text: Catch your breath, keep your core tight, and get ready to lift those hips with power and control.
steps: 1. Sit on the Hip Thrust Machine with your upper back resting on the pad and feet flat on the platform, hip-width apart.
2. Secure the belt or pad over your hips.
3. Engage your core and press through your heels to lift your hips upward.
4. At the top, squeeze your glutes and form a straight line from shoulders to knees.
5. Lower your hips slowly until just above the starting position and repeat.
exercises.tips:
Keep your chin slightly tucked throughout the movement
Drive through your heels, not your toes
Pause and squeeze the glutes at the top for maximum activation
Maintain a straight line from shoulders to knees at full extension

exercises.title: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
exercises.description: The Dumbbell Lateral Raise isolates and strengthens the shoulder’s lateral deltoids, improving shoulder width, symmetry, and upper-body balance. It also enhances core stability and anti-extension control, helping maintain posture and preventing trunk sway during arm movement.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Lifting the weights too high or swinging them
Shrugging shoulders upward
Using momentum instead of muscle control
Bending elbows excessively
exercises.rest_speech_text: Stay tall, control your motion, and lift with precision.
steps: 1. Stand tall with dumbbells at your sides, palms facing inward.
2. Engage your core and maintain a slight bend in your elbows.
3. Raise both arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder level.
4. Pause briefly at the top, keeping tension in the shoulders.
5. Lower the dumbbells slowly back to the starting position.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight and chest lifted
Raise your arms slowly to shoulder height
Lead with the elbows, not the wrists
Control the descent—don’t drop the weights

exercises.title: Dumbbell Arnold Press
exercises.description: The Dumbbell Arnold Press is a dynamic shoulder exercise. It combines a rotational motion with a standard overhead press, targeting all three heads of the deltoids—front, side, and rear—while also engaging the triceps and upper back. This movement improves shoulder strength, mobility, and muscle symmetry.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching the lower back excessively
Moving the elbows too far forward or flaring them outward
Using momentum instead of controlled rotation
Not rotating the wrists smoothly
Lowering the dumbbells too quickly
exercises.rest_speech_text: Engage your core, control the rotation, and press strong through your shoulders.
steps: 1. Sit or stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing you and elbows bent in front of your chest.
2. Engage your core and keep your chest lifted.
3. As you begin to press the weights upward, rotate your palms outward until they face forward at the top of the movement.
4. Extend your arms fully overhead without locking the elbows.
5. Pause briefly at the top, feeling the shoulder contraction.
6. Slowly reverse the motion—rotate your wrists back inward as you lower the dumbbells to the starting position.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core braced and spine neutral
Perform the movement slowly and with full control
Rotate your wrists naturally to avoid shoulder strain
Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower
Use moderate weight to maintain proper form

exercises.title: Side Oblique Stretch
exercises.description: The obliques are the muscles that allow us to rotate our torso and bend sideways. Stretching them regularly can improve posture and can help maintain a correct spinal alignment. Strong obliques add extra support to the back muscles and prevent back pain and injury.
exercises.common_mistakes: Move your hips. Incorrect and irregular breathing. Poor amlitude.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a break. The next exercise is side bends to stretch your obliques, lower back and thighs
steps: 1. Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart. Place your right hand on your hip and raise the left arm.
2. Incline your torso to the right until you feel a stretch in the obliques.
3. Hold the stretch for a few seconds and then repeat on the other side.
exercises.tips: Keep your body relaxed and your weight evenly distributed between both legs.

exercises.title: Band Glute Kickback
exercises.description: The Band Glute Kickback is an effective lower-body strengthening exercise that targets the gluteal muscles, particularly the gluteus maximus. Using a resistance band provides constant tension, helping tone and activate the glutes while improving hip stability and balance. This move is great for enhancing lower-body strength and improving posture
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching the lower back
Swinging the leg too high or too fast
Not keeping the band tight during the movement
Shifting body weight unevenly to one side
exercises.rest_speech_text: Catch your breath and get ready — Band Glute Kickbacks are next! Focus on control and glute squeeze with every lift.
steps: 1. Place a resistance band around your thighs or ankles.
2. Start on all fours with your hands under your shoulders and knees under your hips.
3. Engage your core and keep your back flat.
4. Slowly extend one leg back and upward, squeezing your glutes.
5. Pause briefly, then return to the starting position without touching the floor.
6. Repeat for the set number of reps, then switch legs.
exercises.tips:
Focus on slow, controlled movements
Keep your core tight to protect your lower back
Maintain balance

exercises.title: Barbell Pause Squat
exercises.description: The Barbell Pause Squat is a squat variation designed to increase strength, control, and stability throughout the full range of motion. This exercise improves balance, enhances explosiveness, and strengthens weak points in your squat.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Losing tension at the bottom during the pause
Rounding the lower back when holding the bottom position
Rising too quickly and breaking form
Holding the pause too short or inconsistent durations
Allowing knees to cave inward
exercises.rest_speech_text: Breathe deep, stay tight, and get ready to hold strong at the bottom
steps: 1. Position the barbell across your upper traps (high-bar position) and stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Inhale deeply, brace your core, and begin to lower into a squat by bending your hips and knees.
3. Descend until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
4. Pause at the bottom for 2–3 seconds, keeping your body tight and chest up.
5. Push through your heels and extend your hips and knees to return to standing.
6. Exhale at the top and reset before the next rep.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core braced and chest up throughout the entire movement
Maintain tension even during the pause—don’t relax at the bottom
Control your descent and keep heels grounded
Count the pause consistently
Exhale explosively as you rise

exercises.title: 180 Stretch
exercises.description: 180 Stretch involves extending both arms and moving them sideways in coordination with your upper body. This dynamic stretch improves thoracic spine mobility, shoulder flexibility, and helps release tension in the upper back and chest.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Moving arms without rotating the torso
Over-twisting or forcing the rotation
Raising shoulders toward the ears
Bending elbows during arm movement
Holding breath
exercises.rest_speech_text: Rest. Extend both arms and slowly rotate your upper body to the right with your right arm, then to the left with your left arm
steps: 1. Sit upright on a chair with feet flat on the floor and arms extended forward at shoulder height.
2. Slowly rotate your upper body and extend your right arm out to the right side, keeping the arm straight.
3. Return to the center position with both arms extended forward.
4. Slowly rotate your upper body and extend your left arm out to the left side, keeping the arm straight.
5. Return to the center.
exercises.tips:
Keep arms fully extended during the movement
Rotate the torso gently and within comfortable range
Maintain a tall seated posture with feet flat on the floor
Breathe deeply and breathe during rotation

Move slowly and smoothly to avoid strain

exercises.title: High Plank
exercises.description: The High Plank is an exercise that strengthens the core, shoulders, arms, glutes, and legs. It improves posture, building endurance, and engaging multiple muscle groups.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Dropping or lifting the hips too much
Letting the head overextend the neck
Shrugging the shoulders toward the ears
Bending the elbows
Not engaging the core and glutes
exercises.rest_speech_text: Get ready for High Plank. Place your hands under your shoulders, step back with both feet, keep your body straight and your core tight.
steps: 1. Start on all fours with your hands directly under your shoulders.
2. Step both feet back, one at a time, to form a straight line from head to heels.
3. Keep your arms extended, shoulders stacked above your wrists.
4. Hold this position for the desired time, breathing steadily.
5. Gently lower your knees and return to starting position
exercises.tips:
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels
Engage your core, glutes, and thighs
Spread your fingers 
Look down to avoid neck strain

exercises.title: Chair Perched Pigeon
exercises.description: This stretch is performed while sitting on a chair with one leg bent and placed over the other leg. Leaning forward with the upper body and arms helps deepen the stretch in the hip, glutes, and lower back. It improves hip mobility, reduces tension in the gluteal muscles.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding or slouching the back too much
Forcing the bent leg down
Holding breath
Not leaning forward enough to feel the stretch
exercises.rest_speech_text: Cross one leg over the other, lean your upper body forward, keep your back straight, and breathe deeply to feel the stretch.
steps: 1. Sit on a chair with feet flat on the floor.
2. Bend your right leg and place your right ankle over your left thigh, just above the knee.
3. Slowly lean your upper body forward, using your arms for balance if needed.
4. Hold for 20-30 seconds while breathing deeply.
5. Slowly sit back up.
exercises.tips:
Keep your back as straight as possible 
Move slowly and stop if you feel discomfort or pain
Breathe deeply to relax muscles during the stretch
Use your arms for support as you lean forward

exercises.title: Leg Lift Plank
exercises.description: Leg Lift Plank is acore-strengthening exercise that combines static stability from the plank with dynamic glute and hamstring activation. By lifting one leg at a time you challenge your core, lower back, and posterior chain.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Dropping the hips
Letting the shoulders collapse
Moving the torso when lifting the leg
Lifting the leg too high or too fast
Holding breath
exercises.rest_speech_text: Break Time. Go to the plank postion. Raise one leg and return back, then switch leg.
steps: 1. Start in an elbow plank: forearms on the floor, elbows under shoulders, legs extended, toes on the ground.
2. Lift your right leg a few inches off the floor, keeping it straight and stable.
3. Pause briefly, then lower it back down with control.
4. Repeat the movement with your left leg.
exercises.tips:
Keep your elbows directly under shoulders
Maintain a straight line from head to heels
Engage your core and glutes
Lift the leg only to hip height
Focus on controlled breathing

exercises.title: Cable Rope Overhead Tricep Extension
exercises.description: The Cable Rope Overhead Tricep Extension is an isolation exercise targeting the triceps, especially the long head. Performing this exercise overhead maximizes the stretch in the triceps and improves strength and definition.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting elbows flare out 
Using momentum instead of controlled movement
Arching the lower back excessively
Not fully extending the elbows at the top
Leaning forward or moving the torso during the extension
exercises.rest_speech_text: Stand tall, elbows in, and get ready to extend with control.
steps: 1. Attach a rope handle to a high pulley on a cable machine.
2. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, facing away from the machine, holding the rope with both hands.
3. Raise the rope overhead so your elbows are pointing forward and close to your head.
4. Engage your core and keep your torso upright.
5. Exhale and extend your elbows to push the rope upward and forward until your arms are fully straight.
6. Pause briefly at the top, feeling the triceps contraction.
7. Inhale and slowly return the rope to the starting position behind your head with control.
exercises.tips:
Keep your elbows tucked and stationary.
Maintain a tight core to prevent lower back strain
Focus on the triceps contraction at the top of the movement
Move slowly on both the downward and upward phases
Adjust the cable weight to allow full control

exercises.title: Knee Elbow Crunch Standing
exercises.description: The Knee Elbow Crunch Standing targets the core while also challenging shoulder stability and balance. The exercise strengthens the abs, obliques, and quads, and increases coordination.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Bending forward instead of twisting
Performing reps too fast
Letting arms drop below chest level
Lifting the knee too low or not twisting enough
exercises.rest_speech_text: Knee Elbow Crunch. Stand tall, arms straight in front, palms together. Bring your knee up and twist your torso to meet it.
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart, extend both arms straight forward at chest level, pressing your palms together.
2. Lift your right knee and rotate your torso to the left, bringing your hands toward the raised knee.
3. Return to starting position and repeat with other leg.
exercises.tips:
Keep arms fully extended and palms pressed together
Tighten your core before each twist
Focus on rotating the torso
Maintain good posture
Perform the movement slowly and controlled

exercises.title: Beginners Mountain Climbers
exercises.description: This exercise helps strengthen your core, shoulders, and legs while gently raising your heart rate. It’s perfect for building coordination and endurance.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting hips sag or rise too high
Not engaging the core
Bouncing the body or rushing the movement
Not aligning wrists under shoulders
exercises.rest_speech_text: time to Break. Get into plank, slowly bring one knee forward, then switch legs one by one. Keep your core tigh
steps: 1. Start in a plank position, arms straight, hands under shoulders, keep your body in a straight line from head to heels.
2. Slowly bring your right knee forward toward your chest.
3. Return it to starting position.
4. Now bring your left knee forward, then return.
exercises.tips:
Keep your back flat and core tight
Move at your own pace
Keep your shoulders over your wrists
Breathe with each step

exercises.title: Lying Face Down Bent Leg Raise
exercises.description: This exercise targets the glutes and hamstrings by lifting the bent leg while lying face down. It helps strengthen your hips and improve lower body stability.
exercises.common_mistakes: Too low or high leg elevations. Swinging the leg from side to side.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Lying Face Down Bent Leg Raise. Bend your knee and lift your leg slowly.
steps: 1. Lie flat on your stomach with legs straight behind you
2. Bend one knee to about 90 degrees, keeping your thigh on the floor.
3. Slowly lift your bent leg toward the ceiling by squeezing your glutes.
4. Hold briefly at the top, then lower your leg back down gently
5. Do all reps on one leg, then switch to the other leg.
exercises.tips:
Keep your hips pressed into the floor.
Move slowly and control the movement.
Keep your head relaxed, looking down.

exercises.title: Half Squat Leg Extension
exercises.description: Half Squat Leg Extension involves extending the leg laterally to the side instead of straight forward. It targets the quadriceps and glutes, while also emphasizing the hip abductors.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Allowing the knee of the supporting leg to collapse inward
Tilting the torso instead of keeping it upright
Swinging the extended leg with impulse
Not maintaining tension in the core for stability
Not controlling the descent during the squat
exercises.rest_speech_text: Half Squat Leg Extension. Lower into a half squat, then slowly extend your leg out to the side.
steps: 1. Stand with feet hip-width apart.
2. Lower into a half squat by bending your knees, keep your back straight and chest lifted.
3. From this position, extend one leg slowly out to the side, keeping it straight and toes pointing forward or slightly outward.
4. Hold briefly, then return the leg back to the half squat position.
5. Complete the desired number of reps on one side, then switch legs.
exercises.tips:
Keep your chest lifted and core engaged
Push the supporting knee slightly outward
Extend your leg slowly and with control to the side
Keep your hips level and avoid leaning to one side

exercises.title: Plank Arm Raises
exercises.description: Plank Arm Raises are an exercise performed from a high plank position. The movement involves lifting one arm straight. This exercise primarily targets your core, shoulders, and back.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Shifting weight excessively to one side.
Dropping or lifting the hips.
Bending the arm.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Plank Arm Raises. In a high plank, raise one arm straight ahead, then switch. Keep your body stable and controlled.
steps: 1. Begin in a high plank position with your hands under your shoulders, feet slightly wider than hips.
2. Engage your core and keep your body in a straight line.
3. Lift your right arm straight ahead, keeping it in line with your shoulder.
4. Hold briefly, then lower it back down.
5. Repeat with your left arm.
exercises.tips:
Keep your feet wider apart.
Engage your glutes and core.
Lift your arm slowly and with control.
Keep your neck in a neutral position.

exercises.title: Elbow up
exercises.description: This exercise transitions between a forearm plank and a full plank by pushing up with one arm at a time, then lowering back down. It builds upper body strength, core stability, and enhances endurance.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Twisting the hips or torso too much
Dropping the hips or letting them rise
Moving too fast and losing form
Not alternating arms evenly
exercises.rest_speech_text: Get ready for the exercise. Start in elbow plank. Push up to full plank one arm at a time, then lower back down slowly.
steps: 1. Begin in a forearm plank—elbows under shoulders, body in a straight line.
2. Press up with one hand, straightening the elbow, then the other, to reach a full plank.
3. Pause briefly in the high plank.
4. Lower back down one elbow at a time, returning to forearm plank.
exercises.tips:
Keep hips and shoulders as square to the floor as possible
Engage your core and glutes to stay stable
Move slowly and with purpose
Breathe out when pushing up, in when lowering

exercises.title: Gluteal Muscle Stretch
exercises.description: Gluteal Muscle Stretch is performed lying on your back with legs extended. You bend one knee and lift it to your chest. This stretch targets the gluteal muscles and lower back, helping to relieve tension, improve hip flexibility.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Pulling too forcefully
Allowing the opposite leg or lower back to lift off the floor
Holding the breath
Bending the extended leg
Twisting the hips instead of keeping them flat on the floor
exercises.rest_speech_text: Rest. lie on your back, keep one leg straight on the floor, bend the other knee and gently pull it toward your chest with your arms.
steps: 1. Lie flat on your back with both legs extended straight forward.
2. Bend your right knee and bring it toward your chest.
3. Use both hands to gently grasp your knee or shin and pull it closer to your chest.
4. Hold the stretch for 20–30 seconds while breathing slowly and deeply.
5. Release gently and switch to the other leg.
exercises.tips:
Keep your extended leg flat and relaxed on the floor
Pull the bent knee gently toward your chest
Keep your lower back and hips pressed into the floor
Breathe deeply and hold the stretch

exercises.title: Dumbbell Chest Fly (Flat & Incline)
exercises.description: The Dumbbell Chest Fly isolates the chest muscles, stretching and contracting the pectorals through a wide range of motion. It enhances chest shape, shoulder stability, and control while supporting pressing strength. Performing it on an incline emphasizes the upper chest, while the flat version targets the middle chest.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Dropping arms too low and overstretching shoulders
Bending elbows excessively
Using momentum instead of controlled movement
Failing to squeeze the chest at the top
exercises.rest_speech_text: Control the stretch, squeeze at the top.
steps: 1. Lie on a flat or incline bench holding dumbbells above your chest, palms facing each other.
2. With a slight bend in elbows, slowly lower the dumbbells in a wide arc until your chest feels stretched.
3. Bring the dumbbells back together above your chest, squeezing the pectoral muscles.
4. Repeat with smooth, controlled motion.
exercises.tips:
Keep a slight bend in your elbows
Move the dumbbells in a wide arc, not straight up and down
Focus on squeezing your chest at the top of the motion
Avoid letting shoulders lift off the bench

exercises.title: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.description: The Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift strengthens the hamstrings, glutes, and lower back while improving hip mobility and posterior chain stability. It also develops core stability, lumbopelvic control, and anti-flexion strength, promoting better posture and reducing injury risk in dynamic movements.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the back or shoulders
Bending the knees too much
Lowering the weights too far
Using the back instead of hinging at the hips
exercises.rest_speech_text: Brace your core, hinge with control, and feel the stretch in your hamstrings.
steps: 1. Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs.
2. Engage your core and keep a slight bend in your knees.
3. Hinge at the hips, lowering the dumbbells toward mid-shin level while keeping your back flat.
4. Feel the stretch in your hamstrings, then drive your hips forward to return upright.
5. Squeeze your glutes at the top and repeat.
exercises.tips:
Keep your spine neutral and core engaged
Push your hips back, not your knees forward
Maintain a slight knee bend throughout
Move slowly and under control

exercises.title: Boat Pose
exercises.description: Boat Pose is a classic core-strengthening yoga posture that challenges balance, stability, and control. It targets the abdominal muscles, hip flexors, and spine, helping to build core strength and improve posture.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the back or collapsing the chest
Holding the breath
Letting the legs drop too low or too high
Tension in the neck or shoulders
exercises.rest_speech_text: Time to activate your core — find your balance and hold that boat strong!
steps: 1. Sit on the floor with legs extended in front of you.
2. Place your hands behind your thighs, lean back slightly, and lift your feet off the floor.
3. Balance on your sit bones, keeping your back straight and chest lifted
4. Extend your arms forward parallel to the floor, palms facing each other.
5. If you can, straighten your legs into a “V” shape with your torso.
6. Hold the position for 20–30 seconds while breathing steadily.
7. Lower your legs gently to release.
exercises.tips:
Engage your core throughout the pose
Keep your chest lifted and spine straight
Start with bent knees if the full pose is too challenging

exercises.title: Twisted Mountain Climber
exercises.description: Twisted Mountain Climbers are a cardio and core exercise where you get into a high plank position and drive your knees across your body toward the opposite elbow. It’s like regular mountain climbers, but with a twist. This move targets your abs, especially the obliques, while giving you a full-body burn.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Hips too high
Bouncing or losing control
Not twisting the core — just lifting knees straight
Holding your breath
Not keeping wrists under shoulders
exercises.rest_speech_text: Coming up: twisted mountain climbers. Get into plank position and drive your knees across your body toward the opposite elbow.
steps: 1. Start in a high plank (hands under shoulders, body straight)
2. Bring your right knee across toward your left elbow
3. Return to plank position
4. Bring your left knee toward your right elbow
5. Continue alternating knees at a steady or fast pace
6. Keep your hips level and core tight throughout
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight and back flat
Drive your knee across your body with control
Land lightly on your toes
Breathe steadily
Go at a pace you can keep with good form

exercises.title: Squat Into Star Pose
exercises.description: Squat Into Star Pose is a dynamic movement that combines the strength-building benefits of a squat with an explosive extension into a wide "star" position. This movement helps improve leg strength, balance, coordination, and body control.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Not fully extending arms and legs into the star shape
Letting knees cave inward during the squat
Rising too quickly
Leaning forward excessively
exercises.rest_speech_text: Break Time. Squat down with control, then rise up and stretch out into a star position.”
steps: 1. Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart, arms at your sides.
2. Lower into a squat by bending your knees and pushing hips back.
3. As you rise, extend both arms and legs outward diagonally into a wide star shape.
4. Hold the star position briefly with full body tension.
5. Return to the starting position.
exercises.tips:
Squat with control, keeping your chest up
At the top, stretch arms and legs fully
Focus on balance when transitioning between positions
Keep your core engaged

exercises.title: Walking Squats
exercises.description: Walking Squats combine lateral movement with squatting, targeting the legs and glutes from a different angle. This exercise strengthens the quads, glutes, hamstrings, and calves, while also improving hip mobility, balance, and coordination.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting knees cave inward.                            Leaning torso too far forward or rounding back
Taking uneven or overly large steps
Not keeping weight centered over feet
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Walking Squats. Squat down, step to the side, keep your chest up and knees aligned
steps: 1. Stand with feet hip-width apart.
2. Take a step to the side with one leg.
3. Lower into a squat position, pushing hips back and bending knees.
4. Bring your left foot to meet the right foot, staying low in squat.
5. Continue side-to-side walking in squat position for desired reps or time.
exercises.tips:
Keep knees aligned with toes during squats
Maintain an upright chest and engaged core
Take controlled, moderate lateral steps
Keep feet flat and distribute weight evenly

exercises.title: Fat Butterfly
exercises.description: This exercise targets the inner thighs and helps improve flexibility and strength in the hip and groin area..
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding or slouching the back.
Forcing knees down causing pain.
Holding breath during the stretch.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Fat Butterfly. Sit, bring feet together, and gently press knees down or flap them.
steps: 1. Sit on the chair with your back straight
2. Bend your elbows and start stretching your arms sideways, keeping your back straight.
exercises.tips:
Keep your back straight and chest lifted.
Don’t force your knees down; go only as far as comfortable.
Breathe deeply to relax your muscles.
Use your elbows to gently press knees down if comfortable.

exercises.title: Swallow Pose with Ball
exercises.description: This exercise improves balance, strengthens the lower back, glutes, and hamstrings, and enhances core stability. From a standing position, hold a small exercise ball and extend one leg backward while bending your torso forward.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching the lower back excessively
Letting the torso drop unevenly
Losing balance
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a break. Stand tall, extend one leg back, bend forward with a straight spine, hold the ball steady.
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, holding a small ball in front of you
2. Engage your core and shift weight to one leg.
3. Extend the opposite leg straight back behind you.
4. Slowly bend your torso forward at the hips, keeping your back straight
5. Hold the position briefly, then return to standing and repeat with other leg
exercises.tips:
Keep your spine neutral and long
Engage your core
Keep hips level and avoid twisting
Use the ball to help maintain arm position and control

exercises.title: Dumbbell Forward Lunge
exercises.description: The Dumbbell Forward Lunge is a unilateral lower-body exercise that strengthens the quads, glutes, and hamstrings while improving balance, coordination, and hip mobility. It also enhances core stability, lumbopelvic control, and anti-extension strength, supporting better posture and reducing injury risk during athletic movements.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting the front knee go past the toes
Leaning too far forward
Pushing off with the back leg instead of the front
Losing balance or rushing the movement
exercises.rest_speech_text: Stand tall, stay balanced, and get ready to lunge strong.
steps: 1. Stand upright holding dumbbells at your sides.
2. Step forward with one leg and lower until both knees form 90-degree angles.
3. Keep your chest lifted and your front knee aligned with your ankle.
4. Push through your front heel to return to the starting position.
exercises.tips:
Keep your chest up and core engaged
Step forward with control
Push through the front heel to return
Maintain equal weight in both dumbbells

exercises.title: Squat Hold
exercises.description: The Squat Hold is an exercise that primarily targets the quads, glutes, hamstrings, and core, while also engaging the shoulders and upper back due to the arm position.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Dropping the arms or locking the elbows
Letting knees move too far forward past toes
Arching or rounding the lower back
Lifting heels off the floor
Tensing the shoulders up toward the ears
exercises.rest_speech_text: Squat Hold. Feet shoulder-width apart, lower into a squat, and extend your arms forward—palms facing out, elbows slightly bent.
steps: 1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly pointed outward.
2. Extend both arms forward at shoulder height, elbows slightly bent, palms facing forward.
3. Slowly lower your body into a squat position, keeping your thighs parallel to the floor or as low as comfortable.
4. Hold this position for 30 seconds, maintaining steady breathing and strong posture.
5. Slowly stand up
exercises.tips:
Keep your arms lifted at shoulder level 
Slightly bend the elbows
Press your heels into the floor
Engage your core and keep the back flat
Relax the neck and shoulders

exercises.title: Squat with KB
exercises.description: This exercise strengthens your legs, glutes, and core muscles. You hold a kettlebell close to your chest and perform a squat Adding the kettlebell increases resistance, helping improve strength, balance, and stability
exercises.common_mistakes:
Knees bending too far forward past your toes
Leaning your upper body forward or rounding your back
exercises.rest_speech_text: Kettlebell squat. Hold the kettlebell close, squat down low, then stand back up
steps: 1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding the kettlebell close to your chest.
2. Push hips back and bend your knees to lower into a squat.
3. Lower until your thighs are parallel to the floor or as comfortable.
4. Push through your heels to stand back up.
exercises.tips:
Keep your back straight and chest lifted
Push your hips back as if sitting into a chair
Keep your weight on your heels, not your toes

exercises.title: Side Plank Knee Lift
exercises.description: The Side Plank Knee Lift involves bringing the top elbow and knee toward each other during the movement. It creates a powerful crunching motion that deeply activates the obliques, engages the full core, and challenges balance and coordination.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting hips sag or twist
Failing to engage core fully before moving
Jerky, rushed motion 
Not aligning elbow and knee properly
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next up: Side Plank with Knee to Elbow. Keep your hips high, bring your top elbow down to meet your knee with control.
steps: 1. Start in a side plank: forearm or palm on the floor, legs stacked, body straight.
2. Extend your top arm fully overhead, palm facing forward.
3. Engage your core and lift the top leg, bending the knee toward your chest.
4. Simultaneously bend your top elbow and bring it down toward the knee.
5. Try to touch elbow and knee together at the peak of the movement.
6. Slowly return both arm and leg to the starting position with control.
7. Repeat for reps, then switch sides.
exercises.tips:
Focus on maintaining a straight line from head to foot
Breathe out  as you bring the elbow to the knee
Keep the top arm extended overhead until initiating the crunch
Perform the motion slowly

exercises.title: Band Pull Apart
exercises.description: The Band Pull Apart is a simple yet highly effective exercise for strengthening the rear delts, upper back, and scapular stabilizing muscles. It helps improve posture, relieve tension in the neck and shoulders, and enhance shoulder girdle stability.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Bending the elbows
Raising the shoulders toward the ears
Performing the movement too quickly without control
Using a band that is too light
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a deep breath… get your shoulders back… feel your back engage… and get ready to pull.
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a resistance band in both hands at chest height.
2. Keep arms straight, palms facing down.
3. Slowly pull the band apart to the sides, squeezing the shoulder blades together.
4. Pause when arms are fully extended and you feel the contraction in the back muscles.
5. Slowly return to the starting position, maintaining control of the band.
exercises.tips:
Keep your arms straight throughout the movement
Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together
Avoid shrugging your shoulders
Breathe steadily

exercises.title: Band Pushup
exercises.description: The Band Push-Up is a variation of the traditional push-up that adds resistance using a band, increasing the load on the chest, shoulders, and triceps. It helps build upper body strength, improve core stability, and enhance muscle activation compared to standard push-ups.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Sagging hips or arching the lower back
Flared elbows
Not maintaining tension on the band
Going too fast and losing control of form
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a deep breath, engage your core, and get ready to push.
steps: 1. Wrap a resistance band across your upper back, holding the ends under your palms.
2. Get into a high plank position with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width.
3. Keep your body straight, core tight, and glutes engaged.
4. Lower your chest toward the floor, keeping elbows at about 45 degrees.
5. Push back up explosively, maintaining band tension.
6. Repeat for the recommended number of reps.
exercises.tips:
Wrap the resistance band across your upper back and hold the ends under your hands
Keep your body in a straight line 
Engage your core and glutes to prevent sagging
Lower slowly and push explosively while maintaining band tension

exercises.title: Jumping Jack
exercises.description: Jumping Jack is a dynamic full-body cardio exercise that quickly elevates your heart rate, activates major muscle groups, and enhances coordination. It’s perfect for warming up, energizing your body, or adding intensity to any workout routine—anytime, anywhere.
exercises.common_mistakes: Landing too hard. Slouching. Not stretching arms. Bending knees too much. Not breathing steady.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Start standing tall, feet together, arms by your sides. Get ready to jump, spread out wide, then return.
steps: 1. Stand upright with your feet together and arms at your sides.
2. Jump while spreading your legs shoulder-width or wider and raising your arms overhead.
3. Your hands should meet above your head as your feet land on the floor.
4. Jump your feet back together and lower your arms to the starting position.
5. Breathe rhythmically—inhale as you open, exhale as you return.
exercises.tips: Pay attention to soft landings and smooth, controlled movements. Maintain steady, rhythmic breathing during the exercise. If you're just starting out, begin with fewer repetitions and slowly increase as you build endurance.

exercises.title: Triceps  Extension
exercises.description: The seated triceps extension strengthens the triceps at the back of the upper arms. By sitting on a chair, you minimize body momentum, making the exercise more controlled and focused on isolating the triceps. This move helps tone the arms, improves pushing strength.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching the lower back
Moving the elbows outward
Using too heavy a dumbbell, causing swinging
Not fully extending the arms at the top
Rushing the movement instead
exercises.rest_speech_text: Sit tall, hold the dumbbell overhead, and get ready to work the back of your arms with control.
steps: 1. Sit tall on a chair with feet firmly on the ground.
2. Hold one dumbbell with both hands, gripping it by the handle or cupping the top end.
3. Lift the dumbbell overhead until arms are fully extended.
4. Keeping elbows close to your head, slowly bend your arms to lower the dumbbell behind your head.
5. Pause briefly when elbows are at about 90°.
6. Press the dumbbell back up to the starting position, fully extending the arms.
exercises.tips:
Sit tall with feet flat on the floor and core engaged.

Keep elbows pointing forward and close to your ears
Perform slow, controlled reps
Exhale when extending arms up, inhale when lowering
Start with a light dumbbell to master form

exercises.title: Plank
exercises.description: The Plank is a core-strengthening exercise performed by holding your body in a straight line, supported on your forearms and toes. It's excellent for improving core stability, posture, and endurance.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Dropping or raising hips too high
Letting the head hang or craning the neck
Holding the breath
Bending the arms or shrugging shoulders
exercises.rest_speech_text: Break. Get into a straight line on your forearms and toes. Keep your abs tight and hold the position.
steps: 1. Start on the floor on all fours.
2. Lower down to your forearms, with elbows directly under shoulders.
3. Step your feet back one at a time, forming a straight line from head to heels.
4. Engage your core, glutes, and thighs.
5. Hold the position for the desired time without letting your hips drop or rise
exercises.tips:
Keep your body in one straight line from head to heels
Engage your core and glutes
Keep shoulders over your elbows
Breathe slowly and steadily

exercises.title: Power Jack
exercises.description: The Power Jack is a high-energy jump with simultaneous arm and leg extensions. It boosts strength, endurance, coordination, and serves as a great full-body warm-up.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Not jumping wide enough
Unsynchronized arm-leg movements
Moving too quickly 
Landing with stiff legs
exercises.rest_speech_text: Get ready to jump — open your arms and legs wide, then return to center. Stay strong and controlled
steps: 1. Stand upright with feet together, arms at your sides.
2. Jump up, spreading your legs apart and raising your arms overhead.
3. Land softly and immediately jump back to the starting position.
exercises.tips:
Land softly on the balls of your feet
Move arms and legs in sync
Keep your core engaged for balance

exercises.title: T Raise
exercises.description: Lie on your stomach with your arms extended straight out to the sides, forming a "T" shape with your body. Lift your arms up towards. This exercise strengthens the upper back muscles, improves posture, and helps stabilize the shoulders.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Lifting the chest or head off the ground
Using impulse instead of controlled movement
Overarching the lower back
Not squeezing shoulder blades together during lift
exercises.rest_speech_text: For the next Lie face down, lift your arms out to the sides, squeeze your shoulder blades, then lower them down.
steps: 1. Lie face down on the floor with arms stretched out to the sides at shoulder level.
2. Keep your forehead resting lightly on the floor to keep your neck neutral.
3. Slowly lift both arms off the ground by squeezing your shoulder blades together.
4. Slowly lower your arms back down to the starting position
exercises.tips:
Keep your neck relaxed a
Lift only your arms and upper shoulder area
Move slowly and with control
Breathe steadily

exercises.title: Stretch and Embrace
exercises.description: This exercise helps improve shoulder mobility, stretches the chest and upper back, and strengthens the muscles around the shoulder blades. This movement also promotes better posture and relieves tension in the upper body.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Lifting the chest or head too high
Shrugging shoulders toward ears
Bending elbows
Moving too quickly
exercises.rest_speech_text: Break Time. Lie on your stomach, stretch your arms forward, open them out to the sides straight, then bring them back forward
steps: 1. Lie down on your stomach, facing downwards, with your forehead resting on the ground.
2. Straighten your arms, palms facing down.
3. Extend your arms to shoulder level.
4. Then, rotate your thumbs upward and join your straight arms in front of you.
5. Perform 10 repetitions without lowering your arms.
exercises.tips:
Keep your forehead resting lightly on the floor
Maintain slow, controlled arm movements
Keep shoulders relaxed

exercises.title: Knee Raise Arms Down
exercises.description: This standing exercise involves lifting one knee toward the chest while lowering the arms down from an overhead position. It strengthens the core, improves balance, and engages the arms and shoulders in a controlled, coordinated movement.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Dropping the arms too fast or without control
Not engaging the core when lifting the knee
Leaning the torso backward or forward
Failing to lift the knee high enough
exercises.rest_speech_text: Break Time. Raise your knee, bring your arms down smoothly from above.
steps: 1. Start standing tall with arms extended overhead
2. Lift your right knee toward your chest while lowering and bending both arms down toward knee.
3. Return to the starting position
4. Repeat on the left side
exercises.tips:
Keep your spine straight and shoulders relaxed
Engage your abdominal muscles
Lower the arms with control 
Breathe out as you raise the knee and bring arms down

exercises.title: Punching Squat
exercises.description: A dynamic exercise combining a squat with forward punches. It strengthens the legs, glutes, core, and shoulders while improving coordination and cardiovascular fitness.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Not squatting deep enough
Punching too fast without control
Letting knees cave inward during squat
Leaning too far forward or rounding the back
Not engaging core during movement
exercises.rest_speech_text: Break. Stand tall, feet shoulder-width apart. Squat down, then punch forward.
steps: 1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, arms bent at chest level.
2. Lower into a squat, keeping knees behind toes and back straight.
3. From squat position, punch forward with the arms, keeping the core engaged.
4. Stand back up
exercises.tips:
Keep your chest up and back straight
Maintain knees aligned with toes during squat
Punch with controlled, strong movements
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise
Engage your core to protect your lower back

exercises.title: Dog Legs Up
exercises.description: Dog Legs Up is a bodyweight exercise done in an all-fours position, lifting one leg up and back with an upward motion. It strengthens your glutes, hamstrings, and core, and also improves hip mobility and balance.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching your lower back instead of keeping your core tight
Lifting the leg too high and losing form
Rushing the movement without control
Letting your supporting hip drop to the side
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a break. Go to on all fours, lift one leg up and back, squeeze the glutes, then return. Control the motion
steps: 1. Start in an all-fours position, keep your back flat and core tight
2.Lift one leg upward with the knee bent and squeeze your glutes at the top
3. Slowly lower the leg back down
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight and back straight
Lift your leg with control, not momentum
Stop when your thigh is in line with your torso
Breathe steadily

exercises.title: Butterfly Stretch
exercises.description: The Butterfly Stretch is a classic seated stretch that targets the inner thighs, groin, hips, and lower back. Sitting with the soles of your feet together and knees falling outward naturally opens up the hips and improves flexibility in the groin area.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the back or collapsing the chest
Forcing the knees toward the floor
Holding the feet too far away from the body
Bouncing the knees up and down 
Tensing the shoulders
exercises.rest_speech_text: Sit with your feet together, knees open wide. Keep your back straight and feel the stretch in your inner thighs
steps: 1. Sit on the floor with your back straight and legs extended in front of you.
2. Bend your knees and bring the soles of your feet together, let your knees fall outward, aiming toward the floor.
3. Hold your feet or ankles with your hands.
4. Lean slightly forward to deepen the stretch.
5. Hold the position for 20–30 seconds, breathing deeply.
6. Slowly return to starting position
exercises.tips:
Sit tall and keep your spine straight
Bring the heels as close to the groin as is comfortable
Breathe slowly and relax into the stretch

exercises.title: Deep Squat Stretch
exercises.description: The Deep Squat Stretch is an exercise that opens the hips, stretches the lower back, groin, and ankles, and promotes better posture and joint health.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Heels lifting off the ground
Rounding the back or leaning too far forward
Knees caving inward
Not going deep enough into the squat
Holding breath during the stretch
exercises.rest_speech_text: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart. Drop into a deep squat, press your knees outward, and stretch through the hips
steps: 1. Stand with your feet slightly wider than hip-width apart, toes turned slightly outward.
2. Bend your knees and lower your hips down into a deep squat position.
3. Bring your palms together in front of your chest, elbows inside your knees.
4. Hold this position for 20–30 seconds, breathing slowly and deeply.
5. Slowly return to a standing position.
exercises.tips:
Keep your heels flat on the ground
Keep your back straight and chest open
Breathe deeply and evenly
Hold the position — don’t bounce

exercises.title: Plank Shoulder Taps
exercises.description: Plank Shoulder Taps are an performed in a high plank position.This exercise challenges your core stability, balance, and shoulder strength.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Moving the hips side to side.
Letting the lower back sag.
Not engaging the core fully.
Rushing the movement.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Coming up: Plank Shoulder Taps. Keep a strong plank. Tap your shoulders one by one without letting your hips move.
steps: 1. Start in a high plank position with your hands under shoulders and body in a straight line.
2. Lift your right hand and tap your left shoulder.
3. Place your right hand back on the floor.
4. Lift your left hand and tap your right shoulder.
exercises.tips:
Keep your feet slightly wider.
Move slowly and with control.
Keep your hips and shoulders square to the ground.

exercises.title: Walk Down to Plank
exercises.description: Start standing tall, then slowly walk your hands forward on the floor, lowering your body into a plank position. This exercise strengthens your core, shoulders, and arms while improving flexibility in your hamstrings and spine.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Back rounded
Hips too low or too high
Knees locked
Core not tight
Moving too fast
exercises.rest_speech_text: Rest. For the next exercise, stand with your legs open and crawl forward with your hands to a plank pose. Hold for a moment and then return to the starting position.
steps: 1. Stand with feet hip-width apart.
2. Slowly bend at your hips and walk your hands forward on the floor.
3. Walk your hands out until your body forms a straight line from head to heels
4. Hold the plank for a moment, keeping your core tight.
5. Walk your hands back towards your feet and slowly stand up
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight
Move slowly and controlled 
Keep your hips level in the plank.
Slightly bend your knees if your hamstrings feel tight.

exercises.title: Shoulder Opener
exercises.description: This shoulder-opening stretch begins from an all-fours position and focuses on lengthening the shoulders, upper back, and lats. It encourages thoracic spine mobility and shoulder joint flexibility.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting the elbows rest on the floor.               Arching the lower back
Keeping hips too far back or too far forward
Not breathing deeply
exercises.rest_speech_text: Shoulder Opener. Start on your hands and knees, then lower your chest toward your thighs and stretch your arms forward.
steps: 1. Begin on all fours, hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
2. Slowly walk your hands forward, extending your arms fully.
3. Lower your chest and upper body down toward your thighs.
4. Hold the stretch for 20–30 seconds while breathing slowly.
5. Back to starting position and repeat
exercises.tips:
Keep your hips stacked directly above your knees
Stretch your fingers forward
Relax your neck

exercises.title: Hip Ups
exercises.description: Hip Ups are an exercise that targets the glutes, hamstrings, and lower back. Performed lying on your back, the exercise involves lifting your hips. It’s improving hip mobility, and reducing lower back tension.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Overarching the lower back
Pushing through the toes instead of the heels
Letting the knees fall outward or inward
Not engaging the core and glutes fully
exercises.rest_speech_text: Hip Ups. Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat on the floor. Push through your heels and lift your hips by squeezing your glutes.
steps: 1. Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
2.  Put hands below your glutes for support and stability.
3. Tighten your core and press through your heels.
4. Lift your hips off the ground until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
5. Squeeze your glutes at the top and hold for 1–2 seconds.
6. Slowly lower your hips back to the ground with control.
exercises.tips:
Push through your heels
Keep your core tight
Squeeze your glutes at the top
Keep your knees in line with your hips and feet

exercises.title: Swan Pose
exercises.description: The Swan Pose is a gentle back extension exercise performed while lying on your stomach. It's designed to strengthen the lower back muscles, improve spinal flexibility, open up the chest.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Lifting too high and straining the lower back.
Letting the elbows flare out instead of keeping hands under shoulders.
Overextending the neck by tilting the head too far back.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Lie on your stomach, hands bent below chest with fingers forward. Slowly lift your upper body by extending your arms, and gently lean your head back.
steps: 1. Lie face down on the floor with hands bent just below chest level, fingers pointing forward.
2. Slowly extend your arms to lift your upper body.
3. Lean your head gently back, keeping the neck comfortable.
4. Slowly lower back down to the starting position.
exercises.tips:
Keep the movement controlled and gentle.
Focus on lifting from the upper back, not pushing with your hands.
Breathe steadily throughout the movement.

exercises.title: Fallen Toy
exercises.description: Fallen Toy variation is a core strengthening exercise performed lying on your back. With legs bent off the ground, you slowly lower one heel toward the floor. This movement targets the deep abdominal muscles, improves core stability.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting the lower back arch off the floor 
Using impulse instead controlled movement
Holding breath 
Dropping the leg too fast or too low
Lifting head or neck
exercises.rest_speech_text: Fallen Toy on your back. Lie down,bend your legs, and slowly lower one heel to the floor.
steps: 1. Lie on your back with knees bent and legs lifted so shins are parallel to the floor.
2. Extend your arms over your chest with palms facing each other.
3. Slowly lower your right heel until it touches the floor, keep the leg bent and core engaged.
4. Pause briefly, then slowly raise the leg back to the starting position.
5. Repeat with other leg
exercises.tips:
Keep your lower back pressed gently into the floor 
Engage your core muscles
Move slowly and with control
Breathe out while lowering the leg, breathe in when raising it back

exercises.title: Plank Side Jump
exercises.description: Plank Side Jump is a dynamic, high-intensity bodyweight exercise performed from a high plank position. This movement challenges the core, shoulders, and legs.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting hips drop or rise too high.
Landing heavily instead of softly.
Losing plank alignment during jumps.
Jumping too wide.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next up is Plank Side Jump. Stay in a strong plank and jump your feet together side to side. Keep your hips steady and core tight.
steps: 1.Start in a high plank position—hands under shoulders, body straight.
2. Engage your core and keep your feet together.
3. Jump both feet to the right side, keeping knees slightly bent.
4. Jump back to center and jump left
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight and hips level.
Land softly.
Start with small jumps and increase width gradually.
Maintain steady breathing throughout.

exercises.title: T Chin Ups
exercises.description: Lie face down on the floor with your arms extended out to the sides, forming a "T" shape. Pull your elbows down and back towards your sides. This exercise strengthens the upper back, biceps, and improves shoulder stability.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Lifting chest or head off the ground
Using impulse rather than controlled movement
Not fully squeezing shoulder blades
Overarching the lower back
exercises.rest_speech_text: Break. Pull your elbows down by your sides like a chin-up, then extend back
steps: 1. Lie face down on the floor with arms extended to the sides at shoulder level.
2. Keep your forehead lightly touching the floor.
3. Pull your elbows ups toward your sides, squeezing your shoulder blades and activating your biceps.
4. Slowly extend your arms back out to the starting "T" position.
exercises.tips:
Keep your neck relaxed, looking down
Focus on pulling with your back and biceps
Perform slow and controlled reps
Breathe steadily

exercises.title: Split Squat
exercises.description: Split Squats are a unilateral strength exercise where one leg is elevated behind you , and the front leg performs the squat. This improves flexibility, and strength in the quads, glutes, and hamstrings.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting the front knee move too far past the toes
Leaning forward excessively
Not going deep enough into the squat
Placing the back foot too far or too close to the body
exercises.rest_speech_text: Break time. Place one foot on a chair behind you. Lower your back knee down, then push back up with the front leg
steps: 1. Stand in front of a chair and place one foot back on it, laces down.
2. Keep your front foot firmly planted on the floor, engage your core and maintain an upright posture.
3. Lower your body by bending the front knee until the back knee almost touches the ground.
4. Push through the heel of the front leg to return to the starting position.
5. Repeat for reps, then switch legs.
exercises.tips:
Keep your chest lifted and core tight
Lower your back knee straight down, not forward
Make sure the front knee stays in line with the ankle
Focus on pressing through the heel of the front foot to rise

exercises.title: Bent Over Stretch
exercises.description: This exercise is great for stretching your hamstrings and lower back, so be sure to keep your back straight and avoid rounding your shoulders or back.
exercises.common_mistakes: Slouching. Poor amplitude.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Relax time. For the following exercise Get your hands in a lock behind your back and prepare to bend forward.
steps: 1. Start with your feet hip-width apart with your knees slightly bent and your hands locked behind your back.
2. Bend forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and your head and neck in a neutral position.
3. Hold this position for a while and slowly come back up to a standing position.
exercises.tips: Start with a small bend at the hips and gradually work your way deeper into the stretch. If you feel any pain or discomfort, ease up on the stretch and come out of the position slowly.

exercises.title: Low Lunge
exercises.description: The  is a dynamic stretch that targets the quads, hips, ankles, and calves. It helps improve lower body flexibility, stretches the hips and promotes good posture.
exercises.common_mistakes: Bend the back, round the back, extend the knee beyond the toes.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a short break to rest and take a deep breath. Feel the stretch in your muscles and allow any tension to release. Prepare yourself mentally for the next exercise.
exercises.slow_down_phrases: Slow down and feel the stretch in each movement.
steps: 1.Start from a standing position.
2. Take a step back with one leg, fully extending it.
3. Lower down, bending the front knee to create a 90-degree angle.
4. Place your hands on the floor to support your balance.
5. Arch your back and reach back, extending your arms upward.
6. Hold this pose for several deep breaths.
7. Repeat with the other leg.
exercises.tips: Activate your core muscles to stabilize your body and protect your lower back.

exercises.title: Shoulder Wheel
exercises.description: Shoulder Wheel involves moving your shoulders in slow, controlled circular motions while keeping your hands on your waist. This gentle mobility drill helps improve shoulder flexibility, promote better posture.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Moving too fast and losing control
Shrugging the shoulders up too high
Not keeping the back straight
exercises.rest_speech_text: For the next exercise,sit tall, hands on your waist, roll your shoulders gently in a circle. Keep it slow and smooth.
steps: 1. Sit on a chair with feet flat and back straight and place both hands on your waist
2. Slowly roll your shoulders forward in a circular motion
