Complete several reps, then reverse direction
exercises.tips:
Sit tall with a straight spine
Make slow and smooth circular motions
Breathe steadily throughout

exercises.title: Sides of Chest
exercises.description: This exercise helps strengthen the chest area and improve thoracic flexibility. Lie on your back with a pillow placed under your upper back. Slowly raise your chest, engaging the upper abs and chest muscles.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Jerking the chest upward
Straining the neck
Arching the lower back off the ground
exercises.rest_speech_text: Sides of Chest.Lie on your back, pillow under upper back, hands on your neck. Lift your chest slowly, then lower back down.
steps: 1. Lie on your back and place a pillow under your upper back
2. Bend your arms and place hands behind your neck
3. Breathe out and slowly raise your chest
4. Breathe in and lower chest back down
exercises.tips:
Lift with control and smooth motion
Keep your neck relaxed
Breathe steadily, don’t hold your breath

exercises.title: Leg Extension
exercises.description: The seated leg extension strengthens the quadriceps at the front of the thighs. Sitting on a chair helps provide stability while isolating the quads, making it a safe and effective exercise for building leg strength, supporting knee health, and improving mobility. It’s often used for rehabilitation and functional strength training.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Kicking the leg up too quickly
Not fully straightening the leg at the top
Leaning backward or slouching in the chair
Letting the foot swing instead of controlled lowering
Holding breath during the movement
exercises.rest_speech_text: Sit tall, keep your core tight, and get ready to lift your leg up slowly and with control.
steps: 1. Sit on a chair with your back straight, feet flat on the floor, and hands resting on the sides of the chair for support.
2. Engage your core and look straight ahead.
3. Slowly lift your right leg until it is fully extended in front of you, keeping your thigh on the chair.
4. Hold briefly at the top (1–2 seconds), squeezing your quadriceps.
5. Slowly lower the leg back down to the starting position.
6. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the left leg.
exercises.tips:
Sit tall with your back straight and core engaged
Lift slowly and with control, avoiding momentum
Exhale while extending the leg, inhale while lowering
Keep the movement smooth and avoid locking the knee

exercises.title: Straight Arm Raise
exercises.description: This exercise involves lifting your straight arms from your sides up overhead, enhancing shoulder flexibility, posture, and upper-body strength. It’s useful for warming up the upper body and increasing shoulder range of motion.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching the lower back
Raising arms too quickly
Bending elbows
Tensing the neck or shrugging shoulders
exercises.rest_speech_text: Time to break. In the next exercise,stand tall, raise your arms overhead slowly, then bring them back down with control.
steps: 1.Stand upright, feet shoulder-width apart and arms on your sides
2. Raise arms slowly and straight overhead, palms facing forward
3. Pause at the top, then lower arms back down to the starting position.
exercises.tips:
Keep arms straight but relaxed
Engage your core to avoid back arching
Lift arms slowly and with control
Keep your neck and shoulders relaxed

exercises.title: Bowling
exercises.description: The Bowling focuses on balance, coordination, and core control, while gently activating the legs, arms, and back. This movement is excellent for improving stability, posture, and overall body awareness.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Losing balance during the reach
Rushing the movement without control
Locking the knees
Not maintaining core engagement
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a break. Get ready to perform a smooth bowling motion—reach forward, keep your back straight, and return with balance
steps: 1. Stand with your back straight and take the ball in your hands, placing them in front of you at chest level.
2. Move one leg backward, imitating a lunge, but not touching the floor with your knee, but trying to extend the leg evenly.
3. Rotate your body in the opposite direction from your foot and rotate your arms.
4. Return to the starting position and repeat.
exercises.tips:
Move slowly and with control
Focus on a steady, balanced stance
Keep the knees slightly bent
Engage your core throughout the movement

exercises.title: Bent Elbows Raise
exercises.description: Bent Elbows Raise is a simple but effective exercise that strengthens the shoulders and upper back muscles. It helps improve posture, shoulder stability, and upper body strength.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Raising arms too high above shoulder level
Letting elbows drop or straighten during the raise
Shrugging shoulders up towards ears
exercises.rest_speech_text: Break time. Stand straight, bend elbows, lift arms to shoulder height, hold, then slowly lower.
steps: 1.Stand or sit with your back straight.
2. Bend your elbows, hands in line with elbows.
3. Raise your arms out to the sides until your upper arms are level with your shoulders and hold for 2 second
4. Slowly lower your arms back down.
exercises.tips:
Keep your elbows bent
Move slowly and control the lift and lower phases
Relax your shoulders, don’t let them shrug up
Keep your core engaged

exercises.title: Lat Pulldown
exercises.description: The Lat Pulldown strengthens the back muscles, primarily the latissimus dorsi, while also engaging the biceps, shoulders, and core. It improves upper-body pulling strength, posture, and back width, making it a key exercise for balanced upper-body development and better performance in pull-ups or climbing movements.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Pulling the bar behind the neck, straining the shoulders and neck
Using momentum or leaning too far back
Not engaging the lats—pulling mostly with the arms
Incomplete range of motion
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a deep breath, relax your grip, and get ready to pull down strong—lead with your elbows and engage your back.
steps: 1. Adjust the thigh pad and select your resistance weight.
2. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width, palms facing forward.
3. Sit down with your thighs secured and torso upright.
4. Pull the bar down toward your upper chest, leading with your elbows.
5. Squeeze your back muscles, then slowly return the bar to the starting position.
exercises.tips:
Keep your chest up and shoulders down
Pull the bar to your upper chest, not behind the neck
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the bottom
Control the bar as you return to the starting position

exercises.title: Frog Swim
exercises.description: Frog Swim movement engages the glutes, hamstrings, core, and shoulders, while improving hip mobility, balance, and coordination. The outward toe position increases activation of the outer hips and glutes, promoting better hip stability.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Locking the knees
Allowing the lower back to arch excessively 
Not turning the toes outward during the leg movement
Leaning forward or backward
Moving the leg too quickly without control
exercises.rest_speech_text: Frog Swim. Slightly bent the knees. Slowly move one leg back, then return and switch legs
steps: 1. Stand with feet hip-width apart.
2. Slightly bend your knees, keeping them soft and not locked.
3. Slowly extend your right leg backward with toes turned to sides
4. Return your right leg to the starting position.
5. Repeat with the left leg.
exercises.tips:
Maintain a slight bend in your knees
Keep your core engaged
Turn your toes outward when you extend your leg backward
Move the leg slowly and with control

exercises.title: Side Kick
exercises.description: Side Kick is a dynamic lower-body exercise that targets the glutes, hips, and outer thighs. It improves hip mobility, leg strength, balance, and coordination.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Leaning too far
Bending the standing leg too much
Kicking too high without control
Dropping the upper body instead of staying upright
Not engaging the core
exercises.rest_speech_text: Rest Time. Stand tall, shift weight to one leg, and get ready to kick the other leg to the side with control
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, hands at your chest or on your hips
2. Shift your weight onto one leg.
3. Lift the other leg and kick it straight out to the side, foot flexed or pointed slightly forward.
4. Return the leg to starting position.
5. Repeat for the desired number of reps, then switch legs.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight to stay balanced
Focus on control over height
Keep the kicking leg straight but not locked
Hands can be held in front of your chest for stability
Point your toes slightly forward for better alignment

exercises.title: Bodyweight Squats
exercises.description: Bodyweight squats are a foundational lower-body strength exercise that uses your own body weight as resistance. They target the major muscles of the lower body and help improve balance, flexibility, posture, and overall functional fitness
exercises.common_mistakes:
Knees collapsing inward
Heels lifting off the floor
Rounding the back or leaning too far forward
Not squatting deep enough
Looking down or craning the neck
exercises.rest_speech_text: To do this exercise Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, lower into a squat position, keeping knees aligned, rise back up, and repeat
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly pointed outward.
2. Begin the movement by pushing your hips back and bending your knees.
3. Lower down until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor.
4. Keep heels flat on the ground, knees in line with toes.
5.Push through your heels to return to the starting position.
exercises.tips:
Keep your chest up
Push your hips back
Drive through your heels as you rise
Engage your core
Track knees over toes
Breathe in on the way down, out on the way up

exercises.title: Warrior II
exercises.description: Warrior II is an exercise that strengthens the legs, opens the hips, and improves balance and focus. Standing with feet wide apart, one foot turned out, arms extended parallel to the floor, and bending the front knee, this pose builds lower body strength, stretches the groin and shoulders, and enhances stability.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Front knee collapsing inward
Back foot turned incorrectly
Shoulders lifted
Torso leaning forward
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a break. Stand wide, turn front foot out, bend front knee, arms stretched out, look forward
steps: 1. Stand with feet apart
2. Turn your right foot out and left foot slightly in.
3. Bend your right knee directly over your ankle
4. Extend your arms out to the sides, parallel to the floor, palms down.
5. Keep your torso upright and look forward over your right hand.
6. Hold for desired time, then switch sides.
exercises.tips:
Keep front knee aligned over ankle
Press the outer edge of back foot firmly into the floor
Relax shoulders away from ears

exercises.title: Side Leg Raise
exercises.description: The side leg raise strengthens the hips, thighs and glutes, while also improving balance and stability. This exercise is excellent for toning the outer thighs, improving hip mobility, and enhancing functional movements.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Leaning the torso to the opposite side
Bending or locking the standing leg excessively
Letting the raised leg drop too quickly or swing
Pointing toes outward
Holding breath during the movement
exercises.rest_speech_text: Stand tall behind the chair, keep your core engaged, and get ready to lift your leg slowly to the side.
steps: 1. Stand behind a straight-backed chair with feet slightly apart, hands on the chair for balance.
2. Breathe out and slowly lift your right leg out to the side, keeping your back and legs straight. Your feet should end about 12–18 inches apart.
3. Hold the raised leg for one second.
4. Slowly lower your leg back to the starting position.
5. Repeat 6–8 times with the right leg.
6. Switch to the left leg and repeat.
exercises.tips:
Keep your back straight and core engaged
Slightly bend the standing leg for stability
Lift the leg slowly and control the motion
Keep toes pointing forward, not outward
Use the chair lightly for balance

exercises.title: Lying Face Down Flat Leg Raise
exercises.description: This exercise involves lying on your stomach with legs extended and flat. From this position, on leg lifted slightly off the ground while keeping it straight. It is excellent for strengthening the glutes, hamstrings, and lower back,
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching the lower back excessively
Lifting legs too high
Bending the knees during the lift
Holding breath
Jerking the legs upward
exercises.rest_speech_text: Lie face down, keep legs straight, lift one leg off the ground, hold briefly, lower down, and repeat with other leg
steps: 1. Lie face down on a mat with your legs extended straight and close together.
2. Without bending your knees or arching your back, slowly lift one leg just a few inches off the ground and hold for 1-2 seconds
3. Slowly lower the leg back down to the floor and switch the leg
exercises.tips:
Keep your forehead rested 
Engage your core
Focus on squeezing the glutes
Only lift your leg as high as you can
Breathe steadily

exercises.title: Back Plank Kick
exercises.description: The Back Plank Kick is a compound exercise that targets the core, glutes, hamstrings, and shoulders, performed from a reverse plank position. You maintain a strong bridge-like posture while alternately kicking each leg straight into the air. This movement builds posterior chain strength, improves hip stability.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Dropping the hips too low
Letting shoulders collapse or rounding them forward
Swinging legs instead of controlled kicks
Holding breath
Kicking too high
exercises.rest_speech_text: Get into reverse plank. Lift one leg up, then switch. Keep hips up and body straight.
steps: 1. Sit on the floor with legs extended and place your palms flat behind you, fingers pointing toward your feet.
2. Press into your hands and heels to lift your hips, forming a straight line from shoulders to heels
3. Engage your core and lift one leg straight up without letting your hips drop.
4. Lower the leg with control and repeat with the other leg.
exercises.tips:
Keep your hips lifted and aligned with shoulders and heels
Engage your core and glutes
Kick with control

exercises.title: X Pose
exercises.description: This stretch involves lifting the right arm overhead, placing the left hand at stomach level, crossing the left leg in front of the right, and gently leaning to the left. This exercise helps improve balance, flexibility in the side body, coordination, and posture.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Overarching the back.
Leaning too far and losing balance.
Locking the knees or twisting the hips.
Raising the shoulder with the overhead arm.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Now, lift your right arm up, cross your left leg in front, and lean gently to the left. Feel the stretch and breathe.”
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet together.
2. Raise your right arm overhead, keeping it close to your ear, place your left hand near your stomach
3. Cross your left leg over your right leg.
4. Gently lean to the left side without twisting your torso.
5. Hold briefly, return to center, and switch sides if repeating.
exercises.tips:
Cross the legs gently without forcing balance.
Engage your core to maintain control.
Breathe steadily and don’t hold your breath.

exercises.title: Full Squat
exercises.description: This exercise involves lowering your hips fully toward the seat of a chair, using the chair as a guide or safety net. This exercise strengthens thighs, glutes, and hips.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting knees go past toes
Bending the back instead
Dropping too quickly
Letting heels lift off the floor
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a break before the next exercise. Lower yourself toward the chair with control. Keep your chest up and knees aligned.
steps: 1. Sit on the chair
2. Keep your arms extended in front for balance.
3. Slowly extend your knees and push your hips up to standing.
4. Push through your heels to return to standing.
exercises.tips:
Keep your weight in your heels
Engage your core
Use arms for balance
Move slowly and with control

exercises.title: Lift Lunges
exercises.description: Lift Lunges are an exercise that combines a lunge with an overhead reach. You step one leg straight back while bending the front leg. This movement builds lower-body strength, enhances shoulder flexibility.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Tilting the torso too far forward
Letting the front knee pass beyond the toes
Raising arms with bent elbows 
Not keeping the back leg extended
Rushing through the motion
exercises.rest_speech_text: Lift Lunges. Step back with one leg,while bending other leg and raise extended arms overhead.
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, arms relaxed at your sides.
2. Shift your weight onto one leg.
3. Step the opposite leg straight back, keeping it extended, while bending the front knee and extend arms overhead
4. Pause briefly, feeling the stretch and engagement.
5. Lower your arms and return to standing and switch legs.
exercises.tips:
Move slowly, focusing on posture and control
Keep your core engaged
Align front knee over the ankle
Breathe in as you lunge, breathe out as you return

exercises.title: Seated Elbow Elevation
exercises.description: This exercise is performed while sitting on a chair with your elbows bent and hands resting on your shoulders. This exercise helps improve shoulder mobility, strengthens the upper back and chest, activates posture muscles.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Tilting the torso while moving shoulders
Performing the movement too fast
Raising the shoulders or tensing the neck
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a break and sit straight with your arms on your lap. Relax your shoulders and breathe deeply to release tension.
steps: 1. Sit upright on a chair, feet flat on the floor.
2.  Bend your elbows and rest your hands on your shoulders.
3. Move your shoulders back as you raise your elbows overhead.
4. Bring your shoulders forward and lower your elbows to chest level.
exercises.tips:
Keep your torso stable, move only your shoulders
Perform the motion slowly and smoothly
Ensure your elbows move from chest level up to overhead

exercises.title: Knee Raise Clap Hands
exercises.description: This is a dynamic standing exercise that combines core engagement with upper body coordination. While lifting one knee toward the chest, you clap your hands underneath the raised leg. This exercise helps improve balance, core strength, and coordination.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Leaning the upper body too far forward
Not lifting the knee high enough
Rushing the movement and losing balance
exercises.rest_speech_text: Stand tall, engage your core, and raise your knee high before clapping under. Alternate legs with rhythm and control.
steps: 1.Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and arms overhead.
2. Lift your right knee toward your chest while clapping your hands underneath it
3.Lower your right leg and return arms overhead.
4. Repeat with the left leg
exercises.tips:
Keep your chest upright and back straight
Engage your core
Focus on timing: clap as the knee peaks
Perform the movement at a controlled pace

exercises.title: Side Knee Lift
exercises.description: The Side Knee Lift and exercise that targets the obliques, hip flexors, and glutes by lifting one knee out to the side while simultaneously bending the upper body so the same-side elbow touches the knee. This motion creates a dynamic side crunch, enhancing core activation, balance, and mobility.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Twisting the torso instead of crunching sideways
Not bringing the elbow and knee close enough
Lifting the knee without control
Letting the supporting leg cave inward
Arching the lower back
exercises.rest_speech_text: Side Knee Lift. Hands behind your neck. Lift your knee out and bend to touch it with your elbow. Alternate sides.
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart. Place your hands gently behind your neck with elbows out to the sides.
2. Shift weight to one leg and lift the opposite knee out to the side.
3. At the same time, bend your upper body sideways to bring the same-side elbow toward the knee.
4. Touch or nearly touch your elbow to the knee.
5. Return to the starting position and switch sides.
exercises.tips:
Keep hands gently touching the back of your neck 
Lead with the elbow and knee, not the shoulder
Keep your core tight and chest lifted
Perform the crunch with a controlled side bend
Breathe out as elbow meets knee for better core engagement

exercises.title: Pull-Up with and without asistance
exercises.description: The Pull-Up is a classic upper-body exercise that strengthens the lats, traps, biceps, and shoulders while engaging the core for stabilization. Assisted pull-ups allow beginners to perform the movement safely, while unassisted pull-ups develop maximal upper-body pulling strength, enhance posture, and improve functional fitness.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Swinging the body or using momentum
Partial range of motion (not going fully down or up)
Shrugging shoulders or letting them rise toward the ears
Flaring elbows excessively
exercises.rest_speech_text: Relax your arms, engage your core, and get ready to pull up strong and controlled, focusing on your back and elbows.
steps: 1. Grip the pull-up bar with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width, palms facing away (overhand) or toward you (underhand).
2. Hang fully extended with shoulders relaxed and core engaged.
3. Pull your body up by driving your elbows down and back until your chin passes the bar.
4. Lower yourself slowly to full arm extension.
5. Repeat for the desired number of reps, using assistance if needed.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight and torso straight
Lead the movement with your elbows rather than your hands
Lower slowly to maximize eccentric strength
Adjust assistance as needed to complete controlled reps

exercises.title: Cable Bar Reverse Grip Pushdown
exercises.description: The Cable Bar Reverse Grip Pushdown is an isolation exercise that targets the triceps, particularly the medial and long heads. This movement helps improve arm definition, strength, and stability in pressing exercises.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Using too much weight and swinging the body
Allowing the elbows to move away from the sides
Not fully extending the arms at the bottom
Using wrists instead of triceps to push the bar
Leaning too far forward or arching the back
exercises.rest_speech_text: Stand tall, elbows tight, and get ready to press down with control.
steps: 1. Attach a straight bar to a high pulley on a cable machine.
2. Stand facing the machine, grab the bar with an underhand grip (palms facing up), and position your hands shoulder-width apart.
3. Step back slightly and keep your torso upright with a slight bend in your knees.
4. Tuck your elbows close to your sides and engage your core.
5. Exhale and push the bar downward by extending your elbows until your arms are fully straight.
6. Squeeze your triceps at the bottom for a second.
7. Inhale and slowly allow the bar to rise back to the starting position under control.
exercises.tips:
Keep your elbows locked by your sides throughout the movement
Focus on squeezing your triceps at the bottom of each rep
Move only your forearms—your upper arms should remain stationary
Use a controlled tempo—no jerking or momentum
Exhale while pushing down, inhale as you return to start

exercises.title: Lunges
exercises.description: Lunges are a leg-strengthening exercise that works your thighs, hips, and glutes. You step forward with one leg and lower your body until both knees are bent, then push back to the starting position. Lunges also help improve your balance and coordination.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Knees go too far past the toes.
Front knee falls inward or outward.
Back doesn’t stay straight.
Not stepping far enough forward.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Get ready for lunges. Stand tall, take a deep breath, and get ready to move.
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
2. Step forward with your right leg.
3. Bend both knees to lower your body. Your front thigh should be parallel to the ground.
4. Keep your back straight and your front knee above your ankle
5. Push through your front heel to return to standing.
6. Repeat with the left leg stepping forward
exercises.tips: Make sure your front knee stays directly above your ankle — not past your toes

exercises.title: Forward Shoulders Warm up
exercises.description: This exercise mobilizes the shoulder joints, warms up the upper body, and prepares you for physical activity
exercises.common_mistakes:
Raising elbows too high
Rushing the movement
Letting the chest collapse
Not completing the full circle
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Forward Shoulder Warm Up. Place your hands on your shoulders and gently rotate your elbows forward in circles.
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and place your fingertips on your shoulders, elbows pointing forward.
2. Slowly circle your elbows forward, creating big controlled circles.
3. Breathe in as elbows rise, breathe out as they come down and forward.
exercises.tips:
Keep elbows lifted at chest height without tension
Perform slow, controlled circles
Maintain a tall spine
Breathe steadily throughout the movement

exercises.title: Squat Thrusts
exercises.description: A squat thrust is a fast, full-body move that starts in a push-up position, drops into a squat and then kicks your legs back into a plank. It builds strength and boosts your heart rate.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Not keeping hands flat on the ground
Letting hips drop too low in the plank
Rounding the back when jumping feet 
Moving too fast
Landing hard on feet
exercises.rest_speech_text: Get ready for squat thrusts. Go to a push-ups position and get ready to jump your feet forward to your hands and move with energy.
steps: 1. Start in a push-ups position
2. Keep your body straight and strong in the plank
3. Jump your feet forward to your hands.
4. Keep your body straight and strong in the plank.
5. Jump both feet back towards your hands, landing in a squat position.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight to protect your back
Land softly when jumping your feet in and out
Move at a pace you can control
Make sure your hips stay level in the plank
Keep breathing steadily

exercises.title: Dumbbell Skullcrusher
exercises.description: The Dumbbell Skullcrusher isolates the triceps, building strength and definition in the upper arm. Using dumbbells allows for a natural range of motion and balanced muscle activation. It also develops core stability and anti-extension strength, supporting proper posture during overhead and pressing movements.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Flaring elbows outward
Arching the lower back
Dropping the dumbbells too quickly
Using momentum instead of controlled motion
exercises.rest_speech_text: Elbows tight, core engaged—get ready to extend strong.
steps: 1. Lie on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand, arms extended above your chest.
2. Keep elbows close to your head and core engaged.
3. Lower the dumbbells toward your forehead by bending the elbows.
4. Pause briefly, then press back up to the starting position.
exercises.tips:
Keep elbows tucked close to your head
Move slowly through both lowering and pressing phases
Engage your core to protect your lower back
Focus on squeezing the triceps at the top

exercises.title: Plank Spider Crawl
exercises.description: Plank Spider Crawl is a dynamic core-strengthening exercise performed from a high plank position. This targets the core, shoulders, chest, and hip flexors, while improving coordination and mobility.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting hips sag or rise too high.
Not engaging the core.
Bringing the knee across the body instead of to the side.
Rushing the movement.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next up is Plank Spider Crawl. In a strong plank position, bring each knee toward the same-side elbow.
steps: 1. Start in a high plank position with hands directly under shoulders and body in a straight line.
2. Engage your core and glutes.
3. Bring your right knee toward your right elbow.
4. Return your right foot back to plank and switch sides
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight and back flat.
Move with control and full range
Breathe steadily
Start slow and focus on clean movement

exercises.title: Full Body Crunch
exercises.description: The Full Body Crunch is an exercise that targets the abs and lower back.
exercises.common_mistakes: Pulling on your neck. Not engaging your lower abs. Not keeping your legs straight enough.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Rest time. Now you need to lie on your back, legs straight and slightly raised above the floor, hands behind your head. Simultaneously lift your upper body and legs towards your chest. Return to starting position and repeat
steps: 1. Lie on the mat with your back, knees bent and hands behind your head.
2. Tighten your abs and lift your upper body off the floor, pulling your knees toward your chest.
3. Hold for a few seconds and then slowly lower yourself to the starting position.
4. Repeat for desired number of reps.
exercises.tips: Maintain proper alignment. Breathe rhythmically.

exercises.title: On Place Lunge
exercises.description: The On Place Lunge is a strength exercise where you step into a lunge position and stay in place as you move up and down. It builds strength in your legs, glutes, and core, and improves balance.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching the back
Letting the front knee push too far forward
Losing balance due to poor stance width
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: On-Place Lunge. Step forward and lower down. Stay tall and strong
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
2. Step one foot forward into a lunge position, keep your back straight and both knees bent
3. Lower your body straight down, front knee should be above the ankle, back knee points toward the floor.
4. Push through your front heel and come back up — but stay in the same stance
5.Do all reps on one leg, then switch
exercises.tips:
Keep your chest up, and look forward.
Don’t let your front knee go past your toes.
Tighten your core to help with balance.

exercises.title: High Knee Fast Feet
exercises.description: High Knee Fast Feet is a cardio exercise that combines quick foot taps with high knee lifts, performed in rapid alternation. It boosts cardiovascular endurance, burns calories, and improves agility, coordination, and leg strength.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Slouching or leaning too far forward
Landing heavily
Not lifting knees high enough
Letting the movement get sloppy as speed increases
exercises.rest_speech_text: High Knee Fast Feet. Stand tall, drive your knees up quickly one after another while keeping your feet fast and light.
steps: 1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, arms bent at your sides.
2. Begin moving your feet quickly as if running in place—light, rapid steps.
3. At the same time, lift one knee high toward your chest.
4. Lower that leg and immediately switch, alternating knees quickly.
exercises.tips:
Stay on the balls of your feet to move quickly
Keep your chest lifted and core tight
Pump your arms in rhythm to support balance and speed
Start slow, then increase pace

exercises.title: Bird Dog
exercises.description: The Bird Dog is a fundamental core and balance exercise performed from an all-fours position. It involves extending one arm and the opposite leg simultaneously while keeping the body stable and aligned. This movement trains deep core muscles, improves postural control.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching or rounding the back
Letting the hips tilt or rotate
Lifting the arm or leg too high
Moving too fast
Not engaging the core muscles
exercises.rest_speech_text: Start on all fours. Extend your opposite arm and leg—stay stable and controlled
steps: 1. Begin on your hands and knees, with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
2. Engage your core and extend your right arm forward and left leg back, both parallel to the floor.
3. Hold for a moment while keeping your hips and shoulders square to the floor.
4. Return to the starting position with control.
5. Repeat on the opposite side.
exercises.tips:
Keep your back flat and core engaged 
Extend your arm and leg to shoulder and hip height only
Focus on stability
Perform the movement slowly

exercises.title: Side Lunge with Power
exercises.description: Side Lunge with Power is a dynamic movement that combines strength and agility. You step to the side into a deep lunge, then push off the lunging leg with force to return to standing. This strengthens the legs, glutes, and core while improving balance and explosiveness.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting the knee go past the toes
Leaning too far forward
Not pushing off strongly from the lunge
exercises.rest_speech_text: Rest time. Step wide, lunge low, push back up with power. Stay strong and balanced.
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
2.Step to the side and bend the lunging knee while the other leg stays straight.
3. Push off the lunging foot to return to the start and change sides
exercises.tips:
Keep your chest lifted and back straight
Push off the lunging foot forcefully
Control the movement, don’t rush
Engage your core for balance

exercises.title: Extended Arm Circles
exercises.description: Extended Arm Circles is an exercise performed standing with arms extended horizontally to the sides. You make circular motions with your arms, which helps to increase shoulder mobility, improve circulation, and activate the muscles around the shoulders and upper back.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Using too much speed
Shrugging or tensing shoulders up toward ears
Not maintaining straight arms or proper posture
Making irregular or uneven circles
Holding breath instead of breathing naturally
exercises.rest_speech_text: Extended Arm Circles. Stand tall, stretch your arms out to the sides, and start making small controlled circles.
steps: 1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and extend your arms parallel to the floor.
2. Circle your arms forward using small controlled motions.
exercises.tips:
Keep arms fully extended and parallel to the floor
Move in slow, controlled circles
Keep shoulders relaxed and down away from ears
Start with small circles
Breathe steadily and evenly

exercises.title: Preacher Curl Machine
exercises.description: The Preacher Curl Machine isolates the biceps brachii and helps prevent cheating by stabilizing the upper arms. It strengthens and shapes the biceps while improving elbow control and upper-arm aesthetics, making it ideal for focused arm development.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Lifting with the shoulders or leaning backward
Not fully extending the elbows at the bottom
Using momentum instead of controlled motion
Flaring elbows outward
exercises.rest_speech_text: Relax your arms, keep your elbows steady, and get ready to curl with control, focusing on your biceps.
steps: 1. Sit on the preacher curl machine and place your upper arms on the pad.
2. Grip the handles or bar firmly.
3. Curl the weight upward, fully contracting the biceps at the top.
4. Slowly lower back to the starting position without losing control.
5. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
exercises.tips:
Keep your upper arms pressed firmly against the pad
Exhale while curling up, inhale while lowering
Move slowly and focus on the contraction at the top
Avoid locking out elbows completely to maintain tension

exercises.title: Opposite Arm Circles
exercises.description: This exercise involves moving one arm forward in a circular motion while the opposite arm moves backward in a circle. It improves shoulder mobility, coordination, and upper body flexibility.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Moving arms too fast or out of control
Shrugging shoulders or tensing neck
Arching the lower back
Using only small arm movement instead of full circles
exercises.rest_speech_text: Ready to draw circles with your hands? Circle one arm forward, the other backward, keep control and breathe.
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart and extend arms straight out to the sides at shoulder height.
2. Start circling your right arm forward while circling your left arm backward.
exercises.tips:
Keep movements slow and controlled
Engage your core to stabilize the body
Keep shoulders down and relaxed
Breathe steadily throughout the movement

exercises.title: Wide Leg Double Crunch
exercises.description: Wide Leg Double Crunch is an exercise performed lying on your back with your arms supporting your neck, while both legs are spread wide and lifted off the ground. This exercise effectively targets the rectus abdominis and the inner thighs, improving core strength and flexibility.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Pulling on the neck with hands
Using impulse instead of muscle control
Not keeping legs lifted and wide throughout the movement
Arching the lower back off the floor
exercises.rest_speech_text: Break time. Lie back, legs wide and lifted. Crunch up, bringing shoulders and legs closer together.
steps: 1. Lie on your back with knees bent, feet lifted off the floor and spread wide apart.
2. Place your hands lightly behind your neck to support your head.
3. Engage your core and simultaneously crunch your upper body and legs toward each other.
4. Pause briefly at the top of the movement, then slowly lower back to starting position.
exercises.tips:
Keep your hands gently supporting your neck without pulling
Focus on controlled movements, squeezing abs as you crunch
Keep your lower back pressed into the floor
Breathe out on the crunch and breathe in on the release

exercises.title: Band Kneeling Single Arm Pulldown
exercises.description: The Band Kneeling Single Arm Pulldown is a powerful upper-body exercise that strengthens the lats, shoulders, and biceps while improving posture and core stability.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Pulling with the arm instead of engaging the lats
Rounding or arching the back during the pulldown
Allowing the elbow to flare out
Letting the band snap back too quickly
Not keeping the core tight and upright posture
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a deep breath and get ready — Band Kneeling Single Arm Pulldown is next!
steps: 1. Anchor the resistance band securely above head height — such as a pull-up bar, door anchor, or sturdy overhead beam.
2. Kneel on one or both knees directly under the anchor point, holding the band handle with one hand.
3. Start with your arm extended overhead, palm facing forward.
4. Exhale and pull the band down and back by driving your elbow toward your hip — feel your lats activate.
5. Pause briefly at the bottom position, keeping your shoulder blade squeezed.
6. Slowly return to the starting position with control, feeling resistance on the way up.
7. Complete all reps on one side before switching to the other arm.
exercises.tips:
Think about driving your elbow down and back toward your hip, not just pulling with your hand
Keep your torso tall and core engaged throughout the movement
Control both the pull and return phases to maximize muscle tension
Focus on feeling your lats doing the work

exercises.title: Seated Deltoid Stretch
exercises.description: This exercise is performed while sitting on a chair and gently stretches the shoulder muscle. One arm is extended across the chest, and the opposite hand helps pull it in closer. It improves shoulder flexibility, relieves upper body tension.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Raising the shoulders during the stretch
Bending the stretched arm at the elbow
Leaning the torso forward or sideways
exercises.rest_speech_text: Rest. Sit upright, extend one arm across your chest and use the other arm to gently press it in.
steps: 1. Sit upright on a chair, feet flat on the floor, back straight.
2. Extend your right arm across your chest.
3. Use your left hand to gently press the right arm closer to your body, near the elbow.
4. Hold the stretch for 15–20 seconds, then switch sides.
exercises.tips:
Keep your back straight and neck relaxed
Keep the stretched arm straight
Breathe calmly, don’t hold your breath

exercises.title: Cancan Jump
exercises.description: Cancan Jumps are the cardio-based exercise. You stay light on your feet and kick one leg up at a time while hopping slightly on the other. This move boosts heart rate, improves coordination, and strengthens your legs and core.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Kicking too high and too fast (losing control)
Not using your arms for balance
Landing hard on your feet
exercises.rest_speech_text: Get ready for Cancan Jumps. Stay tall, kick one leg at a time, and land softly. Keep moving with control and energy
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart
2. Hop on your left foot and kick your right leg straight forward.
3. Land softly, then hop on your right foot and kick your left leg
4. Keep your arms moving naturally or place hands on hips
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight to stay balanced
Kick only as high as you can with control
Use your arms to help you stay steady
Land softly on the balls of your feet
Keep a steady rhythm

exercises.title: Easy Sprinters Sit Ups
exercises.description: Easy Sprinters Sit-Ups combine core strengthening with gentle lower-body movement. This exercise improves abdominal endurance, hip flexor strength, and coordination. It’s a great way to engage the core without the intensity of full sit-ups.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Pulling on the neck with hands
Using momentum instead of muscle control
Not fully engaging the core
Moving too quickly, sacrificing form
exercises.rest_speech_text: Let’s warm up the core gently with sprinter-style sit-ups. Stay controlled and steady.
steps: 1. Lie on your back with your legs bent at the knees and your arms at your sides.
2. Pull your head and upper body off the floor and while reaching to your knees, extend one arm and perform a twisting motion with your core to the side.
3. Lower your upper body and legs back down to the starting position. Repeat again with other hand.
exercises.tips:
Keep your neck relaxed and chin slightly tucked
Focus on slow, controlled movements
Engage your abdominal muscles throughout
Exhale as you lift and reach, inhale as you lower

exercises.title: Dips-Maschine (potentially assisted)
exercises.description: The Dips Machine strengthens the triceps, chest, and shoulders while providing a stable and controlled movement. The assisted version helps beginners build strength safely, while the unassisted version challenges the upper body with full bodyweight resistance. This exercise enhances pushing power, improves arm tone, and supports shoulder joint stability.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting the shoulders roll forward during the dip
Going too low and overstressing the shoulders
Swinging or using momentum instead of control
Not keeping the elbows close to the body
exercises.rest_speech_text: Breathe in, reset your grip, and get ready to push strong through your arms and chest with control.
steps: 1. Adjust the assist weight if needed (more weight = more assistance).
2. Grip the handles firmly and position your knees or feet on the platform.
3. Begin with arms straight and shoulders down.
4. Lower your body by bending your elbows to about 90 degrees.
5. Push back up through your palms until your arms are almost straight.
exercises.tips:
Keep your chest slightly forward and core tight
Lower yourself slowly, keeping control through the full range
Stop when your upper arms are parallel to the floor
Push through your palms to return to the start position

exercises.title: Bent Over Twist
exercises.description: The Bent Over Twist is a dynamic rotational exercise performed from a standing, forward-leaning position. With arms extended forward you rotate one arm overhead toward one side along with your head, switch side. This targets the external obliques, core stabilizers, shoulders.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding or collapsing the upper back
Leaning too forward
Moving too fast, losing control
Rotating hips instead of the upper body
Lifting the head excessively
exercises.rest_speech_text: Rest time. Lean forward with arms outstretched. Rotate one arm overhead with your head, then switch sides
steps: 1. Stand with feet hip-width apart and knees slightly bent.
2. Hinge forward at the hips, lowering your upper body so your arms extend forward above your toes.
3. Rotate your torso and lift one arm overhead to the side, turning your head.
4. Return to the center position with arms extended forward.
5. Repeat the twist to the opposite side, lifting the other arm overhead and turning your head
exercises.tips:
Keep your back flat and core engaged 
Maintain a slight bend in the knees for balance
Lead the twist with your shoulder and head
Move slowly and smoothly for control
Focus on stretching through the torso

exercises.title: Knee Push Ups
exercises.description: Knee push-ups are a beginner-friendly version of regular push-ups. You keep your knees on the floor to reduce the load, making it easier to build arm and chest strength.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Lifting your hips too high
Not lowering your chest close enough to the ground
Elbows too wide apart
Neck tension or looking forward instead of down
Rushing the movement
exercises.rest_speech_text: Get ready for knee push-ups. Keep your body straight and lower yourself
steps: 1. Start by kneeling on the floor with your hands on the floor slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
2. Straighten your arms and place your hands under your shoulders.
3.Keep your body in a straight line from head to knees
4. Bend your elbows and lower your chest close to the floor
5. Push back up to the starting position.
exercises.tips: Pause briefly when your chest is a few inches from the floor. Keep your hips in line with your knees and shoulders throughout the exercise to prevent strain on your lower back.

exercises.title: Dumbbell Seated Overhead Press
exercises.description: The Dumbbell Seated Overhead Press targets the shoulders, triceps, and upper chest while minimizing lower back involvement. Sitting provides stability, allowing better focus on the deltoids and improving core stability, lumbopelvic control, and anti-extension strength for safe overhead pressing.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching the lower back
Flaring elbows outward
Using momentum instead of controlled motion
Incomplete range of motion
exercises.rest_speech_text: Sit tall, brace your core, and press with control.
steps: 1. Sit on a bench with back support, holding dumbbells at shoulder height.
2. Engage your core and press the dumbbells overhead until arms are extended.
3. Pause briefly at the top, then lower the dumbbells slowly to shoulder level.
4. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
exercises.tips:
Keep your back pressed against the bench and core tight
Press the dumbbells straight up without leaning
Lower slowly and under control
Avoid locking elbows at the top

exercises.title: Dumbbell Sumo Deadlift
exercises.description: The Dumbbell Sumo Deadlift strengthens the lower body and posterior chain using a wide stance. It targets the glutes, hamstrings, quads, and inner thighs while engaging the core and improving hip mobility and balance. The upright posture reduces lower back strain compared to conventional deadlifts.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the back or shoulders
Letting knees cave inward
Lifting with the back instead of legs
Standing too narrow or too wide
exercises.rest_speech_text: Strong stance—drive through your heels.
steps: 1. Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width, toes slightly pointed out.
2. Hold dumbbells in front of your hips with palms facing your body.
3. Push hips back and bend knees to lower the dumbbells toward the floor.
4. Keep your chest up and spine neutral.
5. Drive through your heels to return to standing, squeezing your glutes at the top.
exercises.tips:
Keep your chest up and back straight
Push through your heels and squeeze your glutes at the top
Keep the dumbbells close to your body
Engage your core throughout the lift

exercises.title: Arm Raise
exercises.description: This strength exercise primarily targets the shoulders and also engages the traps and upper arms.It’s effective for building upper body strength, improving posture, and enhancing stability in daily movements.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Lifting the dumbbells too high
Shrugging the shoulders
Using heavy weights
Leaning forward or arching the back
Holding the breath during the lift
exercises.rest_speech_text: Sit tall, keep your shoulders down, and get ready to lift the dumbbells to the sides with control.
steps: 1. Sit tall on a chair with feet flat on the floor, dumbbells in each hand resting by your sides.
2. Keep your back straight and shoulders rolled back and down.
3. With a slight bend in the elbows, slowly raise both arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height.
4. Pause briefly at the top.
5. Slowly lower the dumbbells back down to the starting position.
exercises.tips:
Keep the core engaged and back straight 
Raise dumbbells only to shoulder height, no higher
Exhale while lifting, inhale while lowering
Choose light to moderate weights for proper form.
Perform the motion slowly

exercises.title: Pigeon Pose
exercises.description: Pigeon Pose is an stretching exercise. It involves folding one leg in front of the body while extending the opposite leg straight behind. This pose improves hip flexibility, reduces lower back tension.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Forcing the front leg into a full 90-degree angle.
Leaning heavily to one side.
Collapsing the upper body 
Letting the back leg angle outward
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next is Pigeon Pose. Bring one leg forward and stretch the other behind. Lean forward to deepen the hip stretch.
exercises.slow_down_phrases: Slower, to feel the stretch fully.
steps: 1. Start sitting on the mat with your right leg bent and your left leg extended back.
2. Bend forward and pull your bent leg between your arms.
3. Then lean back and straighten your leg and lift it behind your back.
exercises.tips:
Keep your hips square and level with the floor.
Relax your upper body and breathe deeply.
Go only as far as is comfortable.

exercises.title: Burpee
exercises.description: Burpees are a full-body exercise that build strength, burn fat, and improve endurance. Start standing, drop into a squat, kick your feet back to a plank, jump them in, then jump up high. Repeat with energy and control.
exercises.common_mistakes: Poor body alignment, jumping too hard, not using your core, landing too stiff, skipping the full squat or plank, and rushing through the movement. Stay controlled, use full range, and keep good form.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Time to rest. Next up—Burpees! Start standing, drop to a squat, kick back to plank, jump in, and leap up.
steps: 1. Start in a standing position with your feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Bend your knees and place your hands on the ground in front of you, shoulder-width apart.
3. Jump both feet back at the same time into a plank position, with your arms straight and your body forming a straight line from your head to your heels.
4. Perform a push-up, lowering your chest towards the ground and then pushing back up.
5. Jump both feet back towards your hands, landing in a squat position.
6. From the squat position, jump up as high as you can, reaching your arms overhead.
7. Land softly and immediately return to the squat position to perform the next rep.
exercises.tips: Focus on maintaining proper form throughout the exercise, keeping your back straight and your core engaged. If you're new to burpees, you can modify the exercise by removing the push-up or the jump at the end of the movement.

exercises.title: Squats
exercises.description: Squats are a basic lower-body exercise that strengthens your thighs, hips, and butt. You lower your body like you're sitting in a chair, then stand back up. It improves strength, balance, and posture.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Knees move too far forward past toes
Heels lift off the floor
Rounding the back or leaning too far forward
Knees cave inward
Going too fast or shallow
exercises.rest_speech_text: Get ready for squats. Stand tall, feet shoulder-width apart, and prepare to lower
steps: 1.  Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart
2. Extend your arms in front for balance or place hands on your hips
3. Push your hips back and bend your knees
4. Lower down as if you're sitting into a chair — thighs as parallel to the floor as possible
5. Keep your chest up and your back straight
6. Knees should not pass your toes
7. Press through your heels to stand back up
exercises.tips:
Keep your chest lifted and back straight
Push your hips back
Keep your feet flat and heels on the ground
Knees should stay in line with your toes
Go slow

exercises.title: Rowing Machine
exercises.description: The Rowing Machine is a full-body, low-impact cardio and strength exercise that engages the legs, glutes, back, shoulders, and arms while activating the core. It improves cardiovascular endurance, muscular endurance, coordination, and posture, making it an excellent functional fitness tool.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the back during the stroke
Overreaching with the arms instead of driving with the legs
Leaning too far back or hunching forward
Pulling too quickly and using momentum instead of controlled strokes
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a deep breath, reset your posture, and get ready to row smoothly and powerfully with full-body control.
steps: 1. Sit on the rowing machine with feet strapped in and hands gripping the handle.
2. Start with knees bent, torso slightly forward, and arms extended.
3. Push through the legs to straighten them while leaning back slightly.
4. Pull the handle toward your lower chest, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
5. Reverse the movement in order: arms → back → legs to return to the starting position.
6. Repeat for the desired number of strokes or time.
exercises.tips:
Drive first with the legs, then follow with the back and arms
Maintain a straight back and tight core throughout
Return smoothly in reverse order: arms → back → legs
Keep a consistent, controlled rhythm for both endurance and strength benefits

exercises.title: Hip Thrust with Stretched Leg
exercises.description: Hip Thrust with Stretched Leg involves lying flat on your back with one leg extended and the other bent. This exercise targets the glutes, hamstrings, and core, and increases demand on balance.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching the lower back
Letting the extended leg drop
Lifting the hips unevenly
Not engaging the glutes
Rushing through reps without control
exercises.rest_speech_text: Hip Thrust with Stretched Leg. Lie on your back, bend one knee, and stretch the other leg straight up. Lift your hips by pressing through the grounded foot.
steps: 1. Lie on your back, bend one leg, and other leg extended straight and off the ground
2. Press through your right heel to lift your hips off the ground.
3. Keep your extended leg in line with your torso throughout the lift.
4. Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower slowly back down.
5. Switch legs
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight and pelvis stable
Focus on driving through the heel of the grounded foot
Your extended leg should remain straight and in line with your torso
Move slowly, squeezing the glutes at the top

exercises.title: Extended Arm Circles Out
exercises.description: This exercise helps warm up your shoulders and arms by making big circles with your arms extended to the sides. It improves shoulder mobility, increases blood flow, and prepares your upper body for other exercises.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Moving arms too fast and losing control
Bending the elbows instead of keeping arms straight
Shrugging or raising shoulders toward ears
exercises.rest_speech_text: Relax. Now stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and stretch your arms out, make slow big circles, keep your shoulders relaxed
steps: 1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and extend your arms parallel to the floor.
2. Stretch arms out to shoulder height
3. Make big slow circles outward with your arms.
exercises.tips:
Move slowly and smoothly
Keep your arms fully extended
Relax your shoulders down

exercises.title: Frog Jump
exercises.description: Frog Jump performing explosive jumps forward and then backward. This challenges your lower body muscles—quads, glutes, hamstrings, and calves—plus your core for stability and balance.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Hands moving
Insufficient squat depth before jumping
Knees caving inward on landing
Losing balance when jumping backward
exercises.rest_speech_text: Frog Jumps forward and backward. Squat deep, then jump forward explosively, land softly, then jump backward
steps: 1. Stand with feet wider than hip-width apart, toes slightly turned out.
2. Lower your hands behind your hips and keep them relaxed.
3. Lower into a deep squat, keeping chest up and knees tracking over toes.
4. Explosively jump forward as far as comfortable, landing softly on the balls of your feet with knees bent.
5. Without pausing, explosively jump backward to your starting point, again landing softly with bent knees.
exercises.tips:
Keep your hands relaxed
Maintain a deep squat before each jump
Land softly onyour feet, with knees bent
Keep chest lifted and core engaged for stability
Focus on controlled, balanced jumps

exercises.title: Bridge Kick
exercises.description: The Bridge Kick is an exercise that strengthens the glutes, hamstrings, and core while also enhancing hip stability and control. Starting in a glute bridge position, you lift your hips off the ground and then extend one leg at a time.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Dropping the hips during the kick
Arching the lower back
Kicking too quickly and losing control
Not engaging the core or glutes
Wrong weight distribution on the supporting foot
exercises.rest_speech_text: Get into bridge position. Lift one leg and kick it straight—keep your hips high.
steps: 1. Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat on the ground, and arms by your sides.
2. Press through your heels and lift your hips into a glute bridge.
3. Engage your core and extend one leg straight out and slightly upward—this is the “kick.”
4. Hold briefly, then return the leg to the starting position without lowering your hips.
5. Repeat with the opposite leg, alternating sides.
exercises.tips:
Squeeze your glutes and keep hips level 
Move slowly and extend the leg fully,
Keep your core tight to prevent back arch
Use a yoga mat or soft surface to protect the spine
Focus on even control on both sides

exercises.title: Cycle Kicks
exercises.description: Cycle Kicks combines core work with dynamic flexibility. While lying flat with legs extended, you alternately bend one knee and reach the opposite arm toward that leg’s toes. It targets abs, obliques, and hip flexors.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Lifting the shoulders using impulse
Letting the extended leg hover too low
Pulling on the neck or twisting with force
Moving too fast without control
Holding breath
exercises.rest_speech_text: Lie on your back, legs extended. Bend one leg, and reach the opposite hand toward the toes. Get ready to alternate sides
steps: 1. Lie on your back with your arms bent and your head raised.
2. Bend your right knee and simultaneously reach your left arm toward your right leg.
3. Extend your right leg back out and bend the left leg, reaching toward it with your right arm.
4. Continue alternating sides in a slow, cycling motion.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight
Focus on smooth, controlled motion, not speed
Point your toes slightly and engage the quads
Keep breathing steadily

exercises.title: Rotation Resistance
exercises.description: This exercise helps strengthening shoulder muscles, improves upper body coordination and mobility and engages core muscles for stability
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rotating the torso instead of just arms
Using impulse rather than muscle control
exercises.rest_speech_text: Rest time. For the next exercise extend arms forward, rotate your arms side to side with control
steps: 1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, arms extended straight in front, palms together
2. Rotate your arms to the right side
3. Rotate your arms back to center, then to the left side.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight and back straight
Focus on controlled, smooth arm rotation
Keep elbows extended 
Breathe naturally throughout the exercise

exercises.title: Tiger
exercises.description: The Tiger exercise begins in an all-fours position and targets the glutes, hamstrings, and lower back while promoting spinal mobility and balance. This exercise enhances hip mobility, strengthens glutes and core
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching the lower back when lifting the leg
Swinging the leg 
Straining the neck
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Tiger. Start on all fours. Extend one leg back, bend the knee and return. Then switch legs.
exercises.slow_down_phrases: Gently return to the starting position before repeating the exercise with the other leg.
steps: 1. Get on all fours – hands under shoulders, knees under hips.
2. Extend your right leg back until it’s parallel to the floor.
3. Squeeze your glutes and hold briefly.
4. Bend the knee and return the leg to the starting position.
5. Repeat the movement with your left leg.
exercises.tips:
Engage your core for stability
Move the leg with control
Keep your head in line with the spine

exercises.title: Dumbbell Bench Press
exercises.description: The Dumbbell Bench Press is a classic upper-body strength exercise that targets the chest, shoulders, and triceps. It improves muscle balance, shoulder stability, and control through a greater range of motion. This exercise also develops core stability, lumbopelvic control, and anti-extension strength.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching the lower back excessively
Lowering the dumbbells too far or too quickly
Letting the elbows flare out too wide
Using uneven arm movement or grip imbalance
Bouncing the weights off the chest
exercises.rest_speech_text: Brace your core, keep control, and get ready to press with power.
steps: 1. Sit on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand resting on your thighs.
2. Lie back and bring the dumbbells to the sides of your chest, palms facing forward.
3. Engage your core and stabilize your shoulder blades against the bench.
4. Exhale as you press the dumbbells upward until your arms are fully extended.
5. Pause briefly at the top without locking the elbows.
6. Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back to chest level under control.
exercises.tips:
Keep your feet flat on the floor and your core engaged
Maintain a slight natural arch in your lower back
Lower the dumbbells slowly and under control
Keep your wrists aligned with your forearms
Exhale as you press up, inhale as you lower

exercises.title: Dumbbell Front Raise
exercises.description: The Dumbbell Front Raise strengthens and isolates the front (anterior) deltoids, improving shoulder definition, posture, and lifting stability. It also enhances control and coordination of the upper body, supporting performance in pressing and overhead movements.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Swinging the dumbbells with momentum
Lifting too high or locking elbows
Leaning back during the raise
Using weights that are too heavy for control
exercises.rest_speech_text: Raise with control, no swinging.
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, holding dumbbells at your sides.
2. With palms facing down, lift both dumbbells in front of you to shoulder height.
3. Pause briefly, keeping your arms parallel to the floor.
4. Lower the dumbbells slowly to the starting position.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight and back straight
Raise the dumbbells only to shoulder height
Move slowly and with control—avoid using momentum
Exhale as you lift, inhale as you lower

exercises.title: Back Shoulders Warm up
exercises.description: This warm-up gently activates and relax your shoulders, upper back, neck, and shoulder blades. It prepares your muscles and joints for movement and helps reduce stiffness or injury risk.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Moving too fast
Holding your breath
Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears
Using too much effort
Overstretching
Not engaging the back muscles
exercises.rest_speech_text: Let’s warm up your back and shoulders. Start with gentle rolls and circles—breathe easy and loosen up.
steps: 1. Stand or sit with your spine tall and your shoulders relaxed.
2. Raise your hands and place your palms on your shoulders.
3. Start performing backward rotations.
exercises.tips:
Move slowly and stay relaxed.
Keep your shoulders away from your ears.
Breathe deeply—don’t hold your breath.
Stand tall with good posture.

exercises.title: C Stretch
exercises.description: C Stretch is an exercise that increases flexibility along the side body. This exercise targets the obliques, lats, and hip abductors and adds balance challenge.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Twisting the torso instead of side bending
Leaning too far and losing balance
Not aligning the arm close to the ear
Letting the back or hips rotate
Locking the knees or arching the lower back
exercises.rest_speech_text: Cross one leg in front, raise your opposite arm, and bend sideways to stretch your side body
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet together.
2. Cross your right leg in front of your left leg, keeping both feet flat and parallel.
3. Raise your left arm overhead, palm facing inward and bicep near your ear and lean to the left
4. Hold for 15–20 seconds, keeping your core engaged and both legs steady.
5. Return to center and switch sides.
exercises.tips:
Keep your feet flat and weight balanced
Engage your core to control the lean
Focus on reaching up and over, not just sideways
Keep your shoulders relaxed
Perform slowly and with intention

exercises.title: Cat Cow Stretch
exercises.description: The Cat Cow Stretch is a gentle, flowing movement between two yoga poses — Cat and Cow — performed on hands and knees. It promotes spinal flexibility, relieves tension in the back and neck, and improves posture and breathing.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Moving too fast without control
Letting the shoulders shrug towards the ears
Dropping the belly too far
Not synchronizing breath with movement
Tensing the face or neck
exercises.rest_speech_text: Come to all fours, arch your back up, then down as you breathe slowly and fully.
steps: 1. Start on all fours, with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
2. Breathe in as you drop your belly, lift your chest and tailbone upward — this is Cow Pose.
3. Breathe out as you round your back toward the ceiling, tucking your chin to your chest — this is Cat Pose.
4. Continue moving slowly between Cat and Cow with each breath.
exercises.tips:
Move slowly and with control
Keep your neck neutral and relaxed
Stack shoulders over wrists and hips over knees

exercises.title: Threading the Needle
exercises.description: Threading the Needle is an exercise performed on all fours. It helps improve spinal mobility, releases tension in the upper back and shoulders, and promotes relaxation.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting hips twist too much 
Holding breath during the movement
Moving too fast
Dropping the head or neck uncomfortably
exercises.rest_speech_text: Rest time. Get on all fours. Lift one arm and thread it under your body, twist spine gently.
steps: 1. Start on all fours with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
2. Breathe in and lift your right hand off the ground.
3. Breathe out and thread your right arm under your left arm, lowering your right shoulder and ear gently to the floor.
4. Hold the stretch for 15–30 seconds while breathing deeply.
5. Slowly return your arm back to the starting position
6. Repeat on the other side.
exercises.tips:
Keep hips stable
Breathe deeply and steadily
Move slowly and with control
Keep the supporting arm strong and avoid collapsing into the floor

exercises.title: Downward Facing Dog
exercises.description: Downward Facing Dog is a foundational yoga pose that stretches and strengthens multiple muscle groups throughout the body. It promotes spinal elongation, opens the shoulders, calves, hamstrings, and strengthens the arms and core.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the back
Locking or hyperextending the knees
Shoulders shrugged up toward ears
Weight placed too far forward on hands
Not engaging the core and legs
exercises.rest_speech_text: Downward Facing Dog. Start on hands and knees, lift your hips toward the ceiling, straighten your legs as much as comfortable.
steps: 1. Begin on hands and knees, with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
2. Move your toes under and lift your hips toward the ceiling, straightening your legs as much as comfortable.
3. Hold the position for 20–30 seconds while breathing steadily.
4. Slowly lower your hips back to hands and knees.
exercises.tips:
Keep spine long by lifting hips high and pushing heels toward the floor
Maintain slight bend in knees if hamstrings are tight
Engage core to support the spine
Breathe deeply and steadily

exercises.title: Sky Touching
exercises.description: A gentle full-body stretch where you stand tall and extend your arms upward as if trying to touch the sky. Helps improve posture, flexibility, and circulation.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching the lower back too much.
Lifting shoulders towards the ears.
Holding breath while stretching.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a break. In the next one, stand tall, raise your arms up to the sky, stretch gently, and breathe.
steps: 1. Stand upright with feet hip-width apart and engage your core and relax your shoulders.
2. Lift your hands up, cross your fingers and bend your arms in a straight line.
3. Slowly lower your arms back down.
exercises.tips:
Keep your spine long and neutral.
Breathe deeply—breathe in as you raise, breathe out as you hold or lower.
Keep knees slightly soft.

exercises.title: Push Ups
exercises.description: Push-Ups strengthen the chest, shoulders, triceps, and core. To do them, start in a plank position with hands shoulder-width apart. Lower your body by bending your elbows, then push back up to the starting position, keeping your body straight throughout. Great for building upper body strength and endurance.
exercises.common_mistakes: Allowing your hips to sag. Letting your elbows flare out. Not going low enough. Allowing your head to drop. Dropping your head.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a break. For the next exercise get in a plank position with your hands shoulder-width apart and your fingers pointing forward
steps: 1. Start in a plank position with your hands shoulder-width apart and your fingers pointing forward.
2. Lower your body by bending your elbows and keeping your back straight. Your chest should touch the floor or come close to it.
3. Push your body back up by straightening your arms and returning to the starting position.
exercises.tips: Keep your elbows tucked in and your body in a straight line throughout the exercise to maximize effectiveness and prevent injury. Focus on controlling your movement and maintaining proper form rather than speed or quantity of reps.

exercises.title: Table Pose
exercises.description: Start in the classic Table Pose (on hands and knees, back flat). From there, perform reverse push-ups. This exercise strengthens the triceps, shoulders, and core while maintaining spinal alignment.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting hips lift too high
Not keeping elbows close to the body
Using impulse instead of controlled movement
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next:Table Pose. From Table Pose, bend elbows and lower hips back, then push up
steps: 1. Start in Table Pose: hands under shoulders, knees under hips, back flat.
2. Slowly bend elbows and lower hips backward toward heels
3. Stop before hips touch the ground.
4. Push through your hands to return to the starting Table Pose.
exercises.tips:
Lower yourself slowly and push up with control
Keep elbows tucked close to your sides
Engage your core

exercises.title: Wide Leg Burpees
exercises.description: Wide Leg Burpees are a dynamic full-body exercise that combines a traditional burpee with a wide leg stance during the jump and squat phases. This exercise boosts cardiovascular fitness, strength, and agility by engaging multiple muscle groups.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting knees collapse inward
Not maintaining a flat back during the plank
Rushing through the movement
Landing heavily
exercises.rest_speech_text: Time to rest. Start standing, drop into wide squat, plank down, jump back wide.
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet wider than shoulder-width apart.
2. Squat down, placing hands on the floor in front of you.
3. Jump feet back to plank position, keeping your body straight.
4. Jump feet forward back to wide squat position.
5. Explosively jump up, reaching arms overhead.
exercises.tips:
Keep knees tracking over toes when squatting wide
Maintain a strong core 
Land softly with bent knees
Control your breathing, breathe out on the jump

exercises.title: Back Stretch with Towel
exercises.description: This dynamic back mobility and shoulder flexibility exercise involves lying on your stomach while holding a towel. It targets the upper back, shoulders, and promotes better scapular movement and posture.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Bending elbows too early or flaring them out
Lifting the chest or head off the floor
Holding the breath
Using impulse instead of controlled motion
exercises.rest_speech_text: Lie on your stomach, arms stretched forward with the towel. Slide the towel slowly back toward your neck — feel your upper back stretch.
steps: 1.Lie face down with your arms extended forward, holding a towel with both hands, shoulder-width apart.
2. Keep your head down and neck relaxed, look toward the floor.
3. Engage your back and slowly move your hands (with towel) from the overhead position back toward your neck.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blades together gently as the towel nears your neck.
5. Hold briefly, then return the towel forward to the starting position.
exercises.tips:
Keep elbows soft but extended throughout the movement
Engage core and glutes to stabilize your lower body
Move the towel slowly and smoothly
Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades as you pull back

exercises.title: Double Leg Half Squat
exercises.description: Double Leg Half Squat is an exercise where you squat halfway down while holding a chair for support. It strengthens your thighs, glutes, and improves balance, making.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Knees going past the toes
Leaning forward too much
Not keeping heels on the ground
Using arms too much for support
exercises.rest_speech_text: Before the next exercise,stand tall, hands on the chair, lower halfway down, keep your back straight, then stand back up.
steps: 1.Stand behind a sturdy chair, feet shoulder-width apart and place both hands lightly on the back of the chair
2.Slowly bend your knees and lower into a half squat
3. Stop when thighs are halfway to parallel
4. Push through your heels to stand up
exercises.tips:
Keep your back straight and chest up
Push hips back, like sitting in a chair
Keep your weight in your heels
Use the chair only for light support

exercises.title: Seated Calf Raise
exercises.description: The Seated Calf Raise is a lower-leg strength exercise performed while sitting. It primarily targets the soleus muscle, which lies underneath the gastrocnemius in the calf. This move improves ankle stability, enhances walking and running power, and supports balance and lower-body strength.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Bouncing or using momentum
Not using full range of motion
Leaning too far back or slouching
Letting heels drop too quickly
Not keeping feet flat on the floor during start position
exercises.rest_speech_text: You’re building strength and endurance in the muscles that support every step you take. Rise with control, lower with purpose.
steps: 1. Sit tall with feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
2. Press through the balls of your feet to lift your heels up, squeezing your calves at the top.
3. Lower your heels slowly and repeat with control.
exercises.tips:
Keep a tall posture, engage your core
Pause briefly at the top of the lift for better contraction
Perform slowly and with control

exercises.title: Plank Toe Touch
exercises.description: Plank Toe Touch combines plank stability with dynamic core movement. From a plank position, you reach with one hand to touch the opposite foot, alternating sides. This works your core, stretches the hamstrings and shoulders.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Dropping the hips or arching the back
Rushing the movement
Not actually reaching toward the toe
Excessive hip rotation
exercises.rest_speech_text: Rest. From plank, reach one hand to the opposite toe. Alternate sides while keeping your core tight and the movement controlled.
steps: 1. Start in a high plank position with your hands under shoulders and body straight.
2. Reach your right hand toward your left toe, lifting your hips slightly.
3. Return to plank.
4. Repeat by reaching your left hand to your right toe.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight
Match the movement with your breath
Try to keep the hips level
Move with control

exercises.title: Eagle Pose
exercises.description: The Eagle Pose is performed while sitting on a chair and focuses solely on the arms. With arms crossed at chest level, you gently pulse them upward and back down. This movement helps activate and stretch the shoulders and upper back.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Lifting shoulders toward ears
Slouching or leaning back in the chair
Using impulse instead of controlled motion
Not maintaining the cross in the arms
exercises.rest_speech_text: Break Time. Cross your arms at chest level. Gently pulse them up and down while keeping your shoulders relaxed and back straight.
steps: 1. Sit tall in a chair with feet flat on the floor and back straight.
2. Cross your right arm over your left at the elbows.
3. Bend the elbows, bringing the backs of your hands or palms together.
4. With your shoulders relaxed, gently lift the crossed arms a few inches upward.
5. Lower the arms back to chest level.
exercises.tips:
Sit up tall with your feet flat on the floor
Keep shoulders relaxed and spine straight
Move arms in a slow and controlled manner
Breathe steadily during the movement

exercises.title: Triangle Pose
exercises.description: Triangle Pose is an exercise that stretches and strengthens the legs, hips, and spine while improving balance and flexibility. This pose helps open the hips and chest, lengthens the spine, and relieves tension.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Leaning forward
Bending the front knee excessively
Collapsing the chest forward 
Overextending the neck
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a break. Stand wide, reach one arm down, the other up, forming a triangle
steps: 1. Stand with feet wide apart, about 3–4 feet distance.
2. Turn your right foot out and left foot slightly in.
3. Extend arms parallel to the floor at shoulder height.
4. Reach your right hand down toward your right ankle.
5. Extend your left arm straight up toward the ceiling
6. Hold the pose, breathing deeply for 20-30 seconds
7. Return to standing and repeat on the other side
exercises.tips:
Keep both legs straight
Engage your core
Keep shoulders stacked vertically

exercises.title: Jumping Squats
