exercises.description: Jumping Squats are an exercise that combines a squat with an explosive jump. This exercise strengthens your legs, glutes, and improves cardiovascular fitness, balance, and coordination.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Not landing softly
Letting knees cave inward during landing or squat
Bending forward too much
Not fully extending hips
exercises.rest_speech_text: Rest and stand with arms behind your neck. Squat down, then jump up explosively. Land softly and repeat
steps: 1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, hands behind your neck.
2. Lower into a squat by bending knees and hips, keeping chest up.
3. Explosively jump straight up, extending hips fully.
4. Land softly on your toes, immediately lowering back into squat.
exercises.tips:
Land quietly on the balls of your feet
Keep your core tight and chest up
Use controlled movements, not just speed
Ensure knees track over toes

exercises.title: Barbell Front Squat
exercises.description: The Barbell Front Squat targets the quads, glutes, hamstrings, and core while improving upright posture and knee stability. Holding the bar in front engages core stability, lumbopelvic control, and anti-extension strength, helping maintain proper spinal alignment and reducing lower-back stress.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting elbows drop forward
Leaning too far forward
Allowing knees to cave inward
Using momentum instead of controlled movement
exercises.rest_speech_text: Chest tall, elbows up—squat controlled and strong.
steps: 1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, barbell resting on the front shoulders.
2. Keep elbows high and chest upright.
3. Push hips back and squat down until thighs are parallel to the floor.
4. Press through the heels to return upright.
5. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
exercises.tips:
Keep chest up and elbows high
Sit back and down, keeping weight on your heels
Engage your core throughout the squat
Lower slowly and push through the heels to rise

exercises.title: Forward Fold
exercises.description: Forward Fold include moving your upper body and arms lowering down with arms reaching toes. It helps open the shoulders, lengthen the spine, and deepen the stretch through the hamstrings and calves. This dynamic stretch enhances flexibility and posture.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the back
Forcing the hands to touch toes,
Shrugging shoulders when arms are overhead
Holding breath.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Forward Fold. Reach up tall, then hinge forward at your hips, lowering arms toward your toes.
steps: 1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, knees slightly bent.
2. Extend both arms overhead with palms facing forward, fingers reaching up actively.
3. Breathe out and hinge at the hips, folding forward, lowering your upper body and arms toward your toes.
4. Lower your arms as far as comfortable, resting hands on shins, ankles, or toes.
5. Hold the stretch for 20–30 seconds, breathing deeply.
6. To rise, engage your core and roll up slowly.
exercises.tips:
Maintain a long spine as you hinge forward from the hips
Lower arms gently toward toes, shins, or ankles
Relax your neck 
Breathe deeply and steadily 
Roll up slowly

exercises.title: Close Grip Pulldown
exercises.description: The Close Grip Pulldown targets the latissimus dorsi, biceps, and middle back while emphasizing elbow and shoulder control. The close grip increases bicep engagement and promotes better posture and upper-body pulling strength, supporting functional lifts like rows and pull-ups.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Leaning excessively backward or using momentum
Pulling the bar behind the neck
Flaring elbows outward instead of keeping them close
Not fully extending arms at the top
exercises.rest_speech_text: Relax your arms, stand tall, brace your core, and get ready to pull down with control and focus on your back.
steps: 1. Sit at the pulldown machine with thighs secured under the pads.
2. Grip the bar with hands close together, palms facing you (underhand grip).
3. Pull the bar down toward your upper chest, keeping elbows close to your torso.
4. Squeeze your back muscles, then slowly return the bar to the starting position.
5. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
exercises.tips:
Keep your chest tall and core engaged
Lead the movement with your elbows, not your hands
Pause and squeeze your lats at the bottom of the pull
Control the bar as you return to the starting position

exercises.title: Reverse Lunges
exercises.description: Reverse lunges are a functional lower-body exercise that builds strength, stability, and coordination. In this move, you step backward with one leg while lowering both knees to around 90 degrees. The primary effort comes from the front leg, especially the glutes and quads.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Front knee goes beyond the toes
Leaning the upper body forward
Losing balance when stepping back
Not lowering enough into the lunge
exercises.rest_speech_text: Now we’ll do reverse lunges. Stand tall and get ready to step back while keeping your torso stable. We’ll begin in a few seconds
steps: 1.Stand upright with your feet hip-width apart, hands on your hips or in front of you.
2.Step backward with your right leg, lowering into a lunge.
3.Your front knee should be at a 90-degree angle, directly over the heel.
4.Lower your back knee toward the floor, but don’t let it touch.
5.Push through the front foot to return to standing.
6.Repeat on the other leg.
exercises.tips:
Start standing tall, shoulders relaxed, core lightly engaged.
As you step backward, lower your back knee toward the floor, stopping just short of touching it.
The front leg should bear most of your weight, heel grounded.
The front shin remains vertical — the knee shouldn’t pass the toes.
Keep your torso upright throughout — avoid leaning forward or arching the lower back.
Push through the heel of the front foot to return to standing.

exercises.title: Triceps Stretch
exercises.description: This stretch helps loosen and lengthen the triceps muscles at the back of your upper arms, improving flexibility and reducing muscle tightness.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting your shoulders rise up toward your ears.
Pulling too hard causing pain.
Bending the wrist awkwardly.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Triceps Stretch. Reach one arm overhead, bend your elbow, and gently pull it down.
steps: 1. Raise one arm overhead and bend the elbow so your hand reaches down your back
2. Use your other hand to gently pull the bent elbow toward your head.
3. Hold the stretch for 20–30 seconds.
4. Relax and switch arms.
exercises.tips: Keep your back straight and avoid leaning forward or arching.

exercises.title: Kettlebell Single Arm Row
exercises.description: The Kettlebell Single Arm Row strengthens the lats, rhomboids, and biceps while improving upper-body stability and posture. Performing it one side at a time enhances core stability, lumbopelvic control, and anti-rotation strength, supporting a stable trunk during pulling movements.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Twisting the torso or jerking the kettlebell
Letting the shoulder drop on the working side
Overextending at the top of the movement
Using momentum instead of controlled motion
exercises.rest_speech_text: Brace your core—pull strong and controlled.
steps: 1. Place one knee and same-side hand on a bench or sturdy surface, holding a kettlebell in the opposite hand.
2. Keep your back flat and core tight.
3. Pull the kettlebell toward your hip, squeezing your back muscles.
4. Pause briefly, then lower the kettlebell under control.
5. Complete reps on one side, then switch arms.
exercises.tips:
Keep your back flat and core engaged
Pull the kettlebell toward your waist, leading with the elbow
Lower slowly and control the descent
Maintain a neutral neck and head position

exercises.title: Wide Leg Squats
exercises.description: Wide Leg Squats are a lower-body strength exercise where you stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart and squat down by bending your knees and pushing your hips back. This targets your inner thighs, glutes, quads, and hamstrings.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Knees collapsing inward
Leaning too far forward with the torso
Not squatting deep enough
Heels lifting off the floor
exercises.rest_speech_text: Stand with feet wide, toes slightly out. Squat down, keeping your knees over toes and chest up.
steps: 1.  Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width apart, toes pointing slightly outward.
2. Engage your core and keep your chest lifted.
3. Slowly bend your knees and push your hips back to lower into a squat.
4. Keep your knees aligned with your toes, don’t let them collapse inward.
5. Lower until your thighs are parallel to the ground or as low as comfortable.
6. Push through your heels to return to standing.
exercises.tips:
Keep your chest up and back straight
Push your knees outward, tracking over your toes
Keep your weight on your heels

exercises.title: Hamstring Stretch
exercises.description: This stretch targets the hamstring muscles using a torniquet. Performed lying on your back, it gently lengthens the back of the leg, improving flexibility, relieving tightness, and supporting lower back health.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Bending the lifted knee
Using jerky or forceful movements
Lifting the hips off the ground
Holding the breath
exercises.rest_speech_text: Lie on your back, loop the torniquet around your foot, and gently pull your leg upward. Feel the stretch in the back of your thigh.
steps: 1. Lie flat on your back with both legs extended.
2. Loop a torniquet around the sole of your right foot.
3. Holding the ends with both hands, gently lift your right leg upward.
4. Keep the leg straight and the opposite leg flat on the floor.
5. Hold the stretch for 15–30 seconds.
6. Slowly lower the leg and switch sides.
exercises.tips:
Keep the opposite leg flat and relaxed on the floor
Breathe slowly and evenly
Keep your neck and shoulders relaxed

exercises.title: Adductor Machine
exercises.description: The Adductor Machine isolates the inner thigh muscles (adductors), improving hip stability, leg control, and balance. Strengthening the adductors supports knee alignment, athletic movements, and overall lower-body strength.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Using excessive weight and relying on momentum
Leaning backward or forward during the movement
Moving too quickly through the range of motion
Not fully squeezing at the end of the movement
exercises.rest_speech_text: Relax your legs, stand tall, engage your core, and get ready to squeeze with control.
steps: 1. Sit on the adductor machine with legs on the pads.
2. Adjust the machine so the starting position is comfortable.
3. Slowly bring your legs together, squeezing the inner thighs.
4. Return to the starting position under control.
5. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
exercises.tips:
Adjust the machine to fit your leg width comfortably
Keep your back straight and core engaged
Move slowly, focusing on squeezing the inner thighs
Exhale while bringing legs together, inhale while returning

exercises.title: Sitting Full Stretch
exercises.description: Sitting Full Stretch is a flexibility-focused exercise designed to stretch your hamstrings, spine, and shoulders. This exercise promotes overall mobility and can be used as part of a warm-up or cool-down.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the spine excessively
Holding the breath
Bouncing to reach further
Locking the knees too tightly
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a break. Lean forward from the hips, extend your arms, and slowly reach for your toes. Breathe into the stretch.
steps: 1. Sit tall on a mat with legs extended straight in front of you.
2. Start with hands bent at your sides, elbows relaxed.
3. Slowly lean forward from the hips.
4. Extend your arms as you go forward, reaching for your toes.
5. Hold the stretch for a few seconds, breathing deeply.
6. Return slowly to the upright position.
exercises.tips:
Keep your back long and hinge from the hips
Breathe out as you reach forward
Keep the movement slow and steady

exercises.title: Seated Core Twist
exercises.description: This exercise involves rotating the torso from side to side while keeping the legs and hips stationary. It targets the core muscles, particularly the external obliques, improving spinal flexibility, core strength, and balance.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Moving or twisting hips and legs
Rounding or slouching the back
Using fast, uncontrolled movements
Holding breath
exercises.rest_speech_text: Rest. Relax your shoulders, breathe deeply, and prepare for the next controlled twist
steps: 1. Sit on a mat with legs extended straight forward, arms extended to your sides
2. Slowly rotate your torso to the right, turning your head to follow the movement.
3. Pause briefly at the end of the twist, feeling the stretch and contraction and return to the center
4. Slowly rotate your torso to the left side, again turning your head with your torso.
exercises.tips:
Keep your spine long and chest lifted
Engage your abdominal muscles
Move slowly and with control
Maintain steady and deep breathing

exercises.title: Rear Delt Machine
exercises.description: The Rear Delt Machine targets the posterior deltoids and upper back muscles, including the traps and rhomboids. It improves shoulder stability, posture, and upper-back strength while enhancing overall shoulder symmetry and functional pulling movements.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Using momentum or swinging the arms
Lifting too high or shrugging the shoulders
Leaning forward or backward excessively
Not keeping elbows slightly bent throughout the motion
exercises.rest_speech_text: Relax your shoulders, brace your core, and get ready to pull back smoothly, focusing on your rear delts.
steps: 1. Sit on the rear delt machine with chest against the pad and arms holding the handles.
2. Keep a slight bend in your elbows.
3. Pull the handles backward in an arc, squeezing the rear delts and upper back.
4. Slowly return to the starting position under control.
5. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
exercises.tips:
Maintain a straight back and tight core
Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout the movement
Move slowly and under control, focusing on the contraction of the rear delts
Pause briefly at the peak for maximum engagement

exercises.title: Back Forth Jump
exercises.description: The Back Forth Jump increases the intensity and muscular involvement of the standard jump, making it ideal for athletic training, or lower-body strength circuits.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Landing with locked knees instead of squatting
Letting knees cave inward during the squat
Rounding the back in the squat position
Jumping too far and losing form
Not engaging core while jumping
exercises.rest_speech_text: Get ready for the exercise. Jump forward and back, land into a squat each time. Stay strong and controlled
steps: 1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, knees slightly bent.
2. Jump forward, landing directly into a controlled squa
3. Hold the squat briefly, then jump backward, again landing into a squat.
4. Continue jumping forward and back, squatting each time you land.
exercises.tips:
Land each jump directly into a controlled squat
Keep your chest up and back straight in the squat
Keep feet hip-width apart for stability
Engage your core and glutes throughout

exercises.title: Dumbbell Hammer Curl
exercises.description: The Dumbbell Hammer Curl strengthens the biceps and forearms while improving grip and arm stability. Holding the dumbbells in a neutral grip reduces wrist strain and promotes balanced arm development. It also builds core stability and anti-extension control, enhancing posture and coordination during upper-body movements.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Swinging the dumbbells with momentum
Lifting elbows away from the body
Not controlling the lowering phase
Arching the back or shrugging shoulders
exercises.rest_speech_text: Stay strong and steady—get ready to curl with control
steps: 1. Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
2. Keep your core engaged and elbows close to your torso.
3. Curl the dumbbells upward toward your shoulders while keeping palms facing in.
4. Pause briefly, then lower the weights slowly back down.
exercises.tips:
Keep your elbows tight to your sides
Curl the weights slowly and with control
Maintain a neutral wrist position
Engage your core throughout the motion

exercises.title: Turning 180 Jump Squats
exercises.description: Turning 180 Jump Squats are an exercise where you perform a squat, then jump explosively while rotating your body 180 degrees in the air before landing softly into the squat position again. This move improves explosive power, agility, balance, and lower body strength.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Not landing softly
Allowing knees to cave inward
Not engaging core
Incomplete squat depth
exercises.rest_speech_text: Rest. Squat down, jump and turn 180 degrees, land softly and squat again
steps: 1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Squat down, keeping chest up and knees aligned over toes.
3. Explosively jump straight up, rotating your body 180 degrees in mid-air
4. Land softly with knees bent, facing the opposite direction.
5. Immediately go into the next squat and repeat the jump turn.
exercises.tips:
Land with knees slightly bent
Keep your chest up and core engaged
Use arms to help with the jump and rotation
Focus on a controlled landing

exercises.title: Beginner Burpee
exercises.description: A Beginner Burpee combines a squat, a step-back to plank, and a stand-up without jumping. It helps build strength, mobility, and cardio endurance in a safe and easy way.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Dropping the hips too low in plank
Rounding the back when squatting down
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Beginner Burpee. Squat, step back, step forward, and stand up tall."
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Squat down and place your hands on the floor.
3. Step one foot back, then the other, to get into a plank position.
4. Step one foot forward, then the other, to return to squat position.
5. Stand up (no jump).
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight when stepping into plank.
Use your hands for balance.
Start slow, then build speed.

exercises.title: Hip Thrust
exercises.description: Hip thrusts strengthen your glutes (butt muscles) and hips. You lie down on the ground, feet flat on the ground, and thrust your hips upward. It’s great for building power and shaping your lower body.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Lifting with your lower back instead of your glutes
Feet too far forward or too close to your body
Hyperextending (arching) the lower back at the top
Not going high enough — hips don’t reach full extension
exercises.rest_speech_text: Get ready for hip thrusts. Lie down on your back, bend your knees and get ready to lift your hips up.
steps: 1. Lie on the floor, on your back, with your knees bent, feet flat and shoulder-width apart
2.  Press through your heels and lift your hips up
3. At the top, pause for a moment until your body forms a straight line
4.  Lower your hip slowly back
exercises.tips:
Press through your heels, not your toes.
Keep your chin tucked and your ribs down.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top.
Don't arch your back too much.
Keep your knees and toes pointed forward.

exercises.title: Toe Touch Walk
exercises.description: Toe Touch Walk focuses on lifting your bent leg out to the side while reaching with the opposite hand toward the lifted foot. It helps improve hip mobility, balance, and coordination.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Leaning the torso too much forward or sideways
Not bending the knee enough when lifting the leg
Moving too fast and losing balance
exercises.rest_speech_text: Relax. For the next exercise Bend the leg and lift sideways to reach opposite hand
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, hands relaxed at your sides.
2. Bend your right knee and lift your leg and reach left hand
3. Lower your right foot back to the floor.
4. Repeat on the left side
exercises.tips:
Keep your upper body upright and stable
Control the leg lift, avoid swinging it too forcefully
Focus on steady breathing and controlled movements

exercises.title: Kettlebell Swing
exercises.description: The Kettlebell Swing is a dynamic full-body exercise that targets the glutes, hamstrings, quads, core, lats, and shoulders while improving power, endurance, and hip hinge mechanics. It develops core stability, lumbopelvic control, and anti-extension strength, making it excellent for athletic performance and functional fitness.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the back or shoulders
Using arms to lift instead of driving with the hips
Overextending or leaning back at the top
Incorrect grip or letting the kettlebell swing uncontrollably
exercises.rest_speech_text: Shake out your arms, reset your grip, brace your core, and get ready to hinge strong for the next swing.
steps: 1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, kettlebell on the floor in front of you.
2. Hinge at the hips, bend knees slightly, and grip the kettlebell with both hands.
3. Swing the kettlebell back between your legs.
4. Drive your hips forward, engaging glutes and core, to swing the kettlebell up to chest or shoulder height.
5. Let the kettlebell swing back down under control and repeat.
exercises.tips:
Hinge at the hips, not the knees
Snap the hips forward to drive the kettlebell upward
Engage your core and keep your back neutral
Maintain a controlled swing, letting momentum come from the hips

exercises.title: Side Kick Squats
exercises.description: Side Kick Squats combine a traditional squat with a lateral leg kick. This movement strengthens the glutes, quads, and hamstrings, while also engaging the obliques and improving balance and coordination.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting the knees collapse inward during the squat
Kicking too high and losing balance
Rounding the back during the squat
Not returning to a strong standing position before kicking
Rushing the movement without control
exercises.rest_speech_text: Squat down, then as you stand, kick one leg to the side. Keep your core tight and stay balanced.
steps: 1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, hands in front of your chest or on your hips.
2. Lower into a squat, pushing hips back and keeping your chest up.
3. As you rise, shift weight to one leg and kick the opposite leg to the side.
4. Bring the leg back down to standing position.
5. Lower back into a squat and repeat, kicking with the other leg.
exercises.tips:
Keep your weight in your heels during the squat
Kick to the side with control, not force
Keep your chest up and shoulders relaxed
Look straight ahead to help with balance

exercises.title: Ball in Ball
exercises.description: Ball in Ball is a stretch exercise where you curl your upper body forward while seated. This movement helps relieve tension in the back and neck, promotes spinal flexibility, and calms the nervous system.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rushing through the motion
Shrugging shoulders toward ears
exercises.rest_speech_text: Break time.Sit on the chair, curl forward like a ball, then open up wide— your arms and chest.
steps: 1. Sit on a chair, keep your back straight.
2. Lower your upper body forward, bringing hands together in front of your legs
3. Pause briefly, then raise your torso slightly while stretching both arms to the sides at shoulder height
4. Open the chest gently as you lean slightly back.
5. Return to starting position and repeat.
exercises.tips:
Move slowly and with control
Keep feet flat and stable
Stretch arms naturally to the sides, not too high

exercises.title: Hip Thrust Foot to Foot
exercises.description: Hip Thrust Foot to Foot performed lying on your back, with one ankle resting on the opposite knee. It’s a powerful movement ideal for glute activation, mobility, and injury prevention.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Not keeping the hip level during the thrust
Letting the raised leg fall
Lifting with the lower back instead of the glutes
Allowing the heel to come off the ground
Moving too fast
exercises.rest_speech_text: Hip Thrust Foot to Foot. Lie on your back, bend both knees, and rest one ankle over the opposite knee. Press through the grounded foot to lift your hips.
steps: 1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
2. Cross your right ankle over your left knee.
3. Place your arms by your sides for stability.
4. Press through your left heel to lift your hips off the floor.
5. At the top, squeeze your glutes and keep your hips square.
6. Slowly lower back down with control.
exercises.tips:
Engage your core
Push through the heel of the supporting foot
Keep the raised leg steady and flexed
Squeeze your glutes at the top of each rep
Keep the motion slow and controlled

exercises.title: Incline Chest Press
exercises.description: The Incline Chest Press targets the upper chest while also engaging the shoulders and triceps. It helps develop upper-body strength, improves pushing power, and enhances the definition of the upper pectorals. The incline angle mimics an overhead press pattern, promoting better posture and balanced chest development.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Lifting the shoulders off the pad during pressing
Using too much weight and losing control
Locking out the elbows at the top
Allowing wrists to bend backward
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a breath, keep your chest up and core tight—get ready to press strong and steady through the upper chest.
steps: 1. Adjust the seat so the handles are at upper-chest level.
2. Sit with your back and head supported and feet flat on the floor.
3. Grip the handles slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
4. Press the handles upward until your arms are almost straight.
5. Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position with control.
exercises.tips:
Keep your back and head firmly against the pad
Exhale as you press up, inhale as you return
Focus on smooth, controlled movements
Keep your wrists straight and elbows slightly bent at the top

exercises.title: Kneeling Hamstring Stretch
exercises.description: Kneeling Hamstring Stretch increases the stretch by incorporating a hip shift backward and forward reach with the arms. This exercise increase flexibility and range of motion.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the back excessively
Not shifting hips backward far enough
Locking the knee forcefully
Letting the front foot rotate outward
Reaching too far and losing balance
exercises.rest_speech_text: Rest. Shift your hips back and keep the front leg straight. Reach toward your toes with both hands.
exercises.slow_down_phrases: Focus on stretching the muscles evenly and without sudden movements.
steps: 1. Begin in a half-kneeling position—left leg forward, right knee on the floor.
2. Straighten your left leg in front of you with the heel on the ground and toes pointing up.
3. Shift your hips back over your rear knee.
4. Keep your spine long and arms extended forward toward your left toes.
5. Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing steadily.
6. Slowly return to the start and switch legs.
exercises.tips:
Shift your hips back slowly until you feel the stretch
Maintain your front leg fully extended with toes up
Hold the stretch steadily
Keep your shoulders relaxed and arms extended

exercises.title: Cross Abs
exercises.description: Cross Abs is an abdominal exercise performed while lying on your back. It involves bringing one shoulder toward the opposite knee in a controlled crunching motion. This move targets the obliques, enhancing core definition and rotational strength.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Pulling on the neck with your hands
Using impulse instead of core strength
Lifting the lower back off the ground
Rushing the movement
Not fully engaging the obliques
exercises.rest_speech_text: Lie on your back, hands behind your head. Crunch one shoulder toward the opposite knee. Get ready to switch sides.
steps: 1. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet off the ground
2. Place your hands lightly behind your head, elbows wide.
3. Engage your core and lift your right shoulder and left knee toward each other, rotating the torso.
4. Repeat on the opposite side, lifting your left shoulder and right knee toward each other
exercises.tips:
Keep your elbows wide
Move slowly to engage your core
Focus on lifting the shoulder blade
Breathe out as you crunch for better core engagement
Keep lower back lightly touching the floor

exercises.title: Double Horse Kick
exercises.description: The Double Horse Kick is a dynamic bodyweight move that combines a low squat with two quick back kicks. It's great for improving leg strength, balance, and core stability.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting the knees cave inward during squat
Arching the back during kicks
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Double Horse Kick. Get low in a wide squat, then kick both legs back quickly. Stay strong and stable
steps: 1. Place a chair in front of you and, bending over, put your palms on the seat.
2. Put one leg on the floor with a slight bend in the knee, bend the other knee and lift it up behind your back.
3. Then pull your leg back imitating a horse kick so that it becomes straight.
4. Smoothly return to the starting position and pull it back sharply for greater amplitude.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight to protect your lower back.
Land lightly on your feet.
Move with control, not just speed.

exercises.title: Dumbbell Curl
exercises.description: The Dumbbell Curl is a fundamental arm exercise that strengthens and defines the biceps while improving grip and forearm stability. Performing it with dumbbells enhances muscle balance and coordination between arms. It also develops core stability and anti-extension control, supporting better posture and trunk alignment.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Swinging the weights with momentum
Lifting the elbows forward or upward
Not fully extending the arms at the bottom
Rounding the shoulders or arching the back
exercises.rest_speech_text: Keep your form tight—get ready to curl with control.
steps: 1. Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
2. Engage your core and keep your elbows tucked in.
3. Curl the dumbbells upward toward your shoulders without swinging.
4. Pause at the top, then lower slowly back to the starting position.
exercises.tips:
Keep elbows close to your body
Move slowly and under control
Exhale while curling up, inhale while lowering
Maintain a stable, upright posture

exercises.title: Swallow Pose
exercises.description: Swallow Pose is a dynamic balance and flexibility exercise. Standing tall, you shift your weight onto one leg, raise the opposite leg behind you, and lower one arm toward the floor. This movement strengthens your glutes, hamstrings, lower back, and improves balance and body control.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Bending the standing leg too much
Tilting the torso too far forward
Not controlling the arm and leg movement
Losing balance
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next, Swallow Pose. Stand tall, lift one leg back, lower one arm down. Get ready to switch sides
steps: 1. Stand tall with your feet together, arms by your sides.
2. Shift your weight onto your left leg.
3. Lift your right leg straight behind you while lowering your left arm toward the floor.
4. Hold briefly, then return to the starting position and switch sides
exercises.tips:
Move slowly and with control.
Engage your core to stabilize.
Don’t raise the leg too high

exercises.title: Thoracic Vertebrae Stretch
exercises.description: This exercise strengthens and stretches the thoracic spine and upper back muscles. Lying on your back with knees bent and stationary stabilizes your lower body, while sliding your arms upward toward the knees and lifting your head and shoulders activates the core and improves thoracic mobility.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Moving knees 
Lifting head and shoulders too high.              Holding breath
Not engaging abdominal muscles
exercises.rest_speech_text: Rest. Lie on your back, knees bent and still. Slide arms upward as you lift head and shoulders.
steps: 1. Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat, knees together and still.
2. Place arms extended by your hips, palms facing down.
3. Slowly slide your arms up toward your knees while simultaneously lifting your head and shoulders off the floor.
4. Hold the position briefly for 10 seconds
5. Slowly lower your head, shoulders, and arms back to the starting position.
exercises.tips:
Keep knees on the ground
Move arms slowly and with control
Lift head and shoulders gently
Keep breathing smooth and steady
Engage core

exercises.title: Knee Pull Out
exercises.description: Knee Pull Out is an dynamic exercise performed sitting on a chair, focusing on extending the legs alternately. This exercise helps improve knee joint mobility, strengthens the quadriceps.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Using hands to assist leg extension for both legs
Not fully extending the leg
Moving too quickly
Slouching or leaning back
exercises.rest_speech_text: Sit straight, place hands on one knee and extend the leg, then extend the other leg without using your hands
steps: 1. Sit on a chair with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
2. Place both hands on your right knee.
3. Slowly extend your right leg straight out in front of you, using your hands to assist if needed.
4. Without using your hands, immediately extend your left leg straight out.
5. Return both legs to the starting position.
exercises.tips:
Sit upright with your back straight and feet flat 
Use your hands only to assist the first leg extension
Extend legs smoothly
Keep breathing steadily

exercises.title: Penguin Stretch
exercises.description: Penguin Stretch a seated stretch that targets the upper back and shoulders while adding a gentle side-to-side movement. This helps increase mobility in the spine and stretches the muscles along the sides of your torso.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Leaning too far 
Shrugging shoulders up toward ears
Slouching or rounding the lower back
Moving the head away from the spine alignment.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Up next, Penguin Stretch with side lean. Sit tall, squeeze shoulder blades, then gently lean side to side
steps: 1. Sit upright on a chair with your feet flat on the floor.
2. Slowly lean your upper body slightly to the right side, keeping your spine straight and neck aligned.
3. Return to the center.
4. Repeat the lean slowly to the left side.
exercises.tips:
Keep feet flat on the floor and sit tall before leaning
Move slowly and controlled
Maintain gentle squeeze of shoulder blades 
Keep the neck neutral and aligned with your spine

exercises.title: Chair Dips
exercises.description: Chair Dips involve facing away from a sturdy chair, placing your hands behind you on the seat, and lowering your back by bending your elbows. This primarily targets the triceps, shoulders, and upper back, helping to improve upper-body strength and flexibility.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Flaring elbows out too far
Lowering too deeply and straining shoulders
Using impulse rather than control
Letting hips sag or arch excessively
exercises.rest_speech_text: Rest time. Place your hands behind you on a chair, slowly lower your back by bending your elbows, then push back up. Keep it smooth and steady.”
steps: 1. Sit at the edge of a sturdy chair and place your hands behind you on the seat, fingers facing forward.
2. Slide your hips slightly off the chair, keeping your feet flat and knees bent.
3. Begin with arms extended and body upright.
4. Slowly lower your back by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
5. Go as low as feels comfortable, then press through your palms to raise your back to the starting position.
exercises.tips:
Keep your elbows close to your body 
Lower your torso slowly and stop at a comfortable depth
Engage your core and glutes for better control
Make sure the chair is stable and won’t tip

exercises.title: Lunge with Jump
exercises.description: Lunge with Jump is an that combines a forward lunge with a jump to switch legs. This exercise improves lower body strength, power, coordination, and cardiovascular fitness.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Landing with stiff legs or locked knees
Knees going too far past toes during lunge
Not controlling landing
Arms not moving opposite to legs or staying static
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a break. Stand tall,jump up into a squat, swing arms opposite to legs, land softly, repeat
steps: 1. Stand tall, feet hip-width apart, arms relaxed.
2. Step forward into a lunge with your right leg
3. Jump explosively up, switching to a squat position
4. Swing your left arm forward and right arm back as you jump.
5. From the squat, step back or reset to standing.
6. Repeat on the other side, alternating legs and arm swings.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core engaged for stability
Land softly with bent knees
Coordinate arm and leg movements smoothly for balance
Maintain upright posture and avoid leaning forward

exercises.title: Side Skiing
exercises.description: Side Skiing focuses on controlled lateral movements without jumping. The movement enhances coordination, balance, and muscular endurance, especially in the legs and core.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Not fully returning to the starting position
Letting the chest collapse forward
Extending the arm too far back or not in sync with the leg
Sloppy or rushed movement
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next up: Side Skiing – slide your leg out as you lower down the opposite hand.
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart, hands bent and pressed lightly against your chest.
2. Slide your right foot to the side while simultaneously extending your left hand downward.
3. Return your right foot and left hand to the starting position.
4. Repeat on the opposite side
exercises.tips:
Keep your core engaged throughout
Move slowly and with control
Slide your foot lightly across the floor – avoid lifting
Synchronize your arm and leg movements

exercises.title: Windmill
exercises.description: The Windmill is a dynamic movement that strengthens the core, improves flexibility in the hamstrings and hips, and enhances shoulder stability.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Bending the front knee.
Rounding the back instead of keeping it straight.
Letting the shoulder drop instead of keeping it stacked over the other.
Twisting too much from the lower back.
exercises.rest_speech_text: Relax time. Stand tall, stretch one arm up, then reach down to the opposite foot with the other. Keep your core tight and move with control
steps: 1. Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width and raise one arm straight overhead, keeping the other at your side.
2. Push hips to the side opposite the raised arm and slowly lower your free arm to the inside of the opposite foot.
3. Return to standing. Switch sides.
exercises.tips:
Keep both legs straight, but not locked.
Move slowly and control the descent.
Engage your core to protect the lower back.

exercises.title: Side Bridge
exercises.description: The Side Bridge is a core-strengthening exercise that targets the obliques, hips, and shoulders. It helps improve stability, balance, and spinal alignment and engages deep abdominal muscles and is great for enhancing core endurance and posture.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting the hips drop
Rotating the body forward or backward
Placing the elbow too far from the shoulder joint
exercises.rest_speech_text: Side Bridge. Lie on your side, place your elbow under your shoulder, lift your hips off the floor, and hold your body straight like a plank.
steps: 1. Lie on your side with legs extended and stacked.
2. Place your elbow directly under your shoulder.
3. Engage your core and lift your hips until your body forms a straight line.
4. Hold the position for a set time or do controlled repetitions by lowering and lifting the hips.
5. Switch sides and repeat.
exercises.tips:
Keep your body in a straight line from head to feet
Engage your glutes and core
Place your elbow directly under your shoulder

exercises.title: Leg Extension Gym
exercises.description: The Leg Extension is an isolation exercise that targets the quadriceps, helping improve knee strength, stability, and muscle definition. It allows controlled activation of the quads while minimizing load on the hips and lower back.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Using momentum instead of controlled movement
Locking the knees at the top of the movement
Lifting the hips off the seat
Moving too quickly through the range of motion
exercises.rest_speech_text: Relax your legs, reset your feet, engage your core, and get ready to extend with control.
steps: 1. Sit on the leg extension machine with feet under the pad.
2. Adjust the backrest and ankle pad for comfort and proper alignment.
3. Extend your legs fully without locking the knees.
4. Lower the weight slowly back to the starting position.
5. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
exercises.tips:
Adjust the machine pad so it rests just above the ankles
Keep back and hips pressed against the seat
Lift slowly and lower under control
Exhale while extending and inhale while returning

exercises.title: Squat with Ball
exercises.description: Squat with Ball is a lower-body strengthening exercise where you place a stability or medicine ball between your lower back and a wall, then perform squats in a controlled manner.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting knees pass the toes
Lifting heels off the ground
Allowing the ball to shift too high or low
Leaning forward
Moving too quickly
exercises.rest_speech_text: Break Time. Stand tall with the ball on your back, squat slowly, press through the heels, and return up
steps: 1.Stand with your back against a wall, placing a ball between your lower back and the wall.
2. Slowly squat down, keeping your back straight and knees above the ankles.
3. Push through your heels to return to standing.
exercises.tips:
Keep knees aligned over ankles
Push through your heels when rising
Engage your core throughout
Lower slowly and avoid sudden movements

exercises.title: Pulse Crunches
exercises.description: Pulse crunches are small, controlled lifts of the upper body from a lying position. Unlike standard crunches, this variation focuses on short, frequent movements up and down near the top of the range. It targets the upper abdominal muscles and helps build core endurance.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Jerking 
Lifting the entire back
Neck strain from trying to reach forward
Holding your breath
exercises.rest_speech_text: Break. Lie on your back, bend your knees, place your hands on your thighs. You’ll do small crunches by sliding your hands toward your knees.
steps: 1. Lie on your back, bend your knees, and place feet flat on the floor.
2. Put your hands on your thighs with slightly bent elbows.
3. Engage your abs and lift your shoulders off the floor.
4. Do small pulsing crunches, sliding hands up toward your knees.
exercises.tips:
Keep your chin slightly lifted
Focus on squeezing your abs
Keep movements short and quick
Maintain steady breathing

exercises.title: Barbell High Bar Squat
exercises.description: The Barbell High-Bar Squat is a classic lower-body strength exercise that primarily targets the quads, glutes, and hamstrings while engaging the core and lower back for stabilization. The bar rests higher on the upper traps, keeping the torso more upright compared to a low-bar squat.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting the knees cave inward
Rounding the lower back at the bottom of the squat
Rising onto the toes
Allowing the chest to drop forward
Using excessive weight and sacrificing form
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a deep breath, tighten your core, and get ready to squat strong.
steps: 1. Position the barbell across your upper traps, not your neck.
2. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width and lift it off the rack.
3. Step back, feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly turned out.
4. Inhale deeply, brace your core, and begin to lower by bending your hips and knees.
5. Keep your chest up and descend until your thighs are parallel (or slightly below parallel) to the floor.
6. Push through your heels to return to the starting position, exhaling as you rise.
exercises.tips:
Keep your chest up and back straight
Push your knees out as you descend
Sit back slightly, keeping your heels flat on the floor
Breathe in on the way down, exhale as you push up
Maintain a controlled pace

exercises.title: Side Step Toe Taps
exercises.description: Side Step Toe Taps is cardio and coordination exercise. It's great for warming up, improving lateral movement, and engaging multiple muscle groups including legs, glutes, and core.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Bending too much at the back instead of the hips
Letting knees collapse inward
Moving too fast and losing form
Not engaging the core for stability
exercises.rest_speech_text: Step side to side, tap your toes, and keep your core tight. Focus on smooth, controlled movement.
steps: 1. Stand with your feet hip-width apart and arms relaxed at your sides.
2. Step your right foot out to the side.
3. Tap your right foot with your right hand or reach near it.
4. Return to center and repeat movement with opposite leg and hand
exercises.tips:
Keep your chest lifted and spine neutral
Step wide enough to feel the stretch and activation
Use controlled movement, don’t rush
Engage your core to support your balance

exercises.title: Barbell Bent Over Row
exercises.description: The Barbell Bent-Over Row is a compound strength exercise that targets the upper and middle back, including lats, traps, rhomboids, and rear delts, while also engaging the biceps and core for stability. It improves posture, increases pulling strength, and enhances overall upper-body development.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the back
Using momentum or jerking the bar upward
Pulling the bar too far toward the chest or belly
Letting elbows flare outward excessively
Lifting the head or looking forward
exercises.rest_speech_text: Breathe deeply… engage your core… get ready to pull with your back.
steps: 1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, barbell on the floor in front of you.
2. Hinge at the hips and slightly bend your knees, keeping your back straight.
3. Grip the barbell with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width, palms facing down.
4. Pull the bar toward your lower chest/upper abdomen, keeping elbows close to your body.
5. Pause at the top, squeezing the back muscles.
6. Slowly lower the bar to the starting position with control.
exercises.tips:
Keep your back flat and core engaged throughout the movement.
Hinge at the hips, maintaining a slight bend in the knees
Pull the bar toward your lower chest or upper abdomen
Pause briefly at the top
Lower the bar slowly with control

exercises.title: Dumbbell Twisting Curl
exercises.description: The Dumbbell Twisting Curl targets the biceps while incorporating a rotational movement to engage the forearms and improve grip strength. It also enhances core stability and anti-rotation control, supporting proper posture and coordination during upper-body movements.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Swinging the dumbbells with momentum
Allowing elbows to drift forward or outward
Rotating the wrists too early or too late
Arching the back or losing core engagement
exercises.rest_speech_text: Core tight, elbows in—twist and curl with control.
steps: 1. Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
2. Keep elbows close to your torso.
3. Curl the dumbbells upward while rotating your wrists so palms face upward at the top.
4. Pause briefly, then slowly lower to the starting position with wrists returning to neutral.
5. Repeat for the desired number of reps.
exercises.tips:
Keep elbows tucked close to your torso
Twist your wrists naturally from neutral to supinated as you curl
Move slowly and under control
Maintain a tight core throughout the exercise

exercises.title: Overhead Press
exercises.description: The Overhead Press is a classic strength exercise focusing on the shoulders and upper body. It improves shoulder strength, stability, and mobility, engages the triceps and upper chest.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching the lower back excessively 
Flaring elbows out too wide or forward
Not fully extending the arms overhead
Locking out the elbows
exercises.rest_speech_text: Rest. Prepare for Overhead Press. Stand tall, engage your core, and press your arms straight overhead with control.
steps: 1. Hold a barbell or dumbbells at shoulder level with your palms facing forward.
2. Start with your hands at shoulder height, elbows bent and close to your body.
3. Press your arms upward overhead in a controlled motion until fully extended.
4. Slowly lower your arms back to the starting position.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core engaged
Control the movement up and down slowly
Keep feet shoulder-width apart and grounded

exercises.title: Seated Row
exercises.description: The Seated Row strengthens the back muscles, primarily the lats, traps, and rhomboids, while also engaging the biceps and rear shoulders. It improves posture, upper-body pulling strength, and shoulder stability, making it essential for balanced back development and functional movements.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the back or leaning too far forward or backward
Using momentum instead of controlled movement
Pulling with the arms instead of leading with the elbows
Not fully extending the arms at the start
exercises.rest_speech_text: Relax your arms, brace your core, and get ready to pull back strong and controlled, leading with your elbows.
steps: 1. Sit at the row machine with feet planted and knees slightly bent.
2. Grip the handle with both hands, arms fully extended.
3. Pull the handle toward your torso, leading with your elbows and keeping your back straight.
4. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end of the movement
5. Slowly return to the starting position under control
exercises.tips:
Sit tall with your chest up and core engaged
Lead the pull with your elbows, keeping them close to your body
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the peak contraction
Control the return phase without letting the weight stack slam

exercises.title: Dumbbell front Raises
exercises.description: Dumbbell Front Raises are a strength training exercise that targets the front deltoid muscles. This move involves lifting dumbbells straight in front of your body to shoulder height. It’s excellent for developing shoulder strength.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Swinging the weights
Bending the elbows too much
Lifting above shoulder level
Arching the back or leaning backward
exercises.rest_speech_text: Stand tall, engage your core. Slowly raise both dumbbells in front of you to shoulder height, then lower back with control.
steps: 1. Stand upright with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand by your thighs, palms facing your body.
2. Keep a slight bend in your elbows and engage your core.
3. Slowly lift both arms straight in front of you until the dumbbells reach shoulder height.
4. Pause briefly at the top.
5. Lower the dumbbells back down with control to the starting position.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core engaged
Use light weights to focus on form
Raise the dumbbells slowly and with control
Breathe out while lifting, breathe in while lowering

exercises.title: Barbell Stiff Leg Deadlifts
exercises.description: The Barbell Stiff Leg Deadlift is a powerful lower-body and posterior chain exercise that emphasizes the hamstrings and glutes while also strengthening the lower back. This movement enhances flexibility, balance, and strength in the posterior chain.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the lower back during the descent
Locking out the knees completely
Lowering the bar too far and losing tension in the hamstrings
Using excessive weight at the expense of form
Not keeping the barbell close to the legs
exercises.rest_speech_text: Brace your core, hinge from the hips, and get ready to feel the stretch through your hamstrings.
steps: 1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, holding a barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip.
2. Keep your knees only slightly bent and your back flat.
3. Engage your core and begin hinging at your hips to lower the barbell toward your feet.
4. Keep the bar close to your legs and your spine neutral as you lower until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
5. Pause briefly at the bottom without rounding your back.
6. Drive your hips forward to return to standing, squeezing your glutes at the top.
exercises.tips:
Maintain a slight bend in the knees
Keep the barbell close to your legs 
Hinge at the hips, not at the waist
Stop when you feel a deep stretch in the hamstrings
Control the movement both down and up

exercises.title: Bent Over Dumbbell Row
exercises.description: The Bent Over Dumbbell Row is a classic strength exercise that targets the back muscles—especially the lats, rhomboids, and traps—while also engaging the biceps and core. It helps improve posture, upper-body pulling strength, and muscular balance between the left and right sides.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the back or hunching the shoulders
Jerking the weights or using momentum
Letting the elbows flare out too wide
Not engaging the core, leading to instability
Dropping the weights quickly without control
exercises.rest_speech_text: Brace your core, hinge forward, and get ready to row strong.
steps: 1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
2. Bend slightly at the knees and hinge forward at the hips until your torso is almost parallel to the floor.
3. Keep your back flat, neck neutral, and core tight.
4. Let the dumbbells hang at arm’s length below your shoulders.
5. Exhale and pull both dumbbells up toward your waist, keeping your elbows close to your body.
6. Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
7. Slowly lower the weights back to the starting position under control.
exercises.tips:
Keep your back straight and chest lifted
Focus on pulling with your elbows, not your hands
Maintain a tight core to stabilize your spine
Control both the upward and downward phases
Exhale as you pull, inhale as you lower

exercises.title: Interval Squat with Hanging
exercises.description: This exercise combines a traditional squat with a static hold using a ball placed between your back and a wall for support. It targets your quads, glutes, and core, helping to build lower-body strength and endurance.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Knees going past toes during squats
Letting the back arch or round away from the ball
Rising too quickly without control
Not engaging the core during the hold
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a break and stand tall, lower into a squat, hold steady, then rise up strong.
steps: 1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, ball behind your back against a wall.
2. Lower into a squat, keeping your back against the ball and thighs parallel to the floor.
3. Hold the squat for a few seconds.
4. Push through your heels to return to standing.
exercises.tips:
Keep knees aligned with toes
Push through your heels when standing
Maintain constant contact with the ball
Breathe steadily and don’t hold your breath during the hang

exercises.title: Chair Head Sway
exercises.description: Chair Head Sway is a gentle neck mobility and relaxation exercise performed while seated. It helps release tension in the neck muscles, improves cervical spine flexibility, and promotes better posture.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Moving too quickly or abruptly
Using the shoulders instead of the neck muscles
Overextending the neck beyond comfortable range
Holding breath during movement
Poor seated posture during exercise
exercises.rest_speech_text: Sit tall in your chair and gently sway your head side to side to release neck tension.
steps: 1. Sit comfortably in a chair with your back straight and feet flat on the floor.
2. Slowly sway your head gently from side to side
3. Perform this sway for 20-30 seconds, breathing deeply.
4. Return your head to the center slowly.
exercises.tips:
Sit up straight with feet flat on the floor
Keep shoulders relaxed and down
Move your head slowly and gently side to side
Breathe deeply and evenly

exercises.title: Back Stretch
exercises.description: This stretch targets your entire back and shoulders, helping relieve tension and improve flexibility. Slowly bend forward from your hips, keeping your back straight, and bring your arms down.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the back excessively
Bending from the waist without hinging at hips
Forcing arms to cross
Moving too fast
exercises.rest_speech_text: Break Time. Reach your arms overhead, bend forward slowly and cross your arms in front. Feel the stretch across your back and shoulders.
steps: 1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, arms fully extended overhead.
2. Slowly bend forward from hips, keeping your spine straight.
3. As you bend, bring your arms down and cross them in front of you at shoulder height.
4. Hold the stretch for 15–30 seconds while breathing evenly.
5. Slowly return arms overhead and stand upright.
exercises.tips:
Hinge from your hips, not your lower back
Keep arms extended overhead at the start
Cross arms gently, avoid overstretching shoulders

exercises.title: Lying Butterfly
exercises.description: ying Butterfly is a gentle exercise focusing on shoulder mobility and upper back activation. It engages the muscles around the shoulder blades and upper back. This helps improve shoulder stability, posture, and upper body strength.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching the lower back excessively
Using impulse instead of controlled movements
Holding breath 
Lifting arms too high
exercises.rest_speech_text: Excellent work! Now lie on your stomach, arms extended to the sides, lift and lower your arms gently with control.
steps: 1. Lie face down on a comfortable surface with arms extended out to the sides, palms facing down.
2. Keep your legs relaxed and your neck neutral, looking down at the floor.
3. Engage your upper back and shoulders to lift your arms slightly off the ground.
4. Hold the lift briefly (1-2 seconds), then slowly lower your arms back down.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core engaged 
Perform slow, controlled lifts and lowers
Breathe steadily
Keep the neck relaxed

exercises.title: KB Lifting
exercises.description: KB Lifting involves lifting a kettlebell helps build strength in the arms, shoulders, legs, and especially the core. It also improves balance, and overall functional fitness.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the back
Lifting with arms only instead of using legs and hips
Jerking the weight instead of a controlled lift
Letting the kettlebell swing away from the body
exercises.rest_speech_text: Kettlebell lifting. Stand strong, hold the kettlebell tight, lift with control, and keep your core engaged
steps: 1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart with a kettlebell
2.Press the kettlebell straight up overhead by fully extending your arm.
3. Slowly lower the kettlebell back down to chest level
4. Switch the kettlebell to the other hand.
exercises.tips:
Keep your back straight and chest lifted
Drive through your legs and engage your core
Keep the kettlebell close to your body
Breathe out as you lift

exercises.title: Hip Stretch
exercises.description: The Hip Stretch helps improve flexibility and mobility in the hip joint and surrounding muscles, gently open and lengthen the hip flexors and glutes.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching the lower back
Tilting the torso forward or sideways
Pulling the foot too hard
exercises.rest_speech_text: Stand tall and grab your ankle behind you. Feel the stretch in your hip and thigh—don’t forget to breathe.
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
2. Shift your weight onto your left foot.
3. Bend your right knee and lift your right foot behind you and grab your right ankle with your right hand.
4. Gently pull your foot toward your glutes, keeping knees close together.
5. Hold for 20–30 seconds, breathing deeply.
6. Return and switch sides
exercises.tips:
Keep your knees aligned and close
Engage your core
Hold onto a chair or wall if needed
Keep your torso upright and relaxed

exercises.title: Wide Legged Bend
exercises.description: Wide Legged Bend is a standing stretch and strengthening exercise targeting the hamstrings, lower back, and inner thighs. Standing with feet wide apart and bending forward at the hips, it helps improve flexibility, promotes spinal mobility, and stretches the calves and hips.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the back excessively
Locking knees too rigidly
Feet not aligned parallel
Holding breath instead
exercises.rest_speech_text: Time to relax. Stand wide, bend forward at hips, keep back long, relax your neck.
steps: 1. Stand with feet wide apart, toes slightly turned forward.
2. Engage your core and slowly hinge forward at the hips, keeping your spine long.
3. Lower your torso toward the floor as far as comfortable, letting your hands rest on the floor.
4. Hold the position and breathe deeply.
5. Engage your core and slowly back to standing position
exercises.tips:
Keep spine long and hinge from the hips
Slightly bend knees if hamstrings are tight
Engage core to protect the lower back
Relax neck

exercises.title: Reverse Snow Angels
exercises.description: Reverse Snow Angels are performed lying on your stomach. With arms extended at your sides. This exercise engages your upper back, shoulders, and postural muscles.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Lifting the chest too much
Bending the elbows during the sweep
Moving too quickly
Letting arms rest on the ground
exercises.rest_speech_text: Lie on your stomach. Sweep your arms from sides to overhead in a wide arc, then return them slowly.
steps: 1. Lie flat on your stomach with legs extended and arms straight at your sides, palms facing the floor.
2. Slightly lift your arms off the ground while keeping them straight.
3. Slowly sweep your arms in a wide arc out to the sides and up near your ears, keeping them elevated.
4. Pause briefly when arms reach overhead.
5. Reverse the motion, bringing arms back down to the starting position.
exercises.tips:
Keep your forehead lightly touching the floor 
Engage your shoulder blades and lift arms slightly off the floor
Breathe steadily

exercises.title: Glute Kickback Machine
exercises.description: The Glute Kickback Machine targets the gluteus maximus and hamstrings, improving lower-body strength, hip stability, and balance. It helps shape and strengthen the glutes while enhancing posture and athletic performance through controlled hip extension.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Arching the lower back instead of engaging the glutes
Using momentum instead of controlled movement
Not fully extending the hip at the top
Shifting weight unevenly on the supporting leg
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a breath, reset your stance, brace your core, and get ready to drive the heel back strong.
steps: 1. Position yourself on the glute kickback machine with one foot on the platform and chest supported.
2. Engage your core and keep your spine neutral.
3. Push your working leg back and upward until your hip is fully extended.
4. Squeeze your glutes at the top, then slowly return to the start.
5. Complete all reps on one leg before switching sides.
exercises.tips:
Keep your torso stable and core tight
Focus on squeezing the glutes at the top of the movement
Move slowly and avoid swinging the leg
Control both the lift and the return phase

exercises.title: Inner Thigh Raises
exercises.description: Inner Thigh Raises are a floor-based leg exercise that targets the inner thigh muscles (adductors). They help strengthen the inner thighs, improve hip stability, and support better leg control.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Swinging the leg
Lifting too fast or too high
Rolling your hips backward
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: Inner Thigh Raises. Lie on your side and lift your bottom leg up and down
steps: 1. Lie on your side with legs extended and stacked.
2.Cross your top leg over the bottom one and place your foot flat on the floor in front of or behind the lower leg..
3. Keep your bottom leg straight and foot flexed.
4. Keep your bottom leg straight and foot flexed
5. Slowly lift the bottom leg toward the ceiling, using control
6. Lower it back down gently
7. Do all reps on one leg, then switch sides
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight to avoid rocking.
Move slowly — quality over speed.
Support your head with your hand or rest it on your arm.

exercises.title: Lateral Dumbbell Raises
exercises.description: Lateral raises are a strength exercise that works your shoulders — especially the side (lateral) deltoid muscles. You raise dumbbells out to your sides, helping build shoulder shape and strength.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Using too much weight
Shrugging your shoulders
Lifting above shoulder height
Locking the elbows
exercises.rest_speech_text: Next: lateral raises. Stand tall, dumbbells by your sides. Lift arms out to shoulder height with control
steps: 1. Stand tall with your feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Hold a dumbbell in each hand by your sides, palms facing inward.
3. Keep a small bend in your elbows — don’t lock them.
4. Slowly lift both arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height (your body forms a “T”
5. Pause briefly at the top
6. Lower the dumbbells slowly back down to your sides
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight and back straight.
Don’t swing the weights — move with control.
Raise to shoulder level only — no higher.
Breathe in as you lift, breath out as you lower.

exercises.title: Lying Leg Lift
exercises.description: Lying leg lift is performed with one leg bent for added lower back support and reduced intensity. One leg is raised while lying on your back with elbows bent at your sides. This exercise isolates the lower abdominal muscles, activates the hip flexors, and lightly engages the quads.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting the extended leg drop too quickly
Arching the back off the floor
Lifting the head or straining the neck
Holding breath during the motion
Using the arms
exercises.rest_speech_text: Lie on your back, relax, and focus on your breathing. When you're ready, prepare to smoothly lift your leg, keeping the movement controlled. Maintain a steady and calm pace
steps: 1. Lie on your back. Bend your left leg, placing the foot flat on the ground and the right leg extended on the floor
2. Bend your elbows and place your forearms flat on the floor beside your torso for stability.
3. Engage your core and slowly raise the extended right leg
4. Hold briefly at the top while keeping your abs tight.
5. Slowly lower the leg back to the floor
6. Repeat, then switch legs.
exercises.tips:
Keep the bent leg flat with foot grounded
Avoid arching the lower back
Move slowly and with control
Keep elbows gently pressed into the floor

exercises.title: Double Knee Lift
exercises.description: Double Knee Lift involves lifting one knee straight forward, lowering it, then lifting the same knee out to the side before switching legs. It helps activate the core, hip flexors, and glutes while enhancing balance and coordination.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Leaning the torso forward or sideways
Using impulse instead of slow movement
Letting the foot drag or not fully lifting the knee
Holding breath or stiffening shoulders
exercises.rest_speech_text: Stand straight, lift your knee forward and lower it, then lift the same knee to the side. Stay balanced and breathe steady.
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet hip-width apart and hands on your hips
2. Lift your right knee forward to hip height, then lower it back down.
3. From standing, lift your right knee out to the side, keeping the torso upright.
4. Lower the right leg back to the starting position.
5. Repeat the same sequence with your left leg
exercises.tips:
Keep your torso upright and shoulders relaxed
Engage your core
Lift your knee only as high as comfortable
Use slow, smooth movements for both directions
Breathe steadily

exercises.title: Backward Arm Circles
exercises.description: This exercise warms up the shoulders and upper back. Slowly make small circles moving your arms backward, engaging your shoulder muscles and improving mobility.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Using too large or too fast circles
Shrugging shoulders or tensing the neck
Arching the back
exercises.rest_speech_text: Rest. Stand tall. Extend your arms and circle them backward slowly and smoothly
steps: 1. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, arms outstretched to sides at shoulder height.
2. Keep arms straight and slowly rotate them backward in small controlled circles.
3. Continue circling backward for the desired time or repetitions.
exercises.tips:
Keep movements controlled and smooth
Start with small circles, gradually increasing size

exercises.title: Barbell Low Bar Good Morning
exercises.description: The Barbell Low-Bar Good Morning is a posterior-chain strength exercise that primarily targets the hamstrings, glutes, and lower back. With the bar positioned low on the traps or rear delts, this movement emphasizes the hip hinge pattern, improving hip stability, posterior strength, and overall control.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the back
Bending the knees too much
Using excessive weight and losing form
Dropping the chin or looking up, straining the neck
Rushing the movement
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a deep breath, brace your core, and get ready to hinge with control.
steps: 1. Position the barbell low on your upper back (on the rear delts/traps) and grip it firmly.
2. Stand with feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent.
3. Inhale, brace your core, and hinge at the hips while keeping your back straight.
4. Push your hips back until your torso is nearly parallel to the ground or you feel a deep stretch in the hamstrings.
5. Exhale and drive your hips forward, returning to the starting position.
6. Maintain control throughout — do not rush the lift.
exercises.tips:
Keep your core tight and your spine neutral 
Push your hips back rather than bending your knees forward                                                     Stop when you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings
Control both the descent and ascent
Engage your glutes and hamstrings to return to the starting position

exercises.title: Leg Lifting on Flow
exercises.description: Leg Lifting on Flow is an exercise that emphasizes abdominal engagement, hip flexor strength, and leg control. From a seated position you raise one leg at a time. This movement activates the lower abdominal muscles promoting postural stability and hip mobility.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting the spine collapse
Using impulse instead of controlled muscle effort
Holding breath during leg lift
Leaning too far backward
Bending knees during the lift
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a break. Sit on the floor with legs extended and arms behind you. Be ready to lift the leg
steps: 1. Sit on a mat with your legs extended forward.
2. Place your arms bent behind you, hands on the mat, palms facing forward for support.
3. Slowly lift one straight leg off the floor to a comfortable height.
4. Lower it back down with control and lift the other leg
exercises.tips:
Press your palms into the floor for stable support
Engage your core before lifting each leg
Move slowly and breathe out as you lift the leg
Keep your legs straight

exercises.title: Ball Stretch
exercises.description: The Ball Stretch is a gentle, dynamic stretch targeting the shoulders, spine, and upper back. Performed in a standing or kneeling position. It’s excellent for improving shoulder mobility, spinal flexibility, and posture.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Bending elbows instead of keeping arms straight
Letting the lower back sag excessively
Not aligning head with spine
Rushing through the motion
exercises.rest_speech_text: Place your hands on the ball, slowly slide it forward as you stretch your back and shoulders, then bring it back in.
steps: 1. Kneel behind the ball, feet or knees hip-width apart.
2. Place both hands on top of the ball in front of you.
3. Keeping your arms straight, slowly roll the ball forward while bending at the hips and lowering your upper body.
4. Stretch your spine and shoulders as your arms extend fully.
5. Pause for a moment at full extension while breathing deeply.
6. Slowly roll the ball back to the starting position.
exercises.tips:
Keep your spine long and hips aligned
Move the ball slowly to feel the stretch
Engage your core to support your back
Keep arms extended without locking elbows

exercises.title: Kettlebell Concentration Curl
exercises.description: The Kettlebell Concentration Curl isolates the biceps for maximum contraction and definition while improving mind-muscle connection. Using a kettlebell allows for a natural wrist rotation and better grip control. It also engages the core for stability and helps maintain anti-extension control during the movement.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Swinging the kettlebell instead of controlled lifting
Allowing the elbow to drift away from the thigh
Arching the back or leaning excessively
Not fully lowering the kettlebell to stretch the biceps
exercises.rest_speech_text: Elbow planted, core tight—curl with control and focus.
steps: 1. Sit on a bench with legs apart, holding a kettlebell in one hand.
2. Rest your working arm’s elbow on the inner thigh.
3. Curl the kettlebell upward toward your shoulder with control.
4. Pause at the top, then slowly lower it back to the starting position.
5. Complete reps on one arm, then switch sides.
exercises.tips:
Keep your working elbow fixed against your inner thigh
Curl the kettlebell slowly, focusing on the biceps contraction
Engage your core to maintain posture
Pause briefly at the top for maximum effect

exercises.title: Reachers
exercises.description: Reachers are a stretching and mobility exercise. Lie on your stomach and stretch your arms forward as if reaching for something. This exercise helps improve shoulder mobility, upper back strength, and core stability.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Reaching too fast
Locking the knees
Letting the shoulders tense up
exercises.rest_speech_text: Break. Lie on your stomach, reach your arms forward, lift chest gently, then relax down.
steps: 1.Lie flat on your stomach with your legs straight and toes pointing down.
2. Stretch your arms straight out in front of you, palms facing down.
3. Slowly lift your chest and arms a little off the ground, reaching forward.
4. Hold for 1-2 seconds while keeping your neck relaxed.
5. Slowly lower back down.
exercises.tips:
Don’t shrug your shoulders — keep them relaxed.
Focus on a smooth forward reach, not speed.
Keep your neck relaxed as you reach.

exercises.title: Side Lunge with Jump
exercises.description: The Side Lunge with Jump is a dynamic lower-body exercise that combines the benefits of a lateral lunge with an explosive jump. It targets the legs, glutes, and hips while improving power, balance, and cardiovascular fitness.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Knees collapsing inward during the lunge
Leaning too far forward or rounding the back
Jumping without control or landing hard
Not fully pushing off during the jump
exercises.rest_speech_text: Get ready for Side Lunge with Jump. Step out wide, lunge low, then explode up with a jump.
steps: 1. Stand up straight with your legs slightly bent at the knees.
2. Next, move your right leg behind your left leg and extend it backward.
3. Jump up and switch leg
exercises.tips:
Keep your chest up and back straight
Push through the heel of the lunging leg
Land softly on the balls of your feet with knees slightly bent
Use your arms to help with balance

exercises.title: Supported V Ups
exercises.description: Supported V-Ups are a core-strengthening exercise performed from a lying position, where both the upper body and legs lift simultaneously, forming a “V” shape.  This exercise strengthens the abdominal muscles, improves core stability, enhances coordination and flexibility
exercises.common_mistakes:
Jerking movements 
Not lifting the torso and legs high enough
Holding the breath
Arching the lower back excessively
exercises.rest_speech_text: Relax. Let's focus on strengthening your core with supported V-ups. Sit on the floor, hands behind you for support. Lift your legs and upper body, aiming to touch your toes. Remember to engage your core muscles and maintain steady breathing.
steps: 1. Lie on your back with legs extended and arms at your sides.
2. Engage your core and lift both legs and upper body at the same time.
3. Reach toward your feet while forming a V shape with your body.
4. Hold briefly at the top, then slowly lower down to starting position.
exercises.tips:
Engage your core
Move slowly and with control
Keep neck relaxed
Breathe out as you lift, breathe in as you lower

exercises.title: Burpee Squat Hold
exercises.description: The Burpee Squat Hold is a dynamic exercise that increases leg muscle endurance, builds core strength, and still delivers a cardiovascular challenge.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting the chest collapse during the squat hold
Not going low enough into the squat
Holding breath during the squat hold
Rushing through the transition without proper control
exercises.rest_speech_text: Time to rest. Drop into a burpee, then land in a deep squat and hold it. Stay strong and steady
steps: 1. Start in a standing position with your feet shoulder-width apart.
2. Bend your knees and place your hands on the ground in front of you, shoulder-width apart.
3. Jump both feet back at the same time into a plank position.
5. Jump both feet back towards your hands, landing in a squat position.
exercises.tips:
Keep your back straight and chest lifted in the squat hold

Engage your core and glutes throughout
Land with heels flat and knees aligned over toes
Hold the squat for at least 2–3 seconds to maximize benefits
Breathe steadily

exercises.title: Biceps Curl
exercises.description: The seated biceps curl strengthens the biceps at the front of the upper arms. Sitting on a chair helps isolate the biceps by reducing momentum from the lower body. This exercise improves arm strength, tone, and functional ability.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Lifting arms to the side
Lifting arms forward
Swinging the dumbbells instead of moving slowly
Letting elbows move away from the torso
Holding breath instead of breathing steadily
exercises.rest_speech_text: Sit tall, keep your elbows close, and get ready to curl the dumbbells with control.
steps: 1. Sit tall on a chair with feet flat on the floor, shoulder-width apart.
2. Hold a dumbbell.
3. Keeping your elbows close to your sides, slowly bend one arm and lift your hand weight toward your chest.
4. Lower slowly back to starting position and change the arms.
exercises.tips:
Sit tall with feet flat on the floor, shoulders relaxed
Keep elbows tucked to your sides
Lift slowly and control the weight
Exhale while lifting, inhale while lowering
Start with light weights to perfect form

exercises.title: Kettlebell Single Arm Reverse Lunge
exercises.description: The Kettlebell Single Arm Reverse Lunge strengthens the quads, glutes, and hamstrings while enhancing balance, coordination, and hip stability. Holding a kettlebell in one hand also engages core stability, lumbopelvic control, and anti-rotation strength, promoting upright posture and safe movement under load.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Letting the front knee go past the toes
Leaning forward or twisting the torso
Using the back leg to push off instead of the front heel
Losing balance during the lunge
exercises.rest_speech_text: Stand tall, core engaged—step back controlled and strong.
steps: 1. Stand upright holding a kettlebell in one hand at your side or front rack position.
2. Step backward with one leg, lowering until both knees are at ~90 degrees.
3. Keep your chest lifted and core engaged throughout.
4. Push through the front heel to return to the starting position.
5. Repeat for the desired reps, then switch legs and kettlebell hand.
exercises.tips:
Keep chest upright and core tight
Step back slowly and control the descent
Push through the front heel to return to standing
Maintain stable grip on the kettlebell

exercises.title: Barbell Deadlift
exercises.description: The Barbell Deadlift is one of the most effective compound exercises for developing full-body strength. It primarily targets the glutes, hamstrings, lower back, and quads, while also engaging the core, traps, and forearms. This foundational lift improves posture, power, and athletic performance by strengthening the entire posterior chain.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Rounding the back
Starting with the bar too far from the shins
Jerking the bar off the floor instead of lifting smoothly
Locking out the knees before extending the hips
Looking up or down excessively, straining the neck
exercises.rest_speech_text: Take a deep breath, brace your core, and get ready to lift strong
steps: 1. Stand with your mid-foot under the barbell, feet hip-width apart.
2. Bend at the hips and knees, gripping the bar just outside your knees.
3. Keep your back straight, chest up, and shoulders slightly in front of the bar.
4. Brace your core, engage your lats, and push through your heels to lift the bar.
5. Extend hips and knees at the same time until you’re standing tall.
6. Pause briefly at the top, then lower the bar with control to the floor by hinging at the hips first.
7. Repeat for the recommended number of reps.
exercises.tips:
Keep the barbell close to your body
Engage your lats and brace your core before pulling
Push through your heels and extend hips and knees simultaneously
Maintain a flat back and neutral neck
Control the descent instead of dropping the bar

exercises.title: Biceps Curls
exercises.description: Biceps Curls is an exercise that involve lifting weights while keeping your upper arms stable to strengthen the biceps. This classic exercise builds arm strength and improves muscle tone.
exercises.common_mistakes:
Swinging the body
Lifting the elbows away from the sides
Arching the back
Lowering weights too quickly
exercises.rest_speech_text: Biceps Curls. Stand tall, keep your elbows close, and curl your hands up toward your shoulders. Slowly lower and repeat.
steps: 1. Stand tall with feet shoulder-width apart, arms down by your sides.
2. Hold weights, palms facing forward, keep your elbows tucked in close to your torso
3. Curl your hands up toward your shoulders by bending the elbows
4. Pause at the top, then slowly lower back down to starting position.
exercises.tips:
Keep your elbows close to your torso
Move slowly and with control                          Breathe out as you lift, breathe in as you lower
